texts.act.5.15: insomuch that they even carried out the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that, as Peter came by, at the least his shadow might overshadow some one of them.
texts.act.5.16: And there also came together the multitudes from the cities round about Jerusalem, bring sick folk, and them that were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed every one.
texts.act.5.17: But the high priest rose up, and all they that were with him (which is the sect of the Sadducees), and they were filled with jealousy,
texts.act.5.18: and laid hands on the apostles, and put them in public ward.
texts.act.5.19: But an angel of the Lord by night opened the prison doors, and brought them out, and said,
texts.act.5.20: Go ye, and stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this Life.
texts.act.5.21: And when they heard [this], they entered into the temple about daybreak, and taught. But the high priest came, and they that were with him, and called the council together, and all the senate of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison-house to have them brought.
texts.act.5.22: But the officers that came found them not in the prison; and they returned, and told,
texts.act.5.23: saying, The prison-house we found shut in all safety, and the keepers standing at the doors: but when we had opened, we found no man within.
texts.act.5.24: Now when the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were much perplexed concerning them whereunto this would grow.
texts.act.5.25: And there came one and told them, Behold, the men whom ye put in the prison are in the temple standing and teaching the people.
texts.act.5.26: Then went the captain with the officers, and brought them, [but] without violence; for they feared the people, lest they should be stoned.
texts.act.5.27: And when they had brought them, they set them before the council. And the high priest asked them,
texts.act.5.28: saying, We strictly charged you not to teach in this name: and behold, ye have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and intend to bring this man's blood upon us.
texts.act.5.29: But Peter and the apostles answered and said, We must obey God rather than men.
texts.act.5.30: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew, hanging him on a tree.
texts.act.5.31: Him did God exalt with his right hand [to be] a Prince and a Saviour, to give repentance to Israel, and remission of sins.
texts.act.5.32: And we are witnesses of these things; and [so is] the Holy Spirit, whom God hath given to them that obey him.
texts.act.5.33: But they, when they heard this, were cut to the heart, and minded to slay them.
texts.act.5.34: But there stood up one in the council, a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, had in honor of all the people, and commanded to put the men forth a little while.
texts.act.5.35: And he said unto them, Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves as touching these men, what ye are about to do.
texts.act.5.36: For before these days rose up Theudas, giving himself out to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were dispersed, and came to nought.
texts.act.5.37: After this man rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the enrolment, and drew away [some of the] people after him: he also perished; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered abroad.
texts.act.5.38: And now I say unto you, Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will be overthrown:
texts.act.5.39: but if it is of God, ye will not be able to overthrow them; lest haply ye be found even to be fighting against God.
texts.act.5.40: And to him they agreed: and when they had called the apostles unto them, they beat them and charged them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
texts.act.5.41: They therefore departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the Name.
texts.act.5.42: And every day, in the temple and at home, they ceased not to teach and to preach Jesus [as] the Christ.
texts.act.6.1: Now in these days, when the number of the disciples was multiplying, there arose a murmuring of the Grecian Jews against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration.
texts.act.6.2: And the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them, and said, It is not fit that we should forsake the word of God, and serve tables.
texts.act.6.3: Look ye out therefore, brethren, from among you seven men of good report, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.
texts.act.6.4: But we will continue stedfastly in prayer, and in the ministry of the word.
texts.act.6.5: And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolaus a proselyte of Antioch;
texts.act.6.6: whom they set before the apostles: and when they had prayed, they laid their hands upon them.
texts.act.6.7: And the word of God increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem exceedingly; and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.
texts.act.6.8: And Stephen, full of grace and power, wrought great wonders and signs among the people.
texts.act.6.9: But there arose certain of them that were of the synagogue called [the synagogue] of the Libertines, and of the Cyrenians, and of the Alexandrians, and of them of Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen.
texts.act.6.10: And they were not able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spake.
texts.act.6.11: Then they suborned men, who said, We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and [against] God.
texts.act.6.12: And they stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes, and came upon him, and seized him, and brought him into the council,
texts.act.6.13: and set up false witnesses, who said, This man ceaseth not to speak words against this holy place, and the law:
texts.act.6.14: for we have heard him say, that this Jesus of Nazareth shall destroy this place, and shall change the customs which Moses delivered unto us.
texts.act.6.15: And all that sat in the council, fastening their eyes on him, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel.
texts.act.7.1: And the high priest said, Are these things so?
texts.act.7.2: And he said, Brethren and fathers, hearken: The God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Haran,
texts.act.7.3: and said unto him, Get thee out of thy land, and from thy kindred, and come into the land which I shall show thee.
texts.act.7.4: Then came he out of the land of the Chaldaeans, and dwelt in Haran: and from thence, when his father was dead, [God] removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell:
texts.act.7.5: and he gave him none inheritance in it, no, not so much as to set his foot on: and he promised that he would give it to him in possession, and to his seed after him, when [as yet] he had no child.
texts.act.7.6: And God spake on this wise, that his seed should sojourn in a strange land, and that they should bring them into bondage, and treat them ill, four hundred years.
texts.act.7.7: And the nation to which they shall be in bondage will I judge, said God: and after that shall they come forth, and serve me in this place.
texts.act.7.8: And he gave him the covenant of circumcision: and so [Abraham] begat Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day; and Isaac [begat] Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
texts.act.7.9: And the patriarchs, moved with jealousy against Joseph, sold him into Egypt: and God was with him,
texts.act.7.10: and delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house.
texts.act.7.11: Now there came a famine over all Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction: and our fathers found no sustenance.
texts.act.7.12: But when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent forth our fathers the first time.
texts.act.7.13: And at the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren; and Joseph's race became manifest unto Pharaoh.
texts.act.7.14: And Joseph sent, and called to him Jacob his father, and all his kindred, threescore and fifteen souls.
texts.act.7.15: And Jacob went down into Egypt; and he died, himself and our fathers;
texts.act.7.16: and they were carried over unto Shechem, and laid in the tomb that Abraham bought for a price in silver of the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
texts.act.7.17: But as the time of the promise drew nigh which God vouchsafed unto Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
texts.act.7.18: till there arose another king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph.
texts.act.7.19: The same dealt craftily with our race, and ill-treated our fathers, that they should cast out their babes to the end they might not live.
texts.act.7.20: At which season Moses was born, and was exceeding fair; and he was nourished three months in his father's house.
texts.act.7.21: and when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.
texts.act.7.22: And Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians; and he was mighty in his words and works.
texts.act.7.23: But when he was well-nigh forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel.
texts.act.7.24: And seeing one [of them] suffer wrong, he defended him, and avenged him that was oppressed, smiting the Egyptian:
texts.act.7.25: and he supposed that his brethren understood that God by his hand was giving them deliverance; but they understood not.
texts.act.7.26: And the day following he appeared unto them as they strove, and would have set them at one again, saying, Sirs, ye are brethren; why do ye wrong one to another?
texts.act.7.27: But he that did his neighbor wrong thrust him away, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us?
texts.act.7.28: Wouldest thou kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian yesterday?
texts.act.7.29: And Moses fled at this saying, and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, where he begat two sons.
texts.act.7.30: And when forty years were fulfilled, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire in a bush.
texts.act.7.31: And when Moses saw it, he wondered at the sight: and as he drew near to behold, there came a voice of the Lord,
texts.act.7.32: I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob. And Moses trembled, and durst not behold.
texts.act.7.33: And the Lord said unto him, Loose the shoes from thy feet: for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
texts.act.7.34: I have surely seen the affliction of my people that is in Egypt, and have heard their groaning, and I am come down to deliver them: and now come, I will send thee into Egypt.
texts.act.7.35: This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? him hath God sent [to be] both a ruler and a deliverer with the hand of the angel that appeared to him in the bush.
texts.act.7.36: This man led them forth, having wrought wonders and signs in Egypt, and in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness forty years.
texts.act.7.37: This is that Moses, who said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall God raise up unto you from among your brethren, like unto me.
texts.act.7.38: This is he that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel that spake to him in the Mount Sinai, and with our fathers: who received living oracles to give unto us:
texts.act.7.39: to whom our fathers would not be obedient, but thrust him from them, and turned back in their hearts unto Egypt,
texts.act.7.40: saying unto Aaron, Make us gods that shall go before us: for as for this Moses, who led us forth out of the land of Egypt, we know not what is become of him.
texts.act.7.41: And they made a calf in those days, and brought a sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their hands.
texts.act.7.42: But God turned, and gave them up to serve the host of heaven; as it is written in the book of the prophets, Did ye offer unto me slain beasts and sacrifices Forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
texts.act.7.43: And ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, And the star of the god Rephan, The figures which ye made to worship them: And I will carry you away beyond Babylon.
texts.act.7.44: Our fathers had the tabernacle of the testimony in the wilderness, even as he appointed who spake unto Moses, that he should make it according to the figure that he had seen.
texts.act.7.45: Which also our fathers, in their turn, brought in with Joshua when they entered on the possession of the nations, that God thrust out before the face of our fathers, unto the days of David;
texts.act.7.46: who found favor in the sight of God, and asked to find a habitation for the God of Jacob.
texts.act.7.47: But Solomon built him a house.
texts.act.7.48: Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in [houses] made with hands; as saith the prophet,
texts.act.7.49: The heaven is my throne, And the earth the footstool of my feet: What manner of house will ye build me? saith the Lord: Or what is the place of my rest?
texts.act.7.50: Did not my hand make all these things?
texts.act.7.51: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Spirit: as your fathers did, so do ye.
texts.act.7.52: Which of the prophets did not your fathers persecute? and they killed them that showed before of the coming of the Righteous One; of whom ye have now become betrayers and murderers;
texts.act.7.53: ye who received the law as it was ordained by angels, and kept it not.
texts.act.7.54: Now when they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth.
texts.act.7.55: But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God,
texts.act.7.56: and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing on the right hand of God.
texts.act.7.57: But they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and rushed upon him with one accord;
texts.act.7.58: and they cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
texts.act.7.59: And they stoned Stephen, calling upon [the Lord], and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
texts.act.7.60: And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.
texts.act.8.1: And Saul was consenting unto his death. And there arose on that day a great persecution against the church which was in Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles.
texts.act.8.2: And devout men buried Stephen, and made great lamentation over him.
texts.act.8.3: But Saul laid waste the church, entering into every house, and dragging men and women committed them to prison.
texts.act.8.4: They therefore that were scattered abroad, went about preaching the word.
texts.act.8.5: And Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and proclaimed unto them the Christ.
texts.act.8.6: And the multitudes gave heed with one accord unto the things that were spoken by Philip, when they heard, and saw the signs which he did.
texts.act.8.7: For [from] many of those that had unclean spirits, they came out, crying with a loud voice: and many that were palsied, and that were lame, were healed.
texts.act.8.8: And there was much joy in that city.
texts.act.8.9: But there was a certain man, Simon by name, who beforetime in the city used sorcery, and amazed the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one:
texts.act.8.10: to whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is that power of God which is called Great.
texts.act.8.11: And they gave heed to him, because that of long time he had amazed them with his sorceries.
texts.act.8.12: But when they believed Philip preaching good tidings concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
texts.act.8.13: And Simon also himself believed: and being baptized, he continued with Philip; and beholding signs and great miracles wrought, he was amazed.
texts.act.8.14: Now when the apostles that were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:
texts.act.8.15: who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit:
texts.act.8.16: for as yet it was fallen upon none of them: only they had been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.8.17: Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.8.18: Now when Simon saw that through the laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Spirit was given, he offered them money,
texts.act.8.19: saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay my hands, he may receive the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.8.20: But Peter said unto him, Thy silver perish with thee, because thou hast thought to obtain the gift of God with money.
texts.act.8.21: Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right before God.
texts.act.8.22: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray the Lord, if perhaps the thought of thy heart shall be forgiven thee.
texts.act.8.23: For I see that thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity.
texts.act.8.24: And Simon answered and said, Pray ye for me to the Lord, that none of the things which ye have spoken come upon me.
texts.act.8.25: They therefore, when they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel to many villages of the Samaritans.
texts.act.8.26: But an angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza: the same is desert.
texts.act.8.27: And he arose and went: and behold, a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure, who had come to Jerusalem to worship;
texts.act.8.28: and he was returning and sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.
texts.act.8.29: And the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot.
texts.act.8.30: And Philip ran to him, and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?
texts.act.8.31: And he said, How can I, except some one shall guide me? And he besought Philip to come up and sit with him.
texts.act.8.32: Now the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; And as a lamb before his shearer is dumb, So he openeth not his mouth:
texts.act.8.33: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away: His generation who shall declare? For his life is taken from the earth.
texts.act.8.34: And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other?
texts.act.8.35: And Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, preached unto him Jesus.
texts.act.8.36: And as they went on the way, they came unto a certain water; and the eunuch saith, Behold, [here is] water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?
texts.act.8.37: [And Philip said, If thou believest with all thy heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.]
texts.act.8.38: And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
texts.act.8.39: And when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip; and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went on his way rejoicing.
texts.act.8.40: But Philip was found at Azotus: and passing through he preached the gospel to all the cities, till he came to Caesarea.
texts.act.9.1: But Saul, yet breathing threatening and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest,
texts.act.9.2: and asked of him letters to Damascus unto the synagogues, that if he found any that were of the Way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
texts.act.9.3: And as he journeyed, it came to pass that he drew nigh unto Damascus: and suddenly there shone round about him a light out of heaven:
texts.act.9.4: and he fell upon the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
texts.act.9.5: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And he [said], I am Jesus whom thou persecutest:
texts.act.9.6: but rise, and enter into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.
texts.act.9.7: And the men that journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing the voice, but beholding no man.
texts.act.9.8: And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw nothing; and they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.
texts.act.9.9: And he was three days without sight, and did neither eat nor drink.
texts.act.9.10: Now there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and the Lord said unto him in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Behold, I [am here], Lord.
texts.act.9.11: And the Lord [said] unto him, Arise, and go to the street which is called Straight, and inquire in the house of Judas for one named Saul, a man of Tarsus: for behold, he prayeth;
texts.act.9.12: and he hath seen a man named Ananias coming in, and laying his hands on him, that he might receive his sight.
texts.act.9.13: But Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard from many of this man, how much evil he did to thy saints at Jerusalem:
texts.act.9.14: and here he hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that call upon thy name.
texts.act.9.15: But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles and kings, and the children of Israel:
texts.act.9.16: for I will show him how many things he must suffer for my name's sake.
texts.act.9.17: And Ananias departed, and entered into the house; and laying his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, [even] Jesus, who appeared unto thee in the way which thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mayest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.9.18: And straightway there fell from his eyes as it were scales, and he received his sight; and he arose and was baptized;
texts.act.9.19: and he took food and was strengthened. And he was certain days with the disciples that were at Damascus.
texts.act.9.20: And straightway in the synagogues he proclaimed Jesus, that he is the Son of God.
texts.act.9.21: And all that heard him were amazed, and said, Is not this he that in Jerusalem made havoc of them that called on this name? and he had come hither for this intent, that he might bring them bound before the chief priests.
texts.act.9.22: But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews that dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.
texts.act.9.23: And when many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel together to kill him:
texts.act.9.24: but their plot became known to Saul. And they watched the gates also day and night that they might kill him:
texts.act.9.25: but his disciples took him by night, and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
texts.act.9.26: And when he was come to Jerusalem, he assayed to join himself to the disciples: and they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
texts.act.9.27: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared unto them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.
texts.act.9.28: And he was with them going in and going out at Jerusalem,
texts.act.9.29: preaching boldly in the name of the Lord: and he spake and disputed against the Grecian Jews; but they were seeking to kill him.
texts.act.9.30: And when the brethren knew it, they brought him down to Caesarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.
texts.act.9.31: So the church throughout all Judaea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being edified; and, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, was multiplied.
texts.act.9.32: And it came to pass, as Peter went throughout all parts, he came down also to the saints that dwelt at Lydda.
texts.act.9.33: And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had kept his bed eight years; for he was palsied.
texts.act.9.34: And Peter said unto him, Aeneas, Jesus Christ healeth thee: arise and make thy bed. And straightway he arose.
texts.act.9.35: And all that dwelt at Lydda and in Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
texts.act.9.36: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.
texts.act.9.37: And it came to pass in those days, that she fell sick, and died: and when they had washed her, they laid her in an upper chamber.
texts.act.9.38: And as Lydda was nigh unto Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men unto him, entreating him, Delay not to come on unto us.
texts.act.9.39: And Peter arose and went with them. And when he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.
texts.act.9.40: But Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down and prayed; and turning to the body, he said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes; and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
texts.act.9.41: And he gave her his hand, and raised her up; and calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.
texts.act.9.42: And it became known throughout all Joppa: and many believed on the Lord.
texts.act.9.43: And it came to pass, that he abode many days in Joppa with one Simon a tanner.
texts.act.10.1: Now [there was] a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of the band called the Italian [band],
texts.act.10.2: a devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, who gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God always.
texts.act.10.3: He saw in a vision openly, as it were about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in unto him, and saying to him, Cornelius.
texts.act.10.4: And he, fastening his eyes upon him, and being affrighted, said, What is it, Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers and thine alms are gone up for a memorial before God.
texts.act.10.5: And now send men to Joppa, and fetch one Simon, who is surnamed Peter:
texts.act.10.6: he lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea side.
texts.act.10.7: And when the angel that spake unto him was departed, he called two of his household-servants, and a devout soldier of them that waited on him continually;
texts.act.10.8: and having rehearsed all things unto them, he sent them to Joppa.
texts.act.10.9: Now on the morrow, as they were on their journey, and drew nigh unto the city, Peter went up upon the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour:
texts.act.10.10: and he became hungry, and desired to eat: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance;
texts.act.10.11: and he beholdeth the heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending, as it were a great sheet, let down by four corners upon the earth:
texts.act.10.12: wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts and creeping things of the earth and birds of the heaven.
texts.act.10.13: And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill and eat.
texts.act.10.14: But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten anything that is common and unclean.
texts.act.10.15: And a voice [came] unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, make not thou common.
texts.act.10.16: And this was done thrice: and straightway the vessel was received up into heaven.
texts.act.10.17: Now while Peter was much perplexed in himself what the vision which he had seen might mean, behold, the men that were sent by Cornelius, having made inquiry for Simon's house, stood before the gate,
texts.act.10.18: and called and asked whether Simon, who was surnamed Peter, were lodging there.
texts.act.10.19: And while Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit said unto him, Behold, three men seek thee.
texts.act.10.20: But arise, and get thee down, and go with them, nothing doubting: for I have sent them.
texts.act.10.21: And Peter went down to the men, and said, Behold, I am he whom ye seek: what is the cause wherefore ye are come?
texts.act.10.22: And they said, Cornelius a centurion, a righteous man and one that feareth God, and well reported of by all the nation of the Jews, was warned [of God] by a holy angel to send for thee into his house, and to hear words from thee.
texts.act.10.23: So he called them in and lodged them. And on the morrow he arose and went forth with them, and certain of the brethren from Joppa accompanied him.
texts.act.10.24: And on the morrow they entered into Caesarea. And Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his kinsmen and his near friends.
texts.act.10.25: And when it came to pass that Peter entered, Cornelius met him, and fell down at his feet, and worshipped him.
texts.act.10.26: But Peter raised him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man.
texts.act.10.27: And as he talked with him, he went in, and findeth many come together:
texts.act.10.28: and he said unto them, Ye yourselves know how it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to join himself or come unto one of another nation; and [yet] unto me hath God showed that I should not call any man common or unclean:
texts.act.10.29: wherefore also I came without gainsaying, when I was sent for. I ask therefore with what intent ye sent for me.
texts.act.10.30: And Cornelius said, Four days ago, until this hour, I was keeping the ninth hour of prayer in my house; and behold, a man stood before me in bright apparel,
texts.act.10.31: and saith, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God.
texts.act.10.32: Send therefore to Joppa, and call unto thee Simon, who is surnamed Peter; he lodgeth in the house of Simon a tanner, by the sea side.
texts.act.10.33: Forthwith therefore I sent to thee; and thou hast well done that thou art come. Now therefore we are all here present in the sight of God, to hear all things that have been commanded thee of the Lord.
texts.act.10.34: And Peter opened his mouth and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:
texts.act.10.35: but in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is acceptable to him.
texts.act.10.36: The word which he sent unto the children of Israel, preaching good tidings of peace by Jesus Christ (He is Lord of all.) --
texts.act.10.37: that saying ye yourselves know, which was published throughout all Judaea, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;
texts.act.10.38: [even] Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.
texts.act.10.39: And we are witnesses of all things which he did both in the country of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; whom also they slew, hanging him on a tree.
texts.act.10.40: Him God raised up the third day, and gave him to be made manifest,
texts.act.10.41: not to all the people, but unto witnesses that were chosen before of God, [even] to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
texts.act.10.42: And he charged us to preach unto the people, and to testify that this is he who is ordained of God [to be] the Judge of the living and the dead.
texts.act.10.43: To him bear all the prophets witness, that through his name every one that believeth on him shall receive remission of sins.
texts.act.10.44: While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all them that heard the word.
texts.act.10.45: And they of the circumcision that believed were amazed, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.10.46: For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter,
texts.act.10.47: Can any man forbid the water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit as well as we?
texts.act.10.48: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then prayed they him to tarry certain days.
texts.act.11.1: Now the apostles and the brethren that were in Judaea heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
texts.act.11.2: And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him,
texts.act.11.3: saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.
texts.act.11.4: But Peter began, and expounded [the matter] unto them in order, saying,
texts.act.11.5: I was in the city of Joppa praying: and in a trance I saw a vision, a certain vessel descending, as it were a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners; and it came even unto me:
texts.act.11.6: upon which when I had fastened mine eyes, I considered, and saw the fourfooted beasts of the earth and wild beasts and creeping things and birds of the heaven.
texts.act.11.7: And I heard also a voice saying unto me, Rise, Peter; kill and eat.
texts.act.11.8: But I said, Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath ever entered into my mouth.
texts.act.11.9: But a voice answered the second time out of heaven, What God hath cleansed, make not thou common.
texts.act.11.10: And this was done thrice: and all were drawn up again into heaven.
texts.act.11.11: And behold, forthwith three men stood before the house in which we were, having been sent from Caesarea unto me.
texts.act.11.12: And the Spirit bade me go with them, making no distinction. And these six brethren also accompanied me; and we entered into the man's house:
texts.act.11.13: and he told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house, and saying, Send to Joppa, and fetch Simon, whose surname is Peter;
texts.act.11.14: who shall speak unto thee words, whereby thou shalt be saved, thou and all thy house.
texts.act.11.15: And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as on us at the beginning.
texts.act.11.16: And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, John indeed baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized in the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.11.17: If then God gave unto them the like gift as [he did] also unto us, when we believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?
texts.act.11.18: And when they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then to the Gentiles also hath God granted repentance unto life.
texts.act.11.19: They therefore that were scattered abroad upon the tribulation that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phoenicia, and Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to none save only to Jews.
texts.act.11.20: But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they were come to Antioch, spake unto the Greeks also, preaching the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.11.21: And the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number that believed turned unto the Lord.
texts.act.11.22: And the report concerning them came to the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem: and they sent forth Barnabas as far as Antioch:
texts.act.11.23: who, when he was come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad; and he exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord:
texts.act.11.24: for he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith: and much people was added unto the Lord.
texts.act.11.25: And he went forth to Tarsus to seek for Saul;
texts.act.11.26: and when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that even for a whole year they were gathered together with the church, and taught much people, and that the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.
texts.act.11.27: Now in these days there came down prophets from Jerusalem unto Antioch.
texts.act.11.28: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be a great famine over all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius.
texts.act.11.29: And the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren that dwelt in Judea:
texts.act.11.30: which also they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
texts.act.12.1: Now about that time Herod the king put forth his hands to afflict certain of the church.
texts.act.12.2: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.
texts.act.12.3: And when he saw that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. And [those] were the days of unleavened bread.
texts.act.12.4: And when he had taken him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to guard him; intending after the Passover to bring him forth to the people.
texts.act.12.5: Peter therefore was kept in the prison: but prayer was made earnestly of the church unto God for him.
texts.act.12.6: And when Herod was about to bring him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and guards before the door kept the prison.
texts.act.12.7: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shined in the cell: and he smote Peter on the side, and awoke him, saying, Rise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.
texts.act.12.8: And the angel said unto him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals. And he did so. And he saith unto him, Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.
texts.act.12.9: And he went out, and followed; and he knew not that it was true which was done by the angel, but thought he saw a vision.
texts.act.12.10: And when they were past the first and the second guard, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth into the city; which opened to them of its own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and straightway the angel departed from him.
texts.act.12.11: And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a truth, that the Lord hath sent forth his angel and delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
texts.act.12.12: And when he had considered [the thing], he came to the house of Mary the mother of John whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together and were praying.
texts.act.12.13: And when he knocked at the door of the gate, a maid came to answer, named Rhoda.
texts.act.12.14: And when she knew Peter's voice, she opened not the gate for joy, but ran in, and told that Peter stood before the gate.
texts.act.12.15: And they said unto her, Thou art mad. But she confidently affirmed that it was even so. And they said, It is his angel.
texts.act.12.16: But Peter continued knocking: and when they had opened, they saw him, and were amazed.
texts.act.12.17: But he, beckoning unto them with the hand to hold their peace, declared unto them how the Lord had brought him forth out of the prison. And he said, Tell these things unto James, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went to another place.
texts.act.12.18: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter.
texts.act.12.19: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not, he examined the guards, and commanded that they should be put to death. And he went down from Judaea to Caesarea, and tarried there.
texts.act.12.20: Now he was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon: and they came with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus the king's chamberlain their friend, they asked for peace, because their country was fed from the king's country.
texts.act.12.21: And upon a set day Herod arrayed himself in royal apparel, and sat on the throne, and made an oration unto them.
texts.act.12.22: And the people shouted, [saying], The voice of a god, and not of a man.
texts.act.12.23: And immediately an angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.
texts.act.12.24: But the word of God grew and multiplied.
texts.act.12.25: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their ministration, taking with them John whose surname was Mark.
texts.act.13.1: Now there were at Antioch, in the church that was [there], prophets and teachers, Barnabas, and Symeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen the foster-brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
texts.act.13.2: And as they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.
texts.act.13.3: Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
texts.act.13.4: So they, being sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia; and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.
texts.act.13.5: And when they were at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews: and they had also John as their attendant.
texts.act.13.6: And when they had gone through the whole island unto Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesus;
texts.act.13.7: who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding. The same called unto him Barnabas and Saul, and sought to hear the word of God.
texts.act.13.8: But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn aside the proconsul from the faith.
texts.act.13.9: But Saul, who is also [called] Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fastened his eyes on him,
texts.act.13.10: and said, O full of all guile and all villany, thou son of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?
texts.act.13.11: And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. And immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness; and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand.
texts.act.13.12: Then the proconsul, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
texts.act.13.13: Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos, and came to Perga in Pamphylia: and John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.
texts.act.13.14: But they, passing through from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia; and they went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and sat down.
texts.act.13.15: And after the reading of the law and the prophets the rulers of the synagogue sent unto them, saying, Brethren, if ye have any word of exhortation for the people, say on.
texts.act.13.16: And Paul stood up, and beckoning with the hand said, Men of Israel, and ye that fear God, hearken:
texts.act.13.17: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they sojourned in the land of Egypt, and with a high arm led he them forth out of it.
texts.act.13.18: And for about the time of forty years as a nursing-father bare he them in the wilderness.
texts.act.13.19: And when he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave [them] their land for an inheritance, for about four hundred and fifty years:
texts.act.13.20: and after these things he gave [them] judges until Samuel the prophet.
texts.act.13.21: And afterward they asked for a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for the space of forty years.
texts.act.13.22: And when he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king; to whom also he bare witness and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after My heart, who shall do all My will.
texts.act.13.23: Of this man's seed hath God according to promise brought unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus;
texts.act.13.24: when John had first preached before his coming the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
texts.act.13.25: And as John was fulfilling his course, he said, What suppose ye that I am? I am not [he]. But behold, there cometh one after me the shoes of whose feet I am not worthy to unloose.
texts.act.13.26: Brethren, children of the stock of Abraham, and those among you that fear God, to us is the word of this salvation sent forth.
texts.act.13.27: For they that dwell in Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they knew him not, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every sabbath, fulfilled [them] by condemning [him].
texts.act.13.28: And though they found no cause of death [in him], yet asked they of Pilate that he should be slain.
texts.act.13.29: And when they had fulfilled all things that were written of him, they took him down from the tree, and laid him in a tomb.
texts.act.13.30: But God raised him from the dead:
texts.act.13.31: and he was seen for many days of them that came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses unto the people.
texts.act.13.32: And we bring you good tidings of the promise made unto the fathers,
texts.act.13.33: that God hath fulfilled the same unto our children, in that he raised up Jesus; as also it is written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.
texts.act.13.34: And as concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he hath spoken on this wise, I will give you the holy and sure [blessings] of David.
texts.act.13.35: Because he saith also in another [psalm], Thou wilt not give Thy Holy One to see corruption.
texts.act.13.36: For David, after he had in his own generation served the counsel of God, fell asleep, and was laid unto his fathers, and saw corruption:
texts.act.13.37: but he whom God raised up saw no corruption.
texts.act.13.38: Be it known unto you therefore, brethren, that through this man is proclaimed unto you remission of sins:
texts.act.13.39: and by him every one that believeth is justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.
texts.act.13.40: Beware therefore, lest that come upon [you] which is spoken in the prophets:
texts.act.13.41: Behold, ye despisers, and wonder, and perish; For I work a work in your days, A work which ye shall in no wise believe, if one declare it unto you.
texts.act.13.42: And as they went out, they besought that these words might be spoken to them the next sabbath.
texts.act.13.43: Now when the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas; who, speaking to them, urged them to continue in the grace of God.
texts.act.13.44: And the next sabbath almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of God.
texts.act.13.45: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with jealousy, and contradicted the things which were spoken by Paul, and blasphemed.
texts.act.13.46: And Paul and Barnabas spake out boldly, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first be spoken to you. Seeing ye thrust it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.
texts.act.13.47: For so hath the Lord commanded us, [saying], I have set thee for a light of the Gentiles, That thou shouldest be for salvation unto the uttermost part of the earth.
texts.act.13.48: And as the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of God: and as many as were ordained to eternal life believed.
texts.act.13.49: And the word of the Lord was spread abroad throughout all the region.
texts.act.13.50: But the Jews urged on the devout women of honorable estate, and the chief men of the city, and stirred up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and cast them out of their borders.
texts.act.13.51: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.
texts.act.13.52: And the disciples were filled with joy with the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.14.1: And it came to pass in Iconium that they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spake that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.
texts.act.14.2: But the Jews that were disobedient stirred up the souls of the Gentiles, and made them evil affected against the brethren.
texts.act.14.3: Long time therefore they tarried [there] speaking boldly in the Lord, who bare witness unto the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
texts.act.14.4: But the multitude of the city was divided; and part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.
texts.act.14.5: And when there was made an onset both of the Gentiles and of the Jews with their rulers, to treat them shamefully and to stone them,
texts.act.14.6: they became aware of it, and fled unto the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the region round about:
texts.act.14.7: and there they preached the gospel.
texts.act.14.8: And at Lystra there sat a certain man, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother's womb, who never had walked.
texts.act.14.9: The same heard Paul speaking, who, fastening eyes upon him, and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,
texts.act.14.10: said with a loud voice, Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped up and walked.
texts.act.14.11: And when the multitude saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.
texts.act.14.12: And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercury, because he was the chief speaker.
texts.act.14.13: And the priest of Jupiter whose [temple] was before the city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the multitudes.
texts.act.14.14: But when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of it, they rent their garments, and sprang forth among the multitude, crying out
texts.act.14.15: and saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and bring you good tidings, that ye should turn from these vain things unto a living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea, and all that in them is:
texts.act.14.16: who in the generations gone by suffered all the nations to walk in their own ways.
texts.act.14.17: And yet He left not himself without witness, in that he did good and gave you from heaven rains and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.
texts.act.14.18: And with these sayings scarce restrained they the multitudes from doing sacrifice unto them.
texts.act.14.19: But there came Jews thither from Antioch and Iconium: and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul, and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.
texts.act.14.20: But as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and entered into the city: and on the morrow he went forth with Barnabas to Derbe.
texts.act.14.21: And when they had preached the gospel to that city, and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, and to Iconium, and to Antioch,
texts.act.14.22: confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.act.14.23: And when they had appointed for them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they had believed.
texts.act.14.24: And they passed through Pisidia, and came to Pamphylia.
texts.act.14.25: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia;
texts.act.14.26: and thence they sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.
texts.act.14.27: And when they were come, and had gathered the church together, they rehearsed all things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith unto the Gentiles.
texts.act.14.28: And they tarried no little time with the disciples.
texts.act.15.1: And certain men came down from Judaea and taught the brethren, [saying], Except ye be circumcised after the custom of Moses, ye cannot be saved.
texts.act.15.2: And when Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and questioning with them, [the brethren] appointed that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.
texts.act.15.3: They therefore, being brought on their way by the church, passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.
texts.act.15.4: And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received of the church and the apostles and the elders, and they rehearsed all things that God had done with them.
texts.act.15.5: But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees who believed, saying, It is needful to circumcise them, and to charge them to keep the law of Moses.
texts.act.15.6: And the apostles and the elders were gathered together to consider of this matter.
texts.act.15.7: And when there had been much questioning, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Brethren, ye know that a good while ago God made choice among you, that by my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.
texts.act.15.8: And God, who knoweth the heart, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Spirit, even as he did unto us;
texts.act.15.9: and he made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.
texts.act.15.10: Now therefore why make ye trial of God, that ye should put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
texts.act.15.11: But we believe that we shall be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, in like manner as they.
texts.act.15.12: And all the multitude kept silence; and they hearkened unto Barnabas and Paul rehearsing what signs and wonders God had wrought among the Gentiles through them.
texts.act.15.13: And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying, Brethren, hearken unto me:
texts.act.15.14: Symeon hath rehearsed how first God visited the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.
texts.act.15.15: And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written,
texts.act.15.16: After these things I will return, And I will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen; And I will build again the ruins thereof, And I will set it up:
texts.act.15.17: That the residue of men may seek after the Lord, And all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called,
texts.act.15.18: Saith the Lord, who maketh these things known from of old.
texts.act.15.19: Wherefore my judgment is, that we trouble not them that from among the Gentiles turn to God;
texts.act.15.20: but that we write unto them, that they abstain from the pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from what is strangled, and from blood.
texts.act.15.21: For Moses from generations of old hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath.
texts.act.15.22: Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole church, to choose men out of their company, and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; [namely], Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:
texts.act.15.23: and they wrote [thus] by them, The apostles and the elders, brethren, unto the brethren who are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia, greeting:
texts.act.15.24: Forasmuch as we have heard that certain who went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls; to whom we gave no commandment;
texts.act.15.25: it seemed good unto us, having come to one accord, to choose out men and send them unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
texts.act.15.26: men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.act.15.27: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who themselves also shall tell you the same things by word of mouth.
texts.act.15.28: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things:
texts.act.15.29: that ye abstain from things sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication; from which if ye keep yourselves, it shall be well with you. Fare ye well.
texts.act.15.30: So they, when they were dismissed, came down to Antioch; and having gathered the multitude together, they delivered the epistle.
texts.act.15.31: And when they had read it, they rejoiced for the consolation.
texts.act.15.32: And Judas and Silas, being themselves also prophets, exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed them.
texts.act.15.33: And after they had spent some time [there], they were dismissed in peace from the brethren unto those that had sent them forth.
texts.act.15.34: [But it seemed good unto Silas to abide there.]
texts.act.15.35: But Paul and Barnabas tarried in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.
texts.act.15.36: And after some days Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us return now and visit the brethren in every city wherein we proclaimed the word of the Lord, [and see] how they fare.
texts.act.15.37: And Barnabas was minded to take with them John also, who was called Mark.
texts.act.15.38: But Paul thought not good to take with them him who withdrew from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.
texts.act.15.39: And there arose a sharp contention, so that they parted asunder one from the other, and Barnabas took Mark with him, and sailed away unto Cyprus;
texts.act.15.40: but Paul choose Silas, and went forth, being commended by the brethren to the grace of the Lord.
texts.act.15.41: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.
texts.act.16.1: And he came also to Derbe and to Lystra: and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess that believed; but his father was a Greek.
texts.act.16.2: The same was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.
texts.act.16.3: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and he took and circumcised him because of the Jews that were in those parts: for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
texts.act.16.4: And as they went on their way through the cities, they delivered them the decrees to keep which had been ordained of the apostles and elders that were at Jerusalem.
texts.act.16.5: So the churches were strengthened in the faith, and increased in number daily.
texts.act.16.6: And they went through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, having been forbidden of the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia;
texts.act.16.7: and when they were come over against Mysia, they assayed to go into Bithynia; and the Spirit of Jesus suffered them not;
texts.act.16.8: and passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.
texts.act.16.9: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night: There was a man of Macedonia standing, beseeching him, and saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.
texts.act.16.10: And when he had seen the vision, straightway we sought to go forth into Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.
texts.act.16.11: Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;
texts.act.16.12: and from thence to Philippi, which is a city of Macedonia, the first of the district, a [Roman] colony: and we were in this city tarrying certain days.
texts.act.16.13: And on the sabbath day we went forth without the gate by a river side, where we supposed there was a place of prayer; and we sat down, and spake unto the women that were come together.
texts.act.16.14: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple of the city of Thyatira, one that worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened to give heed unto the things which were spoken by Paul.
texts.act.16.15: And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide [there]. And she constrained us.
texts.act.16.16: And it came to pass, as we were going to the place of prayer, that a certain maid having a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much gain by soothsaying.
texts.act.16.17: The same following after Paul and us cried out, saying, These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim unto you the way of salvation.
texts.act.16.18: And this she did for many days. But Paul, being sore troubled, turned and said to the spirit, I charge thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And it came out that very hour.
texts.act.16.19: But when her masters saw that the hope of their gain was gone, they laid hold on Paul and Silas, and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers,
texts.act.16.20: and when they had brought them unto the magistrates, they said, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city,
texts.act.16.21: and set forth customs which it is not lawful for us to receive, or to observe, being Romans.
texts.act.16.22: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent their garments off them, and commanded to beat them with rods.
texts.act.16.23: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:
texts.act.16.24: who, having received such a charge, cast them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
texts.act.16.25: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns unto God, and the prisoners were listening to them;
texts.act.16.26: and suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison-house were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.
texts.act.16.27: And the jailor, being roused out of sleep and seeing the prison doors open, drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.
texts.act.16.28: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.
texts.act.16.29: And he called for lights and sprang in, and, trembling for fear, fell down before Paul and Silas,
texts.act.16.30: and brought them out and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
texts.act.16.31: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus, and thou shalt be saved, thou and thy house.
texts.act.16.32: And they spake the word of the Lord unto him, with all that were in his house.
texts.act.16.33: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, immediately.
texts.act.16.34: And he brought them up into his house, and set food before them, and rejoiced greatly, with all his house, having believed in God.
texts.act.16.35: But when it was day, the magistrates sent the sergeants, saying, Let those men go.
texts.act.16.36: And the jailor reported the words to Paul, [saying], The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore come forth, and go in peace.
texts.act.16.37: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us publicly, uncondemned, men that are Romans, and have cast us into prison; and do they now cast us out privily? Nay verily; but let them come themselves and bring us out.
texts.act.16.38: And the sergeants reported these words unto the magistrates: and they feared when they heard that they were Romans;
texts.act.16.39: and they came and besought them; and when they had brought them out, they asked them to go away from the city.
texts.act.16.40: And they went out of the prison, and entered into [the house] of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
texts.act.17.1: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:
texts.act.17.2: and Paul, as his custom was, went in unto them, and for three sabbath days reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
texts.act.17.3: opening and alleging that it behooved the Christ to suffer, and to rise again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom, [said he,] I proclaim unto you, is the Christ.
texts.act.17.4: And some of them were persuaded, and consorted with Paul and Silas, and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.
texts.act.17.5: But the Jews, being moved with jealousy, took unto them certain vile fellows of the rabble, and gathering a crowd, set the city on an uproar; and assaulting the house of Jason, they sought to bring them forth to the people.
texts.act.17.6: And when they found them not, they dragged Jason and certain brethren before the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;
texts.act.17.7: whom Jason hath received: and these all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, [one] Jesus.
texts.act.17.8: And they troubled the multitude and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.
texts.act.17.9: And when they had taken security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.
texts.act.17.10: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Beroea: who when they were come thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.
texts.act.17.11: Now these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of the mind, examining the Scriptures daily, whether these things were so.
texts.act.17.12: Many of them therefore believed; also of the Greek women of honorable estate, and of men, not a few.
texts.act.17.13: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was proclaimed of Paul at Beroea also, they came thither likewise, stirring up and troubling the multitudes.
texts.act.17.14: And then immediately the brethren sent forth Paul to go as far as to the sea: and Silas and Timothy abode there still.
texts.act.17.15: But they that conducted Paul brought him as far as Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timothy that they should come to him with all speed, they departed.
texts.act.17.16: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he beheld the city full of idols.
texts.act.17.17: So he reasoned in the synagogue with Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with them that met him.
texts.act.17.18: And certain also of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers encountered him. And some said, What would this babbler say? others, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached Jesus and the resurrection.
texts.act.17.19: And they took hold of him, and brought him unto the Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new teaching is, which is spoken by thee?
texts.act.17.20: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.
texts.act.17.21: (Now all the Athenians and the strangers sojourning there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell or to hear some new thing.)
texts.act.17.22: And Paul stood in the midst of the Areopagus, and said, Ye men of Athens, in all things, I perceive that ye are very religious.
texts.act.17.23: For as I passed along, and observed the objects of your worship, I found also an altar with this inscription, TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. What therefore ye worship in ignorance, this I set forth unto you.
texts.act.17.24: The God that made the world and all things therein, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
texts.act.17.25: neither is he served by men's hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;
texts.act.17.26: and he made of one every nation of men to dwell on all the face of the earth, having determined [their] appointed seasons, and the bounds of their habitation;
texts.act.17.27: that they should seek God, if haply they might feel after him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us:
texts.act.17.28: for in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain even of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
texts.act.17.29: Being then the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and device of man.
texts.act.17.30: The times of ignorance therefore God overlooked; but now he commandeth men that they should all everywhere repent:
texts.act.17.31: inasmuch as he hath appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.
texts.act.17.32: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked; but others said, We will hear thee concerning this yet again.
texts.act.17.33: Thus Paul went out from among them.
texts.act.17.34: But certain men clave unto him, and believed: among whom also was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
texts.act.18.1: After these things he departed from Athens, and came to Corinth.
texts.act.18.2: And he found a certain Jew named Aquila, a man of Pontus by race, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome: and he came unto them;
texts.act.18.3: and because he was of the same trade, he abode with them, and they wrought, for by their trade they were tentmakers.
texts.act.18.4: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded Jews and Greeks.
texts.act.18.5: But when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was constrained by the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.
texts.act.18.6: And when they opposed themselves and blasphemed, he shook out his raiment and said unto them, Your blood [be] upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.
texts.act.18.7: And he departed thence, and went into the house of a certain man named Titus Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.
texts.act.18.8: And Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.
texts.act.18.9: And the Lord said unto Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak and hold not thy peace:
texts.act.18.10: for I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to harm thee: for I have much people in this city.
texts.act.18.11: And he dwelt [there] a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
texts.act.18.12: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him before the judgment-seat,
texts.act.18.13: saying, This man persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.
texts.act.18.14: But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked villany, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:
texts.act.18.15: but if they are questions about words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves; I am not minded to be a judge of these matters.
texts.act.18.16: And he drove them from the judgment-seat.
texts.act.18.17: And they all laid hold on Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment-seat. And Gallio cared for none of these things.
texts.act.18.18: And Paul, having tarried after this yet many days, took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence for Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila: having shorn his head in Cenchreae; for he had a vow.
texts.act.18.19: And they came to Ephesus, and he left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
texts.act.18.20: And when they asked him to abide a longer time, he consented not;
texts.act.18.21: but taking his leave of them, and saying, I will return again unto you if God will, he set sail from Ephesus.
texts.act.18.22: And when he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and saluted the church, and went down to Antioch.
texts.act.18.23: And having spent some time [there], he departed, and went through the region of Galatia, and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.
texts.act.18.24: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus; and he was mighty in the scriptures.
texts.act.18.25: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spake and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, knowing only the baptism of John:
texts.act.18.26: and he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more accurately.
texts.act.18.27: And when he was minded to pass over into Achaia, the brethren encouraged him, and wrote to the disciples to receive him: and when he was come, he helped them much that had believed through grace;
texts.act.18.28: for he powerfully confuted the Jews, [and that] publicly, showing by the scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.
texts.act.19.1: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper country came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples:
texts.act.19.2: and he said unto them, Did ye receive the Holy Spirit when ye believed? And they [said] unto him, Nay, we did not so much as hear whether the Holy Spirit was [given].
texts.act.19.3: And he said, Into what then were ye baptized? And they said, Into John's baptism.
texts.act.19.4: And Paul said, John baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people that they should believe on him that should come after him, that is, on Jesus.
texts.act.19.5: And when they heard this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.19.6: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
texts.act.19.7: And they were in all about twelve men.
texts.act.19.8: And he entered into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, reasoning and persuading [as to] the things concerning the kingdom of God.
texts.act.19.9: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.
texts.act.19.10: And this continued for the space of two years; so that all they that dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.
texts.act.19.11: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
texts.act.19.12: insomuch that unto the sick were carried away from his body handkerchiefs or aprons, and the evil spirits went out.
texts.act.19.13: But certain also of the strolling Jews, exorcists, took upon them to name over them that had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, I adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
texts.act.19.14: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, a chief priest, who did this.
texts.act.19.15: And the evil spirit answered and said unto them, Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are ye?
texts.act.19.16: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and mastered both of them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
texts.act.19.17: And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, that dwelt at Ephesus; and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
texts.act.19.18: Many also of them that had believed came, confessing, and declaring their deeds.
texts.act.19.19: And not a few of them that practised magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all; and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
texts.act.19.20: So mightily grew the word of the Lord and prevailed.
texts.act.19.21: Now after these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
texts.act.19.22: And having sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.
texts.act.19.23: And about that time there arose no small stir concerning the Way.
texts.act.19.24: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Diana, brought no little business unto the craftsmen;
texts.act.19.25: whom he gathered together, with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this business we have our wealth.
texts.act.19.26: And ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they are no gods, that are made with hands:
texts.act.19.27: and not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana be made of no account, and that she should even be deposed from her magnificence whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
texts.act.19.28: And when they heard this they were filled with wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesus.
texts.act.19.29: And the city was filled with the confusion: and they rushed with one accord into the theatre, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel.
texts.act.19.30: And when Paul was minded to enter in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
texts.act.19.31: And certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent unto him and besought him not to adventure himself into the theatre.
texts.act.19.32: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was in confusion; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.
texts.act.19.33: And they brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made a defense unto the people.
texts.act.19.34: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
texts.act.19.35: And when the townclerk had quieted the multitude, he saith, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there who knoweth not that the city of the Ephesians is temple-keeper of the great Diana, and of the [image] which fell down from Jupiter?
texts.act.19.36: Seeing then that these things cannot be gainsaid, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rash.
texts.act.19.37: For ye have brought [hither] these men, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of our goddess.
texts.act.19.38: If therefore Demetrius, and the craftsmen that are with him, have a matter against any man, the courts are open, and there are proconsuls: let them accuse one another.
texts.act.19.39: But if ye seek anything about other matters, it shall be settled in the regular assembly.
texts.act.19.40: For indeed we are in danger to be accused concerning this day's riot, there being no cause [for it]: and as touching it we shall not be able to give account of this concourse.
texts.act.19.41: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
texts.act.20.1: And after the uproar ceased, Paul having sent for the disciples and exhorted them, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.
texts.act.20.2: And when he had gone through those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece.
texts.act.20.3: And when he had spent three months [there,] and a plot was laid against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.
