texts.act.8.18: And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Spirit was given, he offered them money,
texts.act.8.19: Saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.8.20: But Peter said to him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.
texts.act.8.21: Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right in the sight of God.
texts.act.8.22: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thy heart may be forgiven thee.
texts.act.8.23: For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity.
texts.act.8.24: Then answered Simon, and said, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me.
texts.act.8.25: And they, when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.
texts.act.8.26: And the angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, Arise, and go towards the south, to the way that goeth down from Jerusalem to Gaza, which is desert.
texts.act.8.27: And he arose, and went: and behold, a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem to worship,
texts.act.8.28: Was returning; and sitting in his chariot, read Isaiah the prophet.
texts.act.8.29: Then the Spirit said to Philip, Go near and join thyself to this chariot.
texts.act.8.30: And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him reading the prophet Isaiah, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?
texts.act.8.31: And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up, and sit with him.
texts.act.8.32: The place of the scripture which he read was this, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so he opened not his mouth:
texts.act.8.33: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away: and who shall declare his generation? for his life is taken from the earth.
texts.act.8.34: And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other man?
texts.act.8.35: Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached to him Jesus.
texts.act.8.36: And as they went on their way, they came to a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?
texts.act.8.37: And Philip said, If thou believest with all thy heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
texts.act.8.38: And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him.
texts.act.8.39: And when they had come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.
texts.act.8.40: But Philip was found at Azotus: and passing through, he preached in all the cities, till he came to Cesarea.
texts.act.9.1: And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest,
texts.act.9.2: And desired from him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he should find any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
texts.act.9.3: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined around him a light from heaven:
texts.act.9.4: And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying to him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
texts.act.9.5: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest. It is hard for thee to kick against the goads.
texts.act.9.6: And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said to him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.
texts.act.9.7: And the men who journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man.
texts.act.9.8: And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.
texts.act.9.9: And he was three days without sight, and neither ate nor drank.
texts.act.9.10: And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Behold, I am here, Lord.
texts.act.9.11: And the Lord said to him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and inquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul of Tarsus: for behold, he prayeth,
texts.act.9.12: And hath seen in a vision a man named Ananias, coming in, and putting his hand on him, that he might receive his sight.
texts.act.9.13: Then Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints at Jerusalem:
texts.act.9.14: And here he hath authority from the chief priests, to bind all that call on thy name.
texts.act.9.15: But the Lord said to him, Go, for he is a chosen vessel to me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel.
texts.act.9.16: For I will show him how great things he must suffer for my name's sake.
texts.act.9.17: And Ananias went, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him, said, Brother Saul, the Lord (even Jesus that appeared to thee in the way as thou camest) hath sent me, that thou mayest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.9.18: And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.
texts.act.9.19: And when he had received food, he was strengthened. Then was Saul certain days with the disciples who were at Damascus.
texts.act.9.20: And immediately he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.
texts.act.9.21: But all that heard him were amazed, and said, Is not this he that destroyed them who called on this name in Jerusalem, and came hither for that intent, that he might bring them bound to the chief priests?
texts.act.9.22: But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews who dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ.
texts.act.9.23: And after many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel to kill him.
texts.act.9.24: But their laying in wait, was known to Saul. And they watched the gates day and night to kill him.
texts.act.9.25: Then the disciples took him by night, and let him down by the wall in a basket.
texts.act.9.26: And when Saul had come to Jerusalem, he essayed to join himself to the disciples: but they were all afraid of him, and believed not that he was a disciple.
texts.act.9.27: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared to them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how he had preached boldly at Damascus in the name of Jesus.
texts.act.9.28: And he was with them coming in and going out at Jerusalem.
texts.act.9.29: And he spoke boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus, and disputed against the Grecians: but they went about to slay him.
texts.act.9.30: Which when the brethren knew, they brought him down to Cesarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.
texts.act.9.31: Then had the churches rest throughout all Judea, and Galilee, and Samaria, and were edified: and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, were multiplied.
texts.act.9.32: And it came to pass, as Peter passed throughout all quarters, he came down also to the saints who dwelt at Lydda.
texts.act.9.33: And there he found a certain man named Eneas, who had kept his bed eight years, and was sick with the palsy.
texts.act.9.34: And Peter said to him, Eneas, Jesus Christ healeth thee: arise, and make thy bed. And he arose immediately.
texts.act.9.35: And all that dwelt at Lydda and Saron saw him, and turned to the Lord.
texts.act.9.36: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, who by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and alms-deeds which she did.
texts.act.9.37: And it came to pass in those days, that she was sick, and died: whom, when they had washed, they laid in an upper chamber.
texts.act.9.38: And as Lydda was nigh to Joppa, and the disciples had heard that Peter was there, they sent to him two men, desiring him that he would not delay to come to them.
texts.act.9.39: Then Peter arose, and went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.
texts.act.9.40: But Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down, and prayed; and turning to the body, said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
texts.act.9.41: And he gave her his hand, and lifted her up; and when he had called the saints and widows, presented her alive.
texts.act.9.42: And it was known throughout all Joppa: and many believed in the Lord.
texts.act.9.43: And it came to pass, that he tarried many days in Joppa with one Simon a tanner.
texts.act.10.1: There was a certain man in Cesarea, called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band,
texts.act.10.2: A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, who gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God always.
texts.act.10.3: He saw in a vision evidently, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in to him, and saying to him, Cornelius.
texts.act.10.4: And when he looked on him, he was afraid, and said, What is it, Lord? And he said to him, Thy prayers and thy alms are come up for a memorial before God.
texts.act.10.5: And now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter:
texts.act.10.6: He lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea-side: he will tell thee what thou oughtest to do.
texts.act.10.7: And when the angel who spoke to Cornelius had departed, he called two of his household servants, and a devout soldier of them that waited on him continually;
texts.act.10.8: And when he had declared all these things to them, he sent them to Joppa.
texts.act.10.9: On the morrow, as they were going on their journey, and drew nigh to the city, Peter went up upon the house-top to pray, about the sixth hour:
texts.act.10.10: And he became very hungry, and would have eaten: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance,
texts.act.10.11: And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending to him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:
texts.act.10.12: In which were all manner of four-footed beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping animals, and fowls of the air.
texts.act.10.13: And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.
texts.act.10.14: But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.
texts.act.10.15: And the voice spoke to him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.
texts.act.10.16: This was done thrice: and the vessel was received again into heaven.
texts.act.10.17: Now while Peter doubted in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean, behold, the men who were sent from Cornelius had made inquiry for Simon's house, and were standing before the gate,
texts.act.10.18: And called, and asked whether Simon, who was surnamed Peter, lodged there.
texts.act.10.19: While Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit said to him, Behold, three men seek thee.
texts.act.10.20: Arise therefore, and go down, and go with them, doubting nothing: for I have sent them.
texts.act.10.21: Then Peter went down to the men who were sent to him from Cornelius; and said, Behold, I am he whom ye seek: what is the cause for which ye have come?
texts.act.10.22: And they said, Cornelius the centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews, was warned from God by a holy angel to send for thee into his house, and to hear words from thee.
texts.act.10.23: Then he called them in, and lodged them. And on the morrow Peter went with them, and certain brethren from Joppa accompanied him.
texts.act.10.24: And on the morrow they entered into Cesarea. And Cornelius waited for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends.
texts.act.10.25: And as Peter was coming in, Cornelius met him, and fell down at his feet, and worshiped him.
texts.act.10.26: But Peter took him up, saying, Stand up: I myself also am a man.
texts.act.10.27: And as he talked with him, he went in, and found many that had come together.
texts.act.10.28: And he said to them, Ye know that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come to one of another nation; but God hath shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean.
texts.act.10.29: Therefore I came to you without gainsaying, as soon as I was sent for: I ask therefore for what intent ye have sent for me?
texts.act.10.30: And Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing,
texts.act.10.31: And said, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thy alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God.
texts.act.10.32: Send therefore to Joppa, and call hither Simon, whose surname is Peter; he lodgeth in the house of one Simon a tanner, by the sea-side: who, when he cometh, will speak to thee.
texts.act.10.33: Immediately therefore I sent to thee; and thou hast well done that thou hast come. Now therefore we are all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee from God.
texts.act.10.34: Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, In truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:
texts.act.10.35: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.
texts.act.10.36: The word which God sent to the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)
texts.act.10.37: That word, I say, ye know, which was published throughout all Judea, and began from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;
texts.act.10.38: That God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed by the devil; for God was with him.
texts.act.10.39: And we are witnesses of all things which he did, both in the land of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; whom they slew and hanged on a tree.
texts.act.10.40: Him God raised the third day, and showed him openly;
texts.act.10.41: Not to all the people, but to witnesses chosen before by God, even to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
texts.act.10.42: And he commanded us to preach to the people, and to testify that it is he who was ordained by God to be the Judge of the living and the dead.
texts.act.10.43: To him give all the prophets testimony, that through his name whoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.
texts.act.10.44: While Peter was yet speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all them who heard the word.
texts.act.10.45: And they of the circumcision who believed, were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.10.46: For they heard them speak in languages and magnify God. Then answered Peter,
texts.act.10.47: Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit as well as we?
texts.act.10.48: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then they requested him to tarry certain days.
texts.act.11.1: And the apostles and brethren that were in Judea, heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
texts.act.11.2: And when Peter had come to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him,
texts.act.11.3: Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.
texts.act.11.4: But Peter rehearsed the matter from the beginning, and expounded it by order to them, saying,
texts.act.11.5: I was in the city of Joppa praying: and in a trance I saw a vision, A certain vessel descend, as it had been a great sheet, let down from heaven by four corners; and it came even to me:
texts.act.11.6: Upon which when I had fastened my eyes, I considered, and saw four-footed beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping animals, and fowls of the air.
texts.act.11.7: And I heard a voice saying to me, Arise, Peter; slay and eat.
texts.act.11.8: But I said, Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath at any time entered into my mouth.
texts.act.11.9: But the voice answered me again from heaven, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.
texts.act.11.10: And this was done three times: and all were drawn up again into heaven.
texts.act.11.11: And behold, immediately there were three men already come to the house where I was, sent from Cesarea to me.
texts.act.11.12: And the Spirit bade me go with them, nothing doubting. Moreover, these six brethren accompanied me, and we entered into the man's house:
texts.act.11.13: And he showed us how he had seen an angel in his house, who stood and said to him, Send men to Joppa, and call for Simon, whose surname is Peter;
texts.act.11.14: Who shall tell thee words, by which thou and all thy house shall be saved.
texts.act.11.15: And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, as on us at the beginning.
texts.act.11.16: Then I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, John indeed baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.11.17: Forasmuch then as God gave them the like gift as he did to us, who believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, what was I that I could withstand God?
texts.act.11.18: When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance to life.
texts.act.11.19: Now they who were dispersed upon the persecution that arose about Stephen traveled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but to the Jews only.
texts.act.11.20: And some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Grecians, preaching the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.11.21: And the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number believed, and turned to the Lord.
texts.act.11.22: Then tidings of these things came to the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem: and they sent forth Barnabas, that he should go as far as Antioch.
texts.act.11.23: Who, when he came, and had seen the grace of God, was glad, and exhorted them all that with purpose of heart they would cleave to the Lord.
texts.act.11.24: For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit, and of faith: and many people were added to the Lord.
texts.act.11.25: Then Barnabas departed to Tarsus, to seek Saul:
texts.act.11.26: And when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it came to pass, that a whole year they assembled themselves with the church, and taught many people. And the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
texts.act.11.27: And in these days came prophets from Jerusalem to Antioch.
texts.act.11.28: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cesar.
texts.act.11.29: Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief to the brethren who dwelt in Judea.
texts.act.11.30: Which also they did, and sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.
texts.act.12.1: Now about that time, Herod the king stretched forth his hands to afflict certain of the church.
texts.act.12.2: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.
texts.act.12.3: And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. Then were the days of unleavened bread.
texts.act.12.4: And when he had apprehended him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to keep him; intending after the passover to bring him forth to the people.
texts.act.12.5: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing by the church to God for him.
texts.act.12.6: And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains; and the keepers before the door kept the prison.
texts.act.12.7: And behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison; and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.
texts.act.12.8: And the angel said to him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals; and so he did. And he saith to him, Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.
texts.act.12.9: And he went out, and followed him, and knew not that it was true which was done by the angel; but thought he saw a vision.
texts.act.12.10: When they were past the first and the second ward, they came to the iron gate that leadeth to the city; which opened to them of its own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him.
texts.act.12.11: And when Peter had come to himself, he said, Now I know with certainty, that the Lord hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
texts.act.12.12: And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John whose surname was Mark; where many were assembled, praying.
texts.act.12.13: And as Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a damsel came to hearken, named Rhoda.
texts.act.12.14: And when she knew Peter's voice, she opened not the gate for gladness, but ran in, and told that Peter stood before the gate
texts.act.12.15: And they said to her, Thou art insane. But she constantly affirmed that it was even so. Then they said, It is his angel.
texts.act.12.16: But Peter continued knocking. And when they had opened the door, and saw him, they were astonished.
texts.act.12.17: But he beckoning to them with the hand to hold their peace, declared to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, Go, show these things to James, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went into another place.
texts.act.12.18: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter.
texts.act.12.19: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not, he examined the keepers, and commanded that they should be put to death. And he went down from Judea to Cesarea, and there abode.
texts.act.12.20: And Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon. But they came with one accord to him, and having made Blastus the king's chamberlain their friend, desired peace, because their country was nourished by the king's country.
texts.act.12.21: And upon a set day, Herod arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration to them.
texts.act.12.22: And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.
texts.act.12.23: And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten by worms, and died.
texts.act.12.24: But the word of God grew and multiplied.
texts.act.12.25: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their ministry, and took with them John, whose surname was Mark.
texts.act.13.1: Now there were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
texts.act.13.2: As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, Separate for me Barnabas and Saul, for the work to which I have called them.
texts.act.13.3: And when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
texts.act.13.4: So they being sent forth by the Holy Spirit, departed to Seleucia; and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.
texts.act.13.5: And when they were at Salamis, they preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. And they had also John for their minister.
texts.act.13.6: And when they had gone through the isle to Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Barjesus:
texts.act.13.7: Who was with the deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to hear the word of God.
texts.act.13.8: But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith.
texts.act.13.9: Then Saul (who also is called Paul) filled with the Holy Spirit, set his eyes on him,
texts.act.13.10: And said, O full of all subtilty, and all mischief, thou child of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?
texts.act.13.11: And now behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. And immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness; and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand.
texts.act.13.12: Then the deputy, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the doctrine of the Lord.
texts.act.13.13: Now when Paul and his company loosed from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia. And John departing from them, returned to Jerusalem.
texts.act.13.14: But when they departed from Perga, they came to Antioch in Pisidia, and went into the synagogue on the sabbath, and sat down.
texts.act.13.15: And after the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, Men, brethren, if ye have any word of exhortation for the people, speak.
texts.act.13.16: Then Paul stood up, and beckoning with his hand, said, Men of Israel, and ye that fear God, give audience.
texts.act.13.17: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they dwelt as strangers in the land of Egypt, and with a high arm he brought them out of it.
texts.act.13.18: And about the time of forty years he suffered their manners in the wilderness.
texts.act.13.19: And when he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he divided their land to them by lot.
texts.act.13.20: And after that he gave to them judges, about the space of four hundred and fifty years, until Samuel the prophet.
texts.act.13.21: And afterward they desired a king: and God gave to them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, by the space of forty years.
texts.act.13.22: And when he had removed him, he raised up to them David to be their king: to whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, who shall fulfill all my will.
texts.act.13.23: Of this man's offspring hath God, according to his promise, raised up to Israel a Savior, Jesus:
texts.act.13.24: John having first preached, before his coming, the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
texts.act.13.25: And as John fulfilled his course, he said, Whom think ye that I am? I am not he. But behold, there cometh one after me, whose shoes of his feet I am not worthy to loose.
texts.act.13.26: Men, brethren, children of the stock of Abraham, and whoever among you feareth God, to you is the word of this salvation sent.
texts.act.13.27: For they that dwell at Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they knew him not, nor yet the words of the prophets which are read every sabbath, they have fulfilled them in condemning him.
texts.act.13.28: And though they found no cause of death in him, yet they desired Pilate that he should be put to death.
texts.act.13.29: And when they had fulfilled all that was written concerning him, they took him down from the tree, and laid him in a sepulcher.
texts.act.13.30: But God raised him from the dead:
texts.act.13.31: And he was seen many days by them who came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are his witnesses to the people.
texts.act.13.32: And we declare to you the glad tidings, that the promise which was made to the fathers,
texts.act.13.33: God hath fulfilled the same to us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.
texts.act.13.34: And as concerning that he raised him from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he said on this wise, I will give you the sure mercies of David.
texts.act.13.35: Wherefore he saith also in another psalm, Thou wilt not suffer thy Holy One to see corruption.
texts.act.13.36: For David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell asleep, and was laid to his fathers, and saw corruption:
texts.act.13.37: But he whom God raised again, saw no corruption.
texts.act.13.38: Be it known to you therefore, men, brethren, that through this man is preached to you the forgiveness of sins;
texts.act.13.39: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.
texts.act.13.40: Beware therefore, lest that come upon you which is spoken in the prophets;
texts.act.13.41: Behold, ye despisers, and wonder, and perish: for I work a work in your days, a work which ye will in no wise believe, though a man declare it to you.
texts.act.13.42: And when the Jews had gone out of the synagogue, the Gentiles besought that these words might be preached to them the next sabbath.
texts.act.13.43: Now when the congregation was broken up, many of the Jews and religious proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas; who speaking to them, persuaded them to continue in the grace of God.
texts.act.13.44: And the next sabbath came almost the whole city together to hear the word of God.
texts.act.13.45: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and spoke against those things which were uttered by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.
texts.act.13.46: Then Paul and Barnabas became bold, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first be spoken to you: but seeing ye reject it, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.
texts.act.13.47: For so hath the Lord commanded us, saying, I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldst be for salvation to the ends of the earth.
texts.act.13.48: And when the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of the Lord: and as many as were ordained to eternal life, believed.
texts.act.13.49: And the word of the Lord was published throughout all the region.
texts.act.13.50: But the Jews stirred up the devout and honorable women, and the chief men of the city, and raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and expelled them from their borders.
texts.act.13.51: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came to Iconium.
texts.act.13.52: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
texts.act.14.1: And it came to pass in Iconium, that they went both together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke, that a great multitude both of the Jews, and also of the Greeks, believed.
texts.act.14.2: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles, and made their minds evil-affected against the brethren.
texts.act.14.3: A long time therefore they abode speaking boldly in the Lord, who gave testimony to the word of his grace, and granted signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
texts.act.14.4: But the multitude of the city was divided: and part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.
texts.act.14.5: And when there was an assault made both of the Gentiles, and also of the Jews, with their rulers, to use them despitefully, and to stone them,
texts.act.14.6: Being apprised of it, they fled to Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and to the region in that vicinity.
texts.act.14.7: And there they preached the gospel.
texts.act.14.8: And there sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent in his feet, being a cripple from his mother's womb, who had never walked.
texts.act.14.9: The same heard Paul speak: who steadfastly beholding him, and perceiving that he had faith to be healed,
texts.act.14.10: Said with a loud voice, Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped and walked.
texts.act.14.11: And when the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men.
texts.act.14.12: And they called Barnabas, Jupiter, and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker.
texts.act.14.13: Then the priest of Jupiter, who was before their city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the people.
texts.act.14.14: Which, when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of, they rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out,
texts.act.14.15: And saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and preach to you, that ye should turn from these vanities to the living God, who made heaven and earth, and the sea, and all things that are in them.
texts.act.14.16: Who in times past suffered all nations to walk in their own ways.
texts.act.14.17: Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.
texts.act.14.18: And with these sayings they scarce restrained the people from doing sacrifice to them.
texts.act.14.19: And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch, and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing him to be dead.
texts.act.14.20: But as the disciples stood around him, he rose, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.
texts.act.14.21: And when they had preached the gospel to that city, and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and to Antioch,
texts.act.14.22: Confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.act.14.23: And when they had ordained for them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they believed.
texts.act.14.24: And after they had passed throughout Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
texts.act.14.25: And when they had preached the word in Perga, they went down into Attalia:
texts.act.14.26: And thence sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been commended to the grace of God, for the work which they fulfilled.
texts.act.14.27: And when they had come, and had assembled the church, they rehearsed all that God had done with them, and that he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
texts.act.14.28: And there they abode a long time with the disciples.
texts.act.15.1: And certain men who came down from Judea, taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.
texts.act.15.2: When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain others of them, should go to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders about this question.
texts.act.15.3: And being brought on their way by the church, they passed through Phenice, and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy to all the brethren.
texts.act.15.4: And when they had come to Jerusalem, they were received by the church, and by the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them.
texts.act.15.5: But there rose certain of the sect of the Pharisees, who believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.
texts.act.15.6: And the apostles and elders came together to consider of this matter.
texts.act.15.7: And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose and said to them, Men, brethren, ye know that a good while ago, God made choice among us, that the Gentiles, by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.
texts.act.15.8: And God, who knoweth the hearts, bore them witness, giving to them the Holy Spirit, even as he did to us:
texts.act.15.9: And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.
texts.act.15.10: Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
texts.act.15.11: But we believe, that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, we shall be saved even as they.
texts.act.15.12: Then all the multitude kept silence, and gave audience to Barnabas and Paul, declaring what miracles and wonders God had wrought by them among the Gentiles.
texts.act.15.13: And after they held their peace, James answered, saying, Men, brethren, hearken to me.
texts.act.15.14: Simeon hath declared how God at the first visited the Gentiles to take from among them a people for his name.
texts.act.15.15: And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written,
texts.act.15.16: After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins of it; and I will set it up:
texts.act.15.17: That the residue of men may seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called, saith the Lord, who doeth all these things.
texts.act.15.18: Known to God are all his works from the beginning of the world.
texts.act.15.19: Wherefore my sentence is, that we trouble not them, who from among the Gentiles are turned to God:
texts.act.15.20: But that we write to them that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from lewdness, and from things strangled, and from blood.
texts.act.15.21: For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath.
texts.act.15.22: Then it pleased the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch, with Paul and Barnabas; namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:
texts.act.15.23: And they wrote letters by them after this manner; The apostles, and elders, and brethren, send greeting to the brethren who are of the Gentiles in Antioch, and Syria, and Cilicia.
texts.act.15.24: Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain who went out from us, have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law; to whom we gave no such commandment:
texts.act.15.25: It seemed good to us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men to you, with our beloved Barnabas and Paul:
texts.act.15.26: Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.act.15.27: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who will also tell you the same things by mouth.
texts.act.15.28: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things;
texts.act.15.29: That ye abstain from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from lewdness: from which if ye keep yourselves, ye will do well. Fare ye well.
texts.act.15.30: So when they were dismissed, they came to Antioch: and when they had convened the multitude, they delivered the epistle.
texts.act.15.31: Which when they had read, they rejoiced for the consolation.
texts.act.15.32: And Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed them.
texts.act.15.33: And after they had tarried there a time, they were dismissed in peace from the brethren to the apostles.
texts.act.15.34: Notwithstanding, it pleased Silas to abide there still.
texts.act.15.35: Paul also and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.
texts.act.15.36: And some days after, Paul said to Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren, in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do.
texts.act.15.37: And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark.
texts.act.15.38: But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.
texts.act.15.39: And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed, separating one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed to Cyprus.
texts.act.15.40: And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being commended by the brethren to the grace of God.
texts.act.15.41: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.
texts.act.16.1: Then he came to Derbe and Lystra: and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a certain woman who was a Jewess, and believed, but his father was a Greek.
texts.act.16.2: Who was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.
texts.act.16.3: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him, because of the Jews who were in those quarters: for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
texts.act.16.4: And as they went through the cities, they delivered to them the decrees to keep that were ordained by the apostles and elders who were at Jerusalem.
texts.act.16.5: And so were the churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily.
texts.act.16.6: Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia, and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to preach the word in Asia;
texts.act.16.7: After they had come to Mysia, they essayed to go into Bithynia: but the Spirit suffered them not.
texts.act.16.8: And they, passing by Mysia, came down to Troas.
texts.act.16.9: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night: There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.
texts.act.16.10: And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavored to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering, that the Lord had called us to preach the gospel to them.
texts.act.16.11: Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis;
texts.act.16.12: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.
texts.act.16.13: And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spoke to the women who resorted thither.
texts.act.16.14: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, who worshiped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended to the things which were spoken by Paul.
texts.act.16.15: And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there: And she constrained us.
texts.act.16.16: And it came to pass as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination, met us, who brought her masters much gain by sooth-saying:
texts.act.16.17: The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, who show to us the way of salvation.
texts.act.16.18: And this she did many days. But Paul being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour.
texts.act.16.19: And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the market-place to the rulers,
texts.act.16.20: And brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city,
texts.act.16.21: And teach customs which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.
texts.act.16.22: And the multitude rose together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them.
texts.act.16.23: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailer to keep them safely.
texts.act.16.24: Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
texts.act.16.25: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises to God: and the prisoners heard them.
texts.act.16.26: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.
texts.act.16.27: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had fled.
texts.act.16.28: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.
texts.act.16.29: Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas;
texts.act.16.30: And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
texts.act.16.31: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
texts.act.16.32: And they spoke to him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.
texts.act.16.33: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, without delay.
texts.act.16.34: And when he had brought them into his house, he set food before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
texts.act.16.35: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the sergeants, saying, Let those men go.
texts.act.16.36: And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.
texts.act.16.37: But Paul said to them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privately? no verily; but let them come themselves and bring us out.
texts.act.16.38: And the sergeants told these words to the magistrates: and they feared when they heard that they were Romans.
texts.act.16.39: And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.
texts.act.16.40: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
texts.act.17.1: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis, and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews.
texts.act.17.2: And Paul, as his manner was, went in to them, and on three sabbaths reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
texts.act.17.3: Opening and alledging, that it was needful that Christ should suffer, and rise again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach to you, is Christ.
texts.act.17.4: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas: and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.
texts.act.17.5: But the Jews who believed not, moved with envy, took to them certain vile fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city in an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.
texts.act.17.6: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren to the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down, have come hither also;
texts.act.17.7: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Cesar, saying, That there is another king, one Jesus.
texts.act.17.8: And they troubled the people, and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.
texts.act.17.9: And when they had taken security of Jason and of the other, they let them go.
texts.act.17.10: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night to Berea: who coming thither, went into the synagogue of the Jews.
texts.act.17.11: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
texts.act.17.12: Therefore many of them believed; also of honorable women who were Greeks, and of men not a few.
texts.act.17.13: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached by Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.
texts.act.17.14: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul, to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timothy abode there still.
texts.act.17.15: And they that conducted Paul brought him to Athens: and receiving a commandment to Silas and Timothy to come to him with all speed, they departed.
texts.act.17.16: Now, while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.
texts.act.17.17: Therefore he disputed in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.
texts.act.17.18: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoics, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? some others, He seemeth to be a setter-forth of strange gods: because he preached to them Jesus, and the resurrection.
texts.act.17.19: And they took him, and brought him to Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine is, of which thou speakest?
texts.act.17.20: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears; we would know therefore what these things mean.
texts.act.17.21: (For all the Athenians and strangers who were there, spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)
texts.act.17.22: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars-hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.
texts.act.17.23: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I to you.
texts.act.17.24: God that made the world, and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
texts.act.17.25: Neither is worshiped with men's hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;
texts.act.17.26: And hath made of one blood all nations of men to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;
texts.act.17.27: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he is not far from every one of us:
texts.act.17.28: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, for we are also his offspring.
texts.act.17.29: Being then the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like to gold, or silver, or stone graven by art and man's device.
texts.act.17.30: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
texts.act.17.31: Because he hath appointed a day, in which he will judge the world in righteousness, by that man whom he hath ordained: of which he hath given assurance to all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.
texts.act.17.32: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again concerning this matter.
texts.act.17.33: So Paul departed from among them.
texts.act.17.34: But certain men adhered to him, and believed: among whom was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
texts.act.18.1: After these things, Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
texts.act.18.2: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome) and he came to them.
texts.act.18.3: And because he was of the same occupation, he abode with them, and wrought (for by their occupation they were tent-makers)
texts.act.18.4: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.
texts.act.18.5: And when Silas and Timothy had come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in spirit, and testified to the Jews, that Jesus was Christ.
texts.act.18.6: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said to them, Your blood be upon your own heads: I am clean: from henceforth I will go to the Gentiles.
texts.act.18.7: And he departed thence, and entered into the house of a certain man named Justus, one that worshiped God, whose house joined close to the synagogue.
texts.act.18.8: And Crispus the chief ruler of the synagogue believed on the Lord with all his house: and many of the Corinthians hearing, believed, and were baptized.
texts.act.18.9: Then the Lord spoke to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:
texts.act.18.10: For I am with thee, and no man shall lay hands on thee, to hurt thee: for I have many people in this city.
texts.act.18.11: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
texts.act.18.12: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment-seat,
texts.act.18.13: Saying, This man persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.
texts.act.18.14: And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong, or hainous crime, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:
texts.act.18.15: But if it is a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it: for I will be no judge of such matters.
texts.act.18.16: And he drove them from the judgment-seat.
texts.act.18.17: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment-seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.
texts.act.18.18: And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
texts.act.18.19: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
texts.act.18.20: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not:
texts.act.18.21: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return to you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.
texts.act.18.22: And when he had landed at Cesarea, and gone up and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.
texts.act.18.23: And after he had spent some time there, he departed and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
texts.act.18.24: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
texts.act.18.25: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord: and being fervent in the spirit, he spoke and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
texts.act.18.26: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: Whom, when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him to them, and expounded to him the way of God more perfectly.
texts.act.18.27: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he had come, helped them much who had believed through grace.
texts.act.18.28: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publicly, showing by the scriptures, that Jesus was Christ.
texts.act.19.1: And it came to pass, that while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper region, came to Ephesus; and finding certain disciples,
texts.act.19.2: He said to them, Have ye received the Holy Spirit since ye believed? And they said to him, We have not so much as heard whether there is any Holy Spirit.
texts.act.19.3: And he said to them, Into what then were ye baptized? And they said, Into John's baptism.
texts.act.19.4: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people, That they should believe on him who should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
texts.act.19.5: When they heard this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.19.6: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came on them; and they spoke in languages, and prophesied.
texts.act.19.7: And all the men were about twelve.
texts.act.19.8: And he went into the synagogue, and spoke boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
texts.act.19.9: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spoke evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
texts.act.19.10: And this continued for the space of two years; so that all they who dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
texts.act.19.11: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
texts.act.19.12: So that from his body were brought to the sick, handkerchiefs, or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
texts.act.19.13: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them who had evil spirits, the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
texts.act.19.14: And there were seven sons of one Sceva a Jew, and chief of the priests, who did so.
texts.act.19.15: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
texts.act.19.16: And the man in whom the evil spirit was, leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
texts.act.19.17: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus: and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
texts.act.19.18: And many that believed came, and confessed, and showed their deeds.
texts.act.19.19: Many also of them who used curious arts, brought their books together, and burned them before all men; and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
texts.act.19.20: So mightily grew the word of God, and prevailed.
texts.act.19.21: After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia, and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
texts.act.19.22: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered to him, Timothy and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.
texts.act.19.23: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.
texts.act.19.24: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silver-smith, who made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain to the artificers;
texts.act.19.25: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth:
texts.act.19.26: Moreover, ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away many people, saying, that they are no gods which are made with hands.
texts.act.19.27: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at naught; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia, and the world worshipeth.
texts.act.19.28: And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
texts.act.19.29: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theater.
texts.act.19.30: And when Paul would have entered in to the people, the disciples suffered him not.
texts.act.19.31: And certain of the chief of Asia, who were his friends, sent to him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theater.
texts.act.19.32: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused, and the greater part knew not why they had come together.
texts.act.19.33: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defense to the people.
texts.act.19.34: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
texts.act.19.35: And when the town-clerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not that the city of the Ephesians is a worshiper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?
texts.act.19.36: Seeing then that these things cannot be contradicted, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
texts.act.19.37: For ye have brought hither these men, who are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
texts.act.19.38: Wherefore, if Demetrius and the artificers who are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
texts.act.19.39: But if ye inquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.
texts.act.19.40: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day's uproar, there being no cause by which we may give an account of this concourse.
texts.act.19.41: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
texts.act.20.1: And after the uproar had ceased, Paul called to him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed to go into Macedonia.
texts.act.20.2: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
texts.act.20.3: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
texts.act.20.4: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of Asia, Tychicus, and Trophimus.
texts.act.20.5: These going before, tarried for us at Troas.
texts.act.20.6: And we sailed away from Philippi, after the days of unleavened bread, and came to them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.
texts.act.20.7: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached to them (ready to depart on the morrow) and continued his speech until midnight.
texts.act.20.8: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were assembled.
texts.act.20.9: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, having fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
texts.act.20.10: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him, said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
texts.act.20.11: When he had come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and discoursed a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
texts.act.20.12: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
texts.act.20.13: And we went before to a ship, and sailed to Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so he had appointed, intending himself to go on foot.
texts.act.20.14: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.
texts.act.20.15: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
texts.act.20.16: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
texts.act.20.17: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
texts.act.20.18: And when they had come to him, he said to them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,
texts.act.20.19: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:
texts.act.20.20: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable to you, but have shown you, and have taught you publicly, and from house to house,
texts.act.20.21: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance towards God, and faith towards our Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.act.20.22: And now behold, I go bound in the spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
texts.act.20.23: Save that the Holy Spirit testifieth in every city, saying, that bonds and afflictions abide me.
texts.act.20.24: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my course with joy, and the ministry which I have received from the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
texts.act.20.25: And now behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, will see my face no more.
texts.act.20.26: Wherefore I call you to witness this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.
texts.act.20.27: For I have not shunned to declare to you all the counsel of God.
texts.act.20.28: Take heed therefore to yourselves, and to all the flock over which the Holy Spirit hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
texts.act.20.29: For I know this, that after my departure grievous wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
texts.act.20.30: Also from your own selves will men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
texts.act.20.31: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.
texts.act.20.32: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them who are sanctified.
texts.act.20.33: I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel.
texts.act.20.34: And ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered to my necessities, and to them that were with me.
texts.act.20.35: I have shown you all things, that so laboring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
texts.act.20.36: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.
texts.act.20.37: And they all wept bitterly, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him,
texts.act.20.38: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spoke, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship.
texts.act.21.1: And it came to pass, that after we were separated from them, and had lanched, we came with a straight course to Coos, and the day following to Rhodes, and from thence to Patara:
texts.act.21.2: And finding a ship sailing over to Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
texts.act.21.3: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.
texts.act.21.4: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
texts.act.21.5: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed, and proceeded on our way; and they all conducted us with wives and children, till we were out of the city; and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.
texts.act.21.6: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.
texts.act.21.7: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
texts.act.21.8: And the next day we that were of Paul's company departed, and came to Cesarea; and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven; and abode with him.
texts.act.21.9: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, who prophesied.
texts.act.21.10: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judea a certain prophet, named Agabus.
texts.act.21.11: And when he had come to us, he took Paul's girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Spirit, So will the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
texts.act.21.12: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
texts.act.21.13: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep, and to break my heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.21.14: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
texts.act.21.15: And after those days we took up our furniture, and went up to Jerusalem.
texts.act.21.16: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.
texts.act.21.17: And when we had come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
texts.act.21.18: And the day following Paul went in with us to James: and all the elders were present.
texts.act.21.19: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
texts.act.21.20: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said to him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are who believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
texts.act.21.21: And they are informed concerning thee, that thou teachest all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying, That they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.
texts.act.21.22: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.
texts.act.21.23: Do therefore this that we say to thee: we have four men who have a vow on them;
texts.act.21.24: Take them, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things of which they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.
texts.act.21.25: As concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from lewdness.
texts.act.21.26: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them, entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until an offering should be offered for every one of them.
texts.act.21.27: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews who were from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
texts.act.21.28: Crying out, Men of Israel, help. This is the man that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further, hath brought Greeks also into the temple; and hath polluted this holy place.
texts.act.21.29: (For they had seen before with him in the city, Trophimus, an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
texts.act.21.30: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul and drew him out of the temple. And forthwith the doors were shut.
texts.act.21.31: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came to the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
texts.act.21.32: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down to them. And when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating Paul.
texts.act.21.33: Then the chief captain came near and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains: and inquired who he was, and what he had done.
texts.act.21.34: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
texts.act.21.35: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was that he was borne by the soldiers, for the violence of the people.
texts.act.21.36: For the multitude of the people followed, crying, Away with him.
texts.act.21.37: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said to the chief captain, May I speak to thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?
texts.act.21.38: Art not thou that Egyptian, who before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?
texts.act.21.39: But Paul said, I am a man who am a Jew of Tarsus, a city of Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and I beseech thee suffer me to speak to the people.
texts.act.21.40: And when he had given him license, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand to the people. And when there was made entire silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,
texts.act.22.1: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defense which I make now to you.
texts.act.22.2: (And when they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)
texts.act.22.3: I am verily a man who am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, being zealous towards God, as ye all are this day.
texts.act.22.4: And I persecuted this way even to death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
texts.act.22.5: As also the high priest doth bear me testimony, and all the estate of the elders; from whom also I received letters to the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them who were there bound to Jerusalem, to be punished.
texts.act.22.6: And it came to pass, that as I was passing on my journey, and had come nigh to Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light around me.
texts.act.22.7: And I fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
texts.act.22.8: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said to me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.
texts.act.22.9: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spoke to me.
texts.act.22.10: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said to me, Arise, and go into Damascus, and there it shall be told thee concerning all things which are appointed for thee to do.
texts.act.22.11: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.
texts.act.22.12: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews who dwelt there,
texts.act.22.13: Came to me, and stood, and said to me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
texts.act.22.14: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldst know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldst hear the voice of his mouth.
texts.act.22.15: For thou shalt be his witness to all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
texts.act.22.16: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
texts.act.22.17: And it came to pass, that when I had come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
texts.act.22.18: And saw him saying to me, Make haste, and depart quickly from Jerusalem; for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
texts.act.22.19: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned, and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
texts.act.22.20: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting to his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
texts.act.22.21: And he said to me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence to the Gentiles.
texts.act.22.22: And they gave him audience to this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a man from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
texts.act.22.23: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,
texts.act.22.24: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know for what cause they cried so against him.
texts.act.22.25: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said to the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
texts.act.22.26: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest; for this man is a Roman.
texts.act.22.27: Then the chief captain came, and said to him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yes.
texts.act.22.28: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum I obtained this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.
texts.act.22.29: Then forthwith they departed from him who were about to examine him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
texts.act.22.30: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty why he was accused by the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
texts.act.23.1: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men, brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
texts.act.23.2: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him, to strike him on the mouth.
texts.act.23.3: Then said Paul to him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me according to the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
texts.act.23.4: And they that stood by, said, Revilest thou God's high priest?
texts.act.23.5: Then said Paul, I knew not, brethren, that he is the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
texts.act.23.6: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men, brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
texts.act.23.7: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
texts.act.23.8: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
texts.act.23.9: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees' part arose, and contended, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
texts.act.23.10: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul would have been pulled in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.
texts.act.23.11: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified concerning me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear testimony also at Rome.
texts.act.23.12: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying, that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
