texts.act.10.41: not of all the people, but of witnesses who were chosen before of God, *us* who have eaten and drunk with him after he arose from among [the] dead.
texts.act.10.42: And he commanded us to preach to the people, and to testify that *he* it is who was determinately appointed of God [to be] judge of living and dead.
texts.act.10.43: To him all the prophets bear witness that every one that believes on him will receive through his name remission of sins.
texts.act.10.44: While Peter was yet speaking these words the Holy Spirit fell upon all those who were hearing the word.
texts.act.10.45: And the faithful of the circumcision were astonished, as many as came with Peter, that upon the nations also the gift of the Holy Spirit was poured out:
texts.act.10.46: for they heard them speaking with tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter answered,
texts.act.10.47: Can any one forbid water that these should not be baptised, who have received the Holy Spirit as we also [did]?
texts.act.10.48: And he commanded them to be baptised in the name of the Lord. Then they begged him to stay some days.
texts.act.11.1: And the apostles and the brethren who were in Judaea heard that the nations also had received the word of God;
texts.act.11.2: and when Peter went up to Jerusalem, they of the circumcision contended with him,
texts.act.11.3: saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised and hast eaten with them.
texts.act.11.4: But Peter began and set forth [the matter] to them in order, saying,
texts.act.11.5: I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in an ecstasy I saw a vision, a certain vessel descending like a great sheet, let down by four corners out of heaven, and it came even to me:
texts.act.11.6: on which having fixed mine eyes, I considered, and saw the quadrupeds of the earth, and the wild beasts, and the creeping things, and the fowls of the heaven.
texts.act.11.7: And I heard also a voice saying to me, Rise up, Peter, slay and eat.
texts.act.11.8: And I said, In no wise, Lord, for common or unclean has never entered into my mouth.
texts.act.11.9: And a voice answered the second time out of heaven, What God has cleansed, do not *thou* make common.
texts.act.11.10: And this took place thrice, and again all was drawn up into heaven;
texts.act.11.11: and lo, immediately three men were at the house in which I was, sent to me from Caesarea.
texts.act.11.12: And the Spirit said to me to go with them, nothing doubting. And there went with me these six brethren also, and we entered into the house of the man,
texts.act.11.13: and he related to us how he had seen the angel in his house, standing and saying [to him], Send [men] to Joppa and fetch Simon, who is surnamed Peter,
texts.act.11.14: who shall speak words to thee whereby *thou* shalt be saved, thou and all thy house.
texts.act.11.15: And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them even as upon us also at the beginning.
texts.act.11.16: And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, John baptised with water, but *ye* shall be baptised with [the] Holy Spirit.
texts.act.11.17: If then God has given them the same gift as also to us when we had believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, who indeed was *I* to be able to forbid God?
texts.act.11.18: And when they heard these things they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then indeed God has to the nations also granted repentance to life.
texts.act.11.19: They then who had been scattered abroad through the tribulation that took place on the occasion of Stephen, passed through [the country] to Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to no one but to Jews alone.
texts.act.11.20: But there were certain of them, Cyprians and Cyrenians, who entering into Antioch spoke to the Greeks also, announcing the glad tidings of the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.11.21: And [the] Lord's hand was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.
texts.act.11.22: And the report concerning them reached the ears of the assembly which was in Jerusalem, and they sent out Barnabas to go through as far as Antioch:
texts.act.11.23: who, having arrived and seeing the grace of God, rejoiced, and exhorted all with purpose of heart to abide with the Lord;
texts.act.11.24: for he was a good man and full of [the] Holy Spirit and of faith; and a large crowd [of people] were added to the Lord.
texts.act.11.25: And he went away to Tarsus to seek out Saul.
texts.act.11.26: And having found [him], he brought him to Antioch. And so it was with them that for a whole year they were gathered together in the assembly and taught a large crowd: and the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
texts.act.11.27: Now in these days prophets went down from Jerusalem to Antioch;
texts.act.11.28: and one from among them, by name Agabus, rose up and signified by the Spirit that there was going to be a great famine over all the inhabited earth, which also came to pass under Claudius.
texts.act.11.29: And they determined, according as any one of the disciples was well off, each of them to send to the brethren who dwelt in Judaea, to minister [to them];
texts.act.11.30: which also they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
texts.act.12.1: At that time Herod the king laid his hands on some of those of the assembly to do them hurt,
texts.act.12.2: and slew James, the brother of John, with the sword.
texts.act.12.3: And seeing that it was pleasing to the Jews, he went on to take Peter also: (and they were the days of unleavened bread:)
texts.act.12.4: whom having seized he put in prison, having delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to keep, purposing after the passover to bring him out to the people.
texts.act.12.5: Peter therefore was kept in the prison; but unceasing prayer was made by the assembly to God concerning him.
texts.act.12.6: And when Herod was going to bring him forth, that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards before the door kept the prison.
texts.act.12.7: And lo, an angel of [the] Lord came there, and a light shone in the prison: and having smitten the side of Peter, he roused him up, saying, Rise up quickly. And his chains fell off his hands.
texts.act.12.8: And the angel said to him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals. And he did so. And he says to him, Cast thine upper garment about thee and follow me.
texts.act.12.9: And going forth he followed [him] and did not know that what was happening by means of the angel was real, but supposed he saw a vision.
texts.act.12.10: And having passed through a first and second guard, they came to the iron gate which leads into the city, which opened to them of itself; and going forth they went down one street, and immediately the angel left him.
texts.act.12.11: And Peter, being come to himself, said, Now I know certainly that [the] Lord has sent forth his angel and has taken me out of the hand of Herod and all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
texts.act.12.12: And having become clearly conscious [in himself], he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was surnamed Mark, where were many gathered together and praying.
texts.act.12.13: And when he had knocked at the door of the entry, a maid came to listen, by name Rhoda;
texts.act.12.14: and having recognised the voice of Peter, through joy did not open the entry, but running in, reported that Peter was standing before the entry.
texts.act.12.15: And they said to her, Thou art mad. But she maintained that it was so. And they said, It is his angel.
texts.act.12.16: But Peter continued knocking: and having opened, they saw him and were astonished.
texts.act.12.17: And having made a sign to them with his hand to be silent, he related [to them] how the Lord had brought him out of prison; and he said, Report these things to James and to the brethren. And he went out and went to another place.
texts.act.12.18: And when it was day there was no small disturbance among the soldiers, what then was become of Peter.
texts.act.12.19: And Herod having sought him and not found him, having examined the guards, commanded [them] to be executed. And he went down from Judaea to Caesarea and stayed [there].
texts.act.12.20: And he was in bitter hostility with [the] Tyrians and Sidonians; but they came to him with one accord, and, having gained Blastus the king's chamberlain, sought peace, because their country was nourished by the king's.
texts.act.12.21: And on a set day, clothed in royal apparel and sitting on the elevated seat [of honour], Herod made a public oration to them.
texts.act.12.22: And the people cried out, A god's voice and not a man's.
texts.act.12.23: And immediately an angel of [the] Lord smote him, because he did not give the glory to God, and he expired, eaten of worms.
texts.act.12.24: But the word of God grew and spread itself.
texts.act.12.25: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, having fulfilled the service [entrusted to them], taking also with them John, surnamed Mark.
texts.act.13.1: Now there were in Antioch, in the assembly which was [there], prophets and teachers: Barnabas, and Simeon who was called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, and Manaen, foster-brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
texts.act.13.2: And as they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, Separate me now Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.
texts.act.13.3: Then, having fasted and prayed, and having laid [their] hands on them, they let [them] go.
texts.act.13.4: They therefore, having been sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia, and thence sailed away to Cyprus.
texts.act.13.5: And being in Salamis, they announced the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. And they had John also as [their] attendant.
texts.act.13.6: And having passed through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain man a magician, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesus,
texts.act.13.7: who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. *He*, having called Barnabas and Saul to [him], desired to hear the word of God.
texts.act.13.8: But Elymas the magician (for so his name is by interpretation) opposed them, seeking to turn away the proconsul from the faith.
texts.act.13.9: But Saul, who also [is] Paul, filled with [the] Holy Spirit, fixing his eyes upon him,
texts.act.13.10: said, O full of all deceit and all craft: son of [the] devil, enemy of all righteousness; wilt thou not cease perverting the right paths of [the] Lord?
texts.act.13.11: And now behold, [the] Lord's hand [is] upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. And immediately there fell upon him a mist and darkness; and going about he sought persons who should lead him by the hand.
texts.act.13.12: Then the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed, being amazed at the teaching of the Lord.
texts.act.13.13: And having sailed from Paphos, Paul and his company came to Perga of Pamphylia; and John separated from them and returned to Jerusalem.
texts.act.13.14: But they, passing through from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia; and entering into the synagogue on the sabbath day they sat down.
texts.act.13.15: And after the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, Brethren, if ye have any word of exhortation to the people, speak.
texts.act.13.16: And Paul, rising up and making a sign with the hand, said, Israelites, and ye that fear God, hearken.
texts.act.13.17: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people in their sojourn in [the] land of Egypt, and with a high arm brought them out of it,
texts.act.13.18: and for a time of about forty years he nursed them in the desert.
texts.act.13.19: And having destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave them their land as an inheritance.
texts.act.13.20: And after these things he gave [them] judges till Samuel the prophet, [to the end of] about four hundred and fifty years.
texts.act.13.21: And then they asked for a king, and God gave to them Saul, son of Kis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, during forty years.
texts.act.13.22: And having removed him he raised up to them David for king, of whom also bearing witness he said, I have found David, the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who shall do all my will.
texts.act.13.23: Of this man's seed according to promise has God brought to Israel a Saviour, Jesus;
texts.act.13.24: John having proclaimed before the face of his entry [among the people] [the] baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
texts.act.13.25: And as John was fulfilling his course he said, Whom do ye suppose that I am? *I* am not [he]. But behold, there comes one after me, the sandal of whose feet I am not worthy to loose.
texts.act.13.26: Brethren, sons of Abraham's race, and those who among you fear God, to you has the word of this salvation been sent:
texts.act.13.27: for those who dwell in Jerusalem, and their rulers, not having known him, have fulfilled also the voices of the prophets which are read on every sabbath, [by] judging [him].
texts.act.13.28: And having found no cause of death [in him], they begged of Pilate that he might be slain.
texts.act.13.29: And when they had fulfilled all things written concerning him, they took him down from the cross and put him in a sepulchre;
texts.act.13.30: but God raised him from among [the] dead,
texts.act.13.31: who appeared for many days to those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses to the people.
texts.act.13.32: And *we* declare unto you the glad tidings of the promise made to the fathers,
texts.act.13.33: that God has fulfilled this to us their children, having raised up Jesus; as it is also written in the second psalm, *Thou* art my Son: this day have *I* begotten thee.
texts.act.13.34: But that he raised him from among [the] dead, no more to return to corruption, he spoke thus: I will give to you the faithful mercies of David.
texts.act.13.35: Wherefore also he says in another, Thou wilt not suffer thy gracious one to see corruption.
texts.act.13.36: For David indeed, having in his own generation ministered to the will of God, fell asleep, and was added to his fathers and saw corruption.
texts.act.13.37: But he whom God raised up did not see corruption.
texts.act.13.38: Be it known unto you, therefore, brethren, that through this man remission of sins is preached to you,
texts.act.13.39: and from all things from which ye could not be justified in the law of Moses, in him every one that believes is justified.
texts.act.13.40: See therefore that that which is spoken in the prophets do not come upon [you],
texts.act.13.41: Behold, ye despisers, and wonder and perish; for *I* work a work in your days, a work which ye will in no wise believe if one declare it to you.
texts.act.13.42: And as they went out they begged that these words might be spoken to them the ensuing sabbath.
texts.act.13.43: And the congregation of the synagogue having broken up, many of the Jews and of the worshipping proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who speaking to them, persuaded them to continue in the grace of God.
texts.act.13.44: And on the coming sabbath almost all the city was gathered together to hear the word of God.
texts.act.13.45: But the Jews, seeing the crowds, were filled with envy, and contradicted the things said by Paul, [contradicting and] speaking injuriously.
texts.act.13.46: And Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly and said, It was necessary that the word of God should be first spoken to you; but, since ye thrust it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, lo, we turn to the nations;
texts.act.13.47: for thus has the Lord enjoined us: I have set thee for a light of the nations, that thou shouldest be for salvation to the end of the earth.
texts.act.13.48: And [those of] the nations, hearing it, rejoiced, and glorified the word of the Lord, and believed, as many as were ordained to eternal life.
texts.act.13.49: And the word of the Lord was carried through the whole country.
texts.act.13.50: But the Jews excited the women of the upper classes who were worshippers, and the first people of the city, and raised a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and cast them out of their coasts.
texts.act.13.51: But they, having shaken off the dust of their feet against them, came to Iconium.
texts.act.13.52: And the disciples were filled with joy and [the] Holy Spirit.
texts.act.14.1: And it came to pass in Iconium that they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spake that a great multitude of both Jews and Greeks believed.
texts.act.14.2: But the Jews who did not believe stirred up the minds of [those of] the nations and made [them] evil-affected against the brethren.
texts.act.14.3: They stayed therefore a good while, speaking boldly, [confiding] in the Lord, who gave witness to the word of his grace, giving signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
texts.act.14.4: And the multitude of the city was divided, and some were with the Jews and some with the apostles.
texts.act.14.5: And when an assault was making, both of [those of] the nations and [the] Jews with their rulers, to use [them] ill and stone them,
texts.act.14.6: they, being aware of it, fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the surrounding country,
texts.act.14.7: and there they were announcing the glad tidings.
texts.act.14.8: And a certain man in Lystra, impotent in his feet, sat, [being] lame from his mother's womb, who had never walked.
texts.act.14.9: This [man] heard Paul speaking, who, fixing his eyes on him, and seeing that he had faith to be healed,
texts.act.14.10: said with a loud voice, Rise up straight upon thy feet: and he sprang up and walked.
texts.act.14.11: But the crowds, who saw what Paul had done, lifted up their voices in Lycaonian, saying, The gods, having made themselves like men, are come down to us.
texts.act.14.12: And they called Barnabas Jupiter, and Paul Mercury, because he took the lead in speaking.
texts.act.14.13: And the priest of Jupiter who was before the city, having brought bulls and garlands to the gates, would have done sacrifice along with the crowds.
texts.act.14.14: But the apostles Barnabas and Paul, having heard [it], rent their garments, and rushed out to the crowd, crying
texts.act.14.15: and saying, Men, why do ye these things? *We* also are men of like passions with you, preaching to you to turn from these vanities to the living God, who made the heaven, and the earth, and the sea, and all things in them;
texts.act.14.16: who in the past generations suffered all the nations to go in their own ways,
texts.act.14.17: though indeed he did not leave himself without witness, doing good, and giving to you from heaven rain and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.
texts.act.14.18: And saying these things, they with difficulty kept the crowds from sacrificing to them.
texts.act.14.19: But there came Jews from Antioch and Iconium, and having persuaded the crowds and stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing him to have died.
texts.act.14.20: But while the disciples encircled him, he rose up and entered into the city. And on the morrow he went away with Barnabas to Derbe.
texts.act.14.21: And having announced the glad tidings to that city, and having made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, and Iconium, and Antioch,
texts.act.14.22: establishing the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to abide in the faith, and that through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.act.14.23: And having chosen them elders in each assembly, having prayed with fastings, they committed them to the Lord, on whom they had believed.
texts.act.14.24: And having passed through Pisidia they came to Pamphylia,
texts.act.14.25: and having spoken the word in Perga, they came down to Attalia;
texts.act.14.26: and thence they sailed away to Antioch, whence they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.
texts.act.14.27: And having arrived, and having brought together the assembly, they related to them all that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the nations.
texts.act.14.28: And they stayed no little time with the disciples.
texts.act.15.1: And certain persons, having come down from Judaea, taught the brethren, If ye shall not have been circumcised according to the custom of Moses, ye cannot be saved.
texts.act.15.2: A commotion therefore having taken place, and no small discussion on the part of Paul and Barnabas against them, they arranged that Paul and Barnabas, and certain others from amongst them, should go up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders about this question.
texts.act.15.3: They therefore, having been set on their way by the assembly, passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, relating the conversion of [those of] the nations. And they caused great joy to all the brethren.
texts.act.15.4: And being arrived at Jerusalem, they were received by the assembly, and the apostles, and the elders, and related all that God had wrought with them.
texts.act.15.5: And some of those who were of the sect of the Pharisees, who believed, rose up from among [them], saying that they ought to circumcise them and enjoin them to keep the law of Moses.
texts.act.15.6: And the apostles and the elders were gathered together to see about this matter.
texts.act.15.7: And much discussion having taken place, Peter, standing up, said to them, Brethren, *ye* know that from the earliest days God amongst you chose that the nations by my mouth should hear the word of the glad tidings and believe.
texts.act.15.8: And the heart-knowing God bore them witness, giving [them] the Holy Spirit as to us also,
texts.act.15.9: and put no difference between us and them, having purified their hearts by faith.
texts.act.15.10: Now therefore why tempt ye God, by putting a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear?
texts.act.15.11: But we believe that we shall be saved by the grace of the Lord Jesus, in the same manner as they also.
texts.act.15.12: And all the multitude kept silence and listened to Barnabas and Paul relating all the signs and wonders which God had wrought among the nations by them.
texts.act.15.13: And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying, Brethren, listen to me:
texts.act.15.14: Simon has related how God first visited to take out of [the] nations a people for his name.
texts.act.15.15: And with this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written:
texts.act.15.16: After these things I will return, and will rebuild the tabernacle of David which is fallen, and will rebuild its ruins, and will set it up,
texts.act.15.17: so that the residue of men may seek out the Lord, and all the nations on whom my name is invoked, saith [the] Lord, who does these things
texts.act.15.19: Wherefore *I* judge, not to trouble those who from the nations turn to God;
texts.act.15.20: but to write to them to abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from what is strangled, and from blood.
texts.act.15.21: For Moses, from generations of old, has in every city those who preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath.
texts.act.15.22: Then it seemed good to the apostles and to the elders, with the whole assembly, to send chosen men from among them with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch, Judas called Barsabas and Silas, leading men among the brethren,
texts.act.15.23: having by their hand written [thus]: The apostles, and the elders, and the brethren, to the brethren who are from among [the] nations at Antioch, and [in] Syria and Cilicia, greeting:
texts.act.15.24: Inasmuch as we have heard that some who went out from amongst us have troubled you by words, upsetting your souls, [saying that ye must be circumcised and keep the law]; to whom we gave no commandment;
texts.act.15.25: it seemed good to us, having arrived at a common judgment, to send chosen men to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
texts.act.15.26: men who have given up their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.act.15.27: We have therefore sent Judas and Silas, who themselves also will tell you by word [of mouth] the same things.
texts.act.15.28: For it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things:
texts.act.15.29: to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what is strangled, and from fornication; keeping yourselves from which ye will do well. Farewell.
texts.act.15.30: They therefore, being let go, came to Antioch, and having gathered the multitude delivered to [them] the epistle.
texts.act.15.31: And having read it, they rejoiced at the consolation.
texts.act.15.32: And Judas and Silas, being themselves also prophets, exhorted the brethren with much discourse, and strengthened them.
texts.act.15.33: And having passed some time [there], they were let go in peace from the brethren to those who sent them.
texts.act.15.35: And Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and announcing the glad tidings, with many others also, of the word of the Lord.
texts.act.15.36: But after certain days Paul said to Barnabas, Let us return now and visit the brethren in every city where we have announced the word of the Lord, [and see] how they are getting on.
texts.act.15.37: And Barnabas proposed to take with [them] John also, called Mark;
texts.act.15.38: but Paul thought it not well to take with them him who had abandoned them, [going back] from Pamphylia, and had not gone with them to the work.
texts.act.15.39: There arose therefore very warm feeling, so that they separated from one another; and Barnabas taking Mark sailed away to Cyprus;
texts.act.15.40: but Paul having chosen Silas went forth, committed by the brethren to the grace of God.
texts.act.15.41: And he passed through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the assemblies.
texts.act.16.1: And he came to Derbe and Lystra: and behold, a certain disciple was there, by name Timotheus, son of a Jewish believing woman, but [the] father a Greek,
texts.act.16.2: who had a [good] testimony of the brethren in Lystra and Iconium.
texts.act.16.3: Him would Paul have go forth with him, and took [him and] circumcised him on account of the Jews who were in those places, for they all knew his father that he was a Greek.
texts.act.16.4: And as they passed through the cities they instructed them to observe the decrees determined on by the apostles and elders who were in Jerusalem.
texts.act.16.5: The assemblies therefore were confirmed in the faith, and increased in number every day.
texts.act.16.6: And having passed through Phrygia and the Galatian country, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia,
texts.act.16.7: having come down to Mysia, they attempted to go to Bithynia, and the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them;
texts.act.16.8: and having passed by Mysia they descended to Troas.
texts.act.16.9: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night: There was a certain Macedonian man, standing and beseeching him, and saying, Pass over into Macedonia and help us.
texts.act.16.10: And when he had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go forth to Macedonia, concluding that the Lord had called us to announce to them the glad tidings.
texts.act.16.11: Having sailed therefore away from Troas, we went in a straight course to Samothracia, and on the morrow to Neapolis,
texts.act.16.12: and thence to Philippi, which is [the] first city of that part of Macedonia, a colony. And we were staying in that city certain days.
texts.act.16.13: And on the sabbath day we went outside the gate by the river, where it was the custom for prayer to be, and we sat down and spoke to the women who had assembled.
texts.act.16.14: And a certain woman, by name Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, who worshipped God, heard; whose heart the Lord opened to attend to the things spoken by Paul.
texts.act.16.15: And when she had been baptised and her house, she besought [us], saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and abide [there]. And she constrained us.
texts.act.16.16: And it came to pass as we were going to prayer that a certain female slave, having a spirit of Python, met us, who brought much profit to her masters by prophesying.
texts.act.16.17: She, having followed Paul and us, cried saying, These men are bondmen of the Most High God, who announce to you [the] way of salvation.
texts.act.16.18: And this she did many days. And Paul, being distressed, turned, and said to the spirit, I enjoin thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And it came out the same hour.
texts.act.16.19: And her masters, seeing that the hope of their gains was gone, having seized Paul and Silas, dragged [them] into the market before the magistrates;
texts.act.16.20: and having brought them up to the praetors, said, These men utterly trouble our city, being Jews,
texts.act.16.21: and announce customs which it is not lawful for us to receive nor practise, being Romans.
texts.act.16.22: And the crowd rose up too against them; and the praetors, having torn off their clothes, commanded to scourge [them].
texts.act.16.23: And having laid many stripes upon them they cast [them] into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely;
texts.act.16.24: who, having received such a charge, cast them into the inner prison, and secured their feet to the stocks.
texts.act.16.25: And at midnight Paul and Silas, in praying, were praising God with singing, and the prisoners listened to them.
texts.act.16.26: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison shook, and all the doors were immediately opened, and the bonds of all loosed.
texts.act.16.27: And the jailor being awakened out of his sleep, and seeing the doors of the prison opened, having drawn a sword was going to kill himself, thinking the prisoners had fled.
texts.act.16.28: But Paul called out with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm, for we are all here.
texts.act.16.29: And having asked for lights, he rushed in, and, trembling, fell down before Paul and Silas.
texts.act.16.30: And leading them out said, Sirs, what must I do that I may be saved?
texts.act.16.31: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus and thou shalt be saved, thou and thy house.
texts.act.16.32: And they spoke to him the word of the Lord, with all that were in his house.
texts.act.16.33: And he took them the same hour of the night and washed [them] from their stripes; and was baptised, he and all his straightway.
texts.act.16.34: And having brought them into his house he laid the table [for them], and rejoiced with all his house, having believed in God.
texts.act.16.35: And when it was day, the praetors sent the lictors, saying, Let those men go.
texts.act.16.36: And the jailor reported these words to Paul: The praetors have sent that ye may be let go. Now therefore go out and depart in peace.
texts.act.16.37: But Paul said to them, Having beaten us publicly uncondemned, us who are Romans, they have cast us into prison, and now they thrust us out secretly? no, indeed, but let them come themselves and bring us out.
texts.act.16.38: And the lictors reported these words to the praetors. And they were afraid when they heard they were Romans.
texts.act.16.39: And they came and besought them, and having brought them out, asked them to go out of the city.
texts.act.16.40: And having gone out of the prison, they came to Lydia; and having seen the brethren, they exhorted them and went away.
texts.act.17.1: And having journeyed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was the synagogue of the Jews.
texts.act.17.2: And according to Paul's custom he went in among them, and on three sabbaths reasoned with them from the scriptures,
texts.act.17.3: opening and laying down that the Christ must have suffered and risen up from among the dead, and that this is the Christ, Jesus whom *I* announce to you.
texts.act.17.4: And some of them believed, and joined themselves to Paul and Silas, and of the Greeks who worshipped, a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.
texts.act.17.5: But the Jews having been stirred up to jealousy, and taken to [themselves] certain wicked men of the lowest rabble, and having got a crowd together, set the city in confusion; and having beset the house of Jason sought to bring them out to the people;
texts.act.17.6: and not having found them, dragged Jason and certain brethren before the politarchs, crying out, These [men] that have set the world in tumult, are come here also,
texts.act.17.7: whom Jason has received; and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying, that there is another king, Jesus.
texts.act.17.8: And they troubled the crowd and the politarchs when they heard these things.
texts.act.17.9: And having taken security of Jason and the rest, they let them go.
texts.act.17.10: But the brethren immediately sent away, in the night, Paul and Silas to Berea; who, being arrived, went away into the synagogue of the Jews.
texts.act.17.11: And these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, receiving the word with all readiness of mind, daily searching the scriptures if these things were so.
texts.act.17.12: Therefore many from among them believed, and of Grecian women of the upper classes and men not a few.
texts.act.17.13: But when the Jews from Thessalonica knew that the word of God was announced in Berea also by Paul, they came there also, stirring up the crowds.
texts.act.17.14: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as to the sea; but Silas and Timotheus abode there.
texts.act.17.15: But they that conducted Paul brought him as far as Athens; and, having received a commandment to Silas and Timotheus, that they should come to him as quickly as possible, they departed.
texts.act.17.16: But in Athens, while Paul was waiting for them, his spirit was painfully excited in him seeing the city given up to idolatry.
texts.act.17.17: He reasoned therefore in the synagogue with the Jews, and those who worshipped, and in the market-place every day with those he met with.
texts.act.17.18: But some also of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers attacked him. And some said, What would this chatterer say? and some, He seems to be an announcer of foreign demons, because he announced the glad tidings of Jesus and the resurrection [to them].
texts.act.17.19: And having taken hold on him they brought [him] to Areopagus, saying, Might we know what this new doctrine which is spoken by thee [is]?
texts.act.17.20: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears. We wish therefore to know what these things may mean.
texts.act.17.21: Now all [the] Athenians and the strangers sojourning there spent their time in nothing else than to tell and to hear the news.
texts.act.17.22: And Paul standing in the midst of Areopagus said, Athenians, in every way I see you given up to demon worship;
texts.act.17.23: for, passing through and beholding your shrines, I found also an altar on which was inscribed, To the unknown God. Whom therefore ye reverence, not knowing [him], him I announce to you.
texts.act.17.24: The God who has made the world and all things which are in it, *he*, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands,
texts.act.17.25: nor is served by men's hands as needing something, himself giving to all life and breath and all things;
texts.act.17.26: and has made of one blood every nation of men to dwell upon the whole face of the earth, having determined ordained times and the boundaries of their dwelling,
texts.act.17.27: that they may seek God; if indeed they might feel after him and find him, although he is not far from each one of us:
texts.act.17.28: for in him we live and move and exist; as also some of the poets amongst you have said, For we are also his offspring.
texts.act.17.29: Being therefore [the] offspring of God, we ought not to think that which is divine to be like gold or silver or stone, [the] graven form of man's art and imagination.
texts.act.17.30: God therefore, having overlooked the times of ignorance, now enjoins men that they shall all everywhere repent,
texts.act.17.31: because he has set a day in which he is going to judge the habitable earth in righteousness by [the] man whom he has appointed, giving the proof [of it] to all [in] having raised him from among [the] dead.
texts.act.17.32: And when they heard [of the] resurrection of the dead, some mocked, and some said, We will hear thee again also concerning this.
texts.act.17.33: Thus Paul went out of their midst.
texts.act.17.34: But some men joining themselves to him believed; among whom also was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman by name Damaris, and others with them.
texts.act.18.1: And after these things, having left Athens, he came to Corinth;
texts.act.18.2: and finding a certain Jew by name Aquila, of Pontus by race, just come from Italy, and Priscilla his wife, (because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome,) came to them,
texts.act.18.3: and because they were of the same trade abode with them, and wrought. For they were tent-makers by trade.
texts.act.18.4: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded Jews and Greeks.
texts.act.18.5: And when both Silas and Timotheus came down from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in respect of the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.
texts.act.18.6: But as they opposed and spoke injuriously, he shook his clothes, and said to them, Your blood be upon your own head: *I* [am] pure; from henceforth I will go to the nations.
texts.act.18.7: And departing thence he came to the house of a certain [man], by name Justus, who worshipped God, whose house adjoined the synagogue.
texts.act.18.8: But Crispus the ruler of the synagogue believed in the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing, believed, and were baptised.
texts.act.18.9: And the Lord said by vision in [the] night to Paul, Fear not, but speak and be not silent;
texts.act.18.10: because *I* am with thee, and no one shall set upon thee to injure thee; because I have much people in this city.
texts.act.18.11: And he remained [there] a year and six months, teaching among them the word of God.
texts.act.18.12: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one consent rose against Paul and led him to the judgment-seat,
texts.act.18.13: saying, This [man] persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.
texts.act.18.14: But as Paul was going to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, If indeed it was some wrong or wicked criminality, O Jews, of reason I should have borne with you;
texts.act.18.15: but if it be questions about words, and names, and the law that ye have, see to it yourselves; [for] *I* do not intend to be judge of these things.
texts.act.18.16: And he drove them from the judgment-seat.
texts.act.18.17: And having all laid hold on Sosthenes the ruler of the synagogue, they beat him before the judgment-seat. And Gallio troubled himself about none of these things.
texts.act.18.18: And Paul, having yet stayed [there] many days, took leave of the brethren and sailed thence to Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila, having shorn his head in Cenchrea, for he had a vow;
texts.act.18.19: and he arrived at Ephesus, and left them there. But entering himself into the synagogue he reasoned with the Jews.
texts.act.18.20: And when they asked him that he would remain for a longer time [with them] he did not accede,
texts.act.18.21: but bade them farewell, saying, [I must by all means keep the coming feast at Jerusalem]; I will return to you again, if God will: and he sailed away from Ephesus.
texts.act.18.22: And landing at Caesarea, and having gone up and saluted the assembly, he went down to Antioch.
texts.act.18.23: And having stayed [there] some time, he went forth, passing in order through the country of Galatia and Phrygia, establishing all the disciples.
texts.act.18.24: But a certain Jew, Apollos by name, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, who was mighty in the scriptures, arrived at Ephesus.
texts.act.18.25: He was instructed in the way of the Lord, and being fervent in his spirit, he spoke and taught exactly the things concerning Jesus, knowing only the baptism of John.
texts.act.18.26: And *he* began to speak boldly in the synagogue. And Aquila and Priscilla, having heard him, took him to [them] and unfolded to him the way of God more exactly.
texts.act.18.27: And when he purposed to go into Achaia, the brethren wrote to the disciples engaging them to receive him, who, being come, contributed much to those who believed through grace.
texts.act.18.28: For he with great force convinced the Jews publicly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.
texts.act.19.1: And it came to pass, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper districts, came to Ephesus, and finding certain disciples,
texts.act.19.2: he said to them, Did ye receive [the] Holy Spirit when ye had believed? And they [said] to him, We did not even hear if [the] Holy Spirit was [come].
texts.act.19.3: And he said, To what then were ye baptised? And they said, To the baptism of John.
texts.act.19.4: And Paul said, John indeed baptised [with] the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe on him that was coming after him, that is, on Jesus.
texts.act.19.5: And when they heard that, they were baptised to the name of the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.19.6: And Paul having laid [his] hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke with tongues and prophesied.
texts.act.19.7: And all the men were about twelve.
texts.act.19.8: And entering into the synagogue, he spoke boldly during three months, reasoning and persuading [the things] concerning the kingdom of God.
texts.act.19.9: But when some were hardened and disbelieved, speaking evil of the way before the multitude, he left them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.
texts.act.19.10: And this took place for two years, so that all that inhabited Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.
texts.act.19.11: And God wrought no ordinary miracles by the hands of Paul,
texts.act.19.12: so that even napkins or aprons were brought from his body [and put] upon the sick, and the diseases left them, and the wicked spirits went out.
texts.act.19.13: And certain of the Jewish exorcists also, who went about, took in hand to call upon those who had wicked spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, I adjure you by Jesus, whom Paul preaches.
texts.act.19.14: And there were certain [men], seven sons of Sceva, Jewish high priest, who were doing this.
texts.act.19.15: But the wicked spirit answering said to them, Jesus I know, and Paul I am acquainted with; but *ye*, who are ye?
texts.act.19.16: And the man in whom the wicked spirit was leaped upon them, and having mastered both, prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
texts.act.19.17: And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who inhabited Ephesus, and fear fell upon all of them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
texts.act.19.18: And many of those that believed came confessing and declaring their deeds.
texts.act.19.19: And many of those that practised curious arts brought their books [of charms] and burnt them before all. And they reckoned up the prices of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
texts.act.19.20: Thus with might the word of the Lord increased and prevailed.
texts.act.19.21: And when these things were fulfilled, Paul purposed in his spirit to go to Jerusalem, passing through Macedonia and Achaia, saying, After I have been there I must see Rome also.
texts.act.19.22: And having sent into Macedonia two of those ministering to him, Timotheus and Erastus, he remained himself awhile in Asia.
texts.act.19.23: And there took place at that time no small disturbance about the way.
texts.act.19.24: For a certain [man] by name Demetrius, a silver-beater, making silver temples of Artemis, brought no small gain to the artisans;
texts.act.19.25: whom having brought together, and those who wrought in such things, he said, Men, ye know that our well-living arises from this work,
texts.act.19.26: and ye see and hear that this Paul has persuaded and turned away a great crowd, not only of Ephesus, but almost of all Asia, saying that they are no gods which are made with hands.
texts.act.19.27: Now not only there is danger for us that our business come into discredit, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis be counted for nothing, and that her greatness should be destroyed whom the whole of Asia and the world reveres.
texts.act.19.28: And having heard [this], and being filled with rage, they cried out, saying, Great [is] Artemis of the Ephesians.
texts.act.19.29: And the [whole] city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord to the theatre, having seized and carried off with [them] Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, fellow-travellers of Paul.
texts.act.19.30: But Paul intending to go in to the people, the disciples suffered him not;
texts.act.19.31: and some of the Asiarchs also, who were his friends, sent to him and urged him not to throw himself into the theatre.
texts.act.19.32: Different persons therefore cried out some different thing; for the assembly was tumultuous, and the most did not know for what cause they had come together.
texts.act.19.33: But from among the crowd they put forward Alexander, the Jews pushing him forward. And Alexander, beckoning with his hand, would have made a defence to the people.
texts.act.19.34: But, recognising that he was a Jew, there was one cry from all, shouting for about two hours, Great [is] Artemis of the Ephesians.
texts.act.19.35: And the townclerk, having quieted the crowd, said, Ephesians, what man is there then who does not know that the city of the Ephesians is temple-keeper of Artemis the great, and of the [image] which fell down from heaven?
texts.act.19.36: These things therefore being undeniable, it is necessary that ye should be calm and do nothing headlong.
texts.act.19.37: For ye have brought these men, [who are] neither temple-plunderers, nor speak injuriously of your goddess.
texts.act.19.38: If therefore Demetrius and the artisans who [are] with him have a matter against any one, the courts are being held, and there are proconsuls: let them accuse one another.
texts.act.19.39: But if ye inquire anything concerning other matters, it will be settled in the regular assembly.
texts.act.19.40: For also we are in danger to be put in accusation for sedition for this [affair] of to-day, no cause existing in reference to which we shall be able to give a reason for this concourse.
texts.act.19.41: And having said these things, he dismissed the assembly.
texts.act.20.1: But after the tumult had ceased, Paul having called the disciples to [him] and embraced [them], went away to go to Macedonia.
texts.act.20.2: And having passed through those parts, and having exhorted them with much discourse, he came to Greece.
texts.act.20.3: And having spent three months [there], a treacherous plot against him having been set on foot by the Jews, as he was going to sail to Syria, [the] resolution was adopted of returning through Macedonia.
texts.act.20.4: And there accompanied him as far as Asia, Sopater [son] of Pyrrhus, a Berean; and of Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius and Timotheus of Derbe, and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
texts.act.20.5: These going before waited for us in Troas;
texts.act.20.6: but we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and we came to them to Troas in five days, where we spent seven days.
texts.act.20.7: And the first day of the week, we being assembled to break bread, Paul discoursed to them, about to depart on the morrow. And he prolonged the discourse till midnight.
texts.act.20.8: And there were many lights in the upper room where we were assembled.
texts.act.20.9: And a certain youth, by name Eutychus, sitting at the window-opening, overpowered by deep sleep, while Paul discoursed very much at length, having been overpowered by the sleep, fell from the third story down to the bottom, and was taken up dead.
texts.act.20.10: But Paul descending fell upon him, and enfolding [him] [in his arms], said, Be not troubled, for his life is in him.
texts.act.20.11: And having gone up, and having broken the bread, and eaten, and having long spoken until daybreak, so he went away.
texts.act.20.12: And they brought [away] the boy alive, and were no little comforted.
texts.act.20.13: And we, having gone before on board ship, sailed off to Assos, going to take in Paul there; for so he had directed, he himself being about to go on foot.
texts.act.20.14: And when he met with us at Assos, having taken him on board, we came to Mitylene;
texts.act.20.15: and having sailed thence, on the morrow arrived opposite Chios, and the next day put in at Samos; and having stayed at Trogyllium, the next day we came to Miletus:
texts.act.20.16: for Paul thought it desirable to sail by Ephesus, so that he might not be made to spend time in Asia; for he hastened, if it was possible for him, to be the day of Pentecost at Jerusalem.
texts.act.20.17: But from Miletus having sent to Ephesus, he called over [to him] the elders of the assembly.
texts.act.20.18: And when they were come to him, he said to them, *Ye* know how I was with you all the time from the first day that I arrived in Asia,
texts.act.20.19: serving the Lord with all lowliness, and tears, and temptations, which happened to me through the plots of the Jews;
texts.act.20.20: how I held back nothing of what is profitable, so as not to announce [it] to you, and to teach you publicly and in every house,
texts.act.20.21: testifying to both Jews and Greeks repentance towards God, and faith towards our Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.act.20.22: And now, behold, bound in my spirit *I* go to Jerusalem, not knowing what things shall happen to me in it;
texts.act.20.23: only that the Holy Spirit testifies to me in every city, saying that bonds and tribulations await me.
texts.act.20.24: But I make no account of [my] life [as] dear to myself, so that I finish my course, and the ministry which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the glad tidings of the grace of God.
texts.act.20.25: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone about preaching the kingdom [of God], shall see my face no more.
texts.act.20.26: Wherefore I witness to you this day, that I am clean from the blood of all,
texts.act.20.27: for I have not shrunk from announcing to you all the counsel of God.
texts.act.20.28: Take heed therefore to yourselves, and to all the flock, wherein the Holy Spirit has set you as overseers, to shepherd the assembly of God, which he has purchased with the blood of his own.
texts.act.20.29: [For] *I* know [this,] that there will come in amongst you after my departure grievous wolves, not sparing the flock;
texts.act.20.30: and from among your own selves shall rise up men speaking perverted things to draw away the disciples after them.
texts.act.20.31: Wherefore watch, remembering that for three years, night and day, I ceased not admonishing each one [of you] with tears.
texts.act.20.32: And now I commit you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build [you] up and give [to you] an inheritance among all the sanctified.
texts.act.20.33: I have coveted [the] silver or gold or clothing of no one.
texts.act.20.34: Yourselves know that these hands have ministered to my wants, and to those who were with me.
texts.act.20.35: I have shewed you all things, that thus labouring [we] ought to come in aid of the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
texts.act.20.36: And having said these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
texts.act.20.37: And they all wept sore; and falling upon the neck of Paul they ardently kissed him,
texts.act.20.38: specially pained by the word which he had said, that they would no more see his face. And they went down with him to the ship.
texts.act.21.1: And when, having got away from them, we at last sailed away, we came by a direct course to Cos, and on the morrow to Rhodes, and thence to Patara.
texts.act.21.2: And having found a ship passing over into Phoenicia, we went on board and sailed;
texts.act.21.3: and having sighted Cyprus, and left it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria, and made the land at Tyre, for there the ship was to discharge her cargo.
texts.act.21.4: And having found out the disciples, we remained there seven days; who said to Paul by the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.
texts.act.21.5: But when we had completed the days, we set out and took our journey, all of them accompanying us, with wives and children, till [we were] out of the city. And kneeling down upon the shore we prayed.
texts.act.21.6: And having embraced one another, we went on board ship, and they returned home.
texts.act.21.7: And we, having completed the voyage, arrived from Tyre at Ptolemais, and having saluted the brethren, we remained one day with them.
texts.act.21.8: And leaving on the morrow, we came to Caesarea; and entering into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was of the seven, we abode with him.
texts.act.21.9: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
texts.act.21.10: And as we stayed there many days, a certain man, by name Agabus, a prophet, came down from Judaea,
texts.act.21.11: and coming to us and taking the girdle of Paul, and having bound his own hands and feet, said, Thus saith the Holy Spirit, The man whose this girdle is shall the Jews thus bind in Jerusalem, and deliver him up into the hands of [the] Gentiles.
texts.act.21.12: And when we heard these things, both we and those of the place besought [him] not to go up to Jerusalem.
texts.act.21.13: But Paul answered, What do ye, weeping and breaking my heart? for *I* am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.21.14: And when he would not be persuaded, we were silent, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
texts.act.21.15: And after these days, having got our effects ready, we went up to Jerusalem.
texts.act.21.16: And [some] of the disciples from Caesarea went with us, bringing [with them] a certain Mnason, a Cyprian, an old disciple, with whom we were to lodge.
texts.act.21.17: And when we arrived at Jerusalem the brethren gladly received us.
texts.act.21.18: And on the morrow Paul went in with us to James, and all the elders came there.
texts.act.21.19: And having saluted them, he related one by one the things which God had wrought among the nations by his ministry.
texts.act.21.20: And they having heard [it] glorified God, and said to him, Thou seest, brother, how many myriads there are of the Jews who have believed, and all are zealous of the law.
texts.act.21.21: And they have been informed concerning thee, that thou teachest all the Jews among the nations apostasy from Moses, saying that they should not circumcise their children, nor walk in the customs.
texts.act.21.22: What is it then? a multitude must necessarily come together, for they will hear that thou art come.
texts.act.21.23: This do therefore that we say to thee: We have four men who have a vow on them;
texts.act.21.24: take these and be purified with them, and pay their expenses, that they may have their heads shaved; and all will know that [of those things] of which they have been informed about thee nothing is [true]; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, keeping the law.
texts.act.21.25: But concerning [those of] the nations who have believed, we have written, deciding that they should [observe no such thing, only to] keep themselves both from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication.
texts.act.21.26: Then Paul, taking the men, on the next day, having been purified, entered with them into the temple, signifying the time the days of the purification would be fulfilled, until the offering was offered for every one of them.
texts.act.21.27: And when the seven days were nearly completed, the Jews from Asia, having seen him in the temple, set all the crowd in a tumult, and laid hands upon him,
texts.act.21.28: crying, Israelites, help! this is the man who teaches all everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place, and has brought Greeks too into the temple, and profaned this holy place.
texts.act.21.29: For they had before seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.
texts.act.21.30: And the whole city was moved, and there was a concourse of the people; and having laid hold on Paul they drew him out of the temple, and immediately the doors were shut.
texts.act.21.31: And as they were seeking to kill him, a representation came to the chiliarch of the band that the whole of Jerusalem was in a tumult;
texts.act.21.32: who, taking with him immediately soldiers and centurions, ran down upon them. But they, seeing the chiliarch and the soldiers, ceased beating Paul.
texts.act.21.33: Then the chiliarch came up and laid hold upon him, and commanded [him] to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he might be, and what he had done.
texts.act.21.34: And different persons cried some different thing in the crowd. But he, not being able to know the certainty on account of the uproar, commanded him to be brought into the fortress.
texts.act.21.35: But when he got upon the stairs it was so that he was borne by the soldiers on account of the violence of the crowd.
texts.act.21.36: For the multitude of the people followed, crying, Away with him.
texts.act.21.37: But as he was about to be led into the fortress, Paul says to the chiliarch, Is it allowed me to say something to thee? And he said, Dost thou know Greek?
texts.act.21.38: Thou art not then that Egyptian who before these days raised a sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the assassins?
texts.act.21.39: But Paul said, *I* am a Jew of Tarsus, citizen of no insignificant city of Cilicia, and I beseech of thee, allow me to speak to the people.
texts.act.21.40: And when he had allowed him, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people; and a great silence having been made, he addressed them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,
texts.act.22.1: Brethren and fathers, hear my defence which I now make to you.
texts.act.22.2: And hearing that he addressed them in the Hebrew tongue, they kept the more quiet; and he says,
texts.act.22.3: *I* am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city, at the feet of Gamaliel, educated according to [the] exactness of the law of [our] fathers, being zealous for God, as *ye* are all this day;
texts.act.22.4: who have persecuted this way unto death, binding and delivering up to prisons both men and women;
texts.act.22.5: as also the high priest bears me witness, and all the elderhood: from whom also, having received letters to the brethren, I went to Damascus to bring those also who were there, bound, to Jerusalem, to be punished.
texts.act.22.6: And it came to pass, as I was journeying and drawing near to Damascus, that, about mid-day, there suddenly shone out of heaven a great light round about me.
texts.act.22.7: And I fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
texts.act.22.8: And *I* answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said to me, *I* am Jesus the Nazaraean, whom *thou* persecutest.
texts.act.22.9: But they that were with me beheld the light, [and were filled with fear], but heard not the voice of him that was speaking to me.
texts.act.22.10: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said to me, Rise up, and go to Damascus, and there it shall be told thee of all things which it is appointed thee to do.
texts.act.22.11: And as I could not see, through the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came to Damascus.
texts.act.22.12: And a certain Ananias, a pious man according to the law, borne witness to by all the Jews who dwelt [there],
texts.act.22.13: coming to me and standing by me, said to me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And *I*, in the same hour, received my sight and saw him.
texts.act.22.14: And he said, The God of our fathers has chosen thee beforehand to know his will, and to see the just one, and to hear a voice out of his mouth;
texts.act.22.15: for thou shalt be a witness for him to all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
texts.act.22.16: And now why lingerest thou? Arise and get baptised, and have thy sins washed away, calling on his name.
texts.act.22.17: And it came to pass when I had returned to Jerusalem, and as I was praying in the temple, that I became in ecstasy,
texts.act.22.18: and saw him saying to me, Make haste and go quickly out of Jerusalem, for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
texts.act.22.19: And *I* said, Lord, they themselves know that *I* was imprisoning and beating in every synagogue those that believe on thee;
texts.act.22.20: and when the blood of thy witness Stephen was shed, I also myself was standing by and consenting, and kept the clothes of them who killed him.
texts.act.22.21: And he said to me, Go, for *I* will send thee to the nations afar off.
texts.act.22.22: And they heard him until this word, and lifted up their voice, saying, Away with such a one as that from the earth, for it was not fit he should live.
texts.act.22.23: And as they were crying, and throwing away their clothes, and casting dust into the air,
texts.act.22.24: the chiliarch commanded him to be brought into the fortress, saying that he should be examined by scourging, that he might ascertain for what cause they cried thus against him.
texts.act.22.25: But as they stretched him forward with the thongs, Paul said to the centurion who stood [by], Is it lawful for you to scourge a man [who is] a Roman and uncondemned?
texts.act.22.26: And the centurion, having heard it, went and reported it to the chiliarch, saying, What art thou going to do? for this man is a Roman.
texts.act.22.27: And the chiliarch coming up said to him, Tell me, Art *thou* a Roman? And he said, Yes.
texts.act.22.28: And the chiliarch answered, *I*, for a great sum, bought this citizenship. And Paul said, But *I* was also [free] born.
texts.act.22.29: Immediately therefore those who were going to examine him left him, and the chiliarch also was afraid when he ascertained that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
texts.act.22.30: And on the morrow, desirous to know the certainty [of the matter] why he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him, and commanded the chief priests and all the council to meet, and having brought Paul down set him before them.
texts.act.23.1: And Paul, fixing his eyes on the council, said, Brethren, I have walked in all good conscience with God unto this day.
texts.act.23.2: But the high priest Ananias ordered those standing by him to smite his mouth.
texts.act.23.3: Then Paul said to him, God will smite thee, whited wall. And *thou*, dost thou sit judging me according to the law, and breaking the law commandest me to be smitten?
texts.act.23.4: And those that stood by said, Dost thou rail against the high priest of God?
texts.act.23.5: And Paul said, I was not conscious, brethren, that he was high priest; for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evilly of the ruler of thy people.
texts.act.23.6: But Paul, knowing that the one part [of them] were of the Sadducees and the other of the Pharisees, cried out in the council, Brethren, *I* am a Pharisee, son of Pharisees: *I* am judged concerning the hope and resurrection of [the] dead.
texts.act.23.7: And when he had spoken this, there was a tumult of the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the multitude was divided.
texts.act.23.8: For Sadducees say there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but Pharisees confess both of them.
texts.act.23.9: And there was a great clamour, and the scribes of the Pharisees' part rising up contended, saying, We find nothing evil in this man; and if a spirit has spoken to him, or an angel ...
texts.act.23.10: And a great tumult having arisen, the chiliarch, fearing lest Paul should have been torn in pieces by them, commanded the troop to come down and take him by force from the midst of them, and to bring [him] into the fortress.
texts.act.23.11: But the following night the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good courage; for as thou hast testified the things concerning me at Jerusalem, so thou must bear witness at Rome also.
texts.act.23.12: And when it was day, the Jews, having banded together, put themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they should kill Paul.
texts.act.23.13: And they were more than forty who had joined together in this oath;
texts.act.23.14: and they went to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have cursed ourselves with a curse to taste nothing until we kill Paul.
texts.act.23.15: Now therefore do ye with the council make a representation to the chiliarch so that he may bring him down to you, as about to determine more precisely what concerns him, and we, before he draws near, are ready to kill him.
texts.act.23.16: But Paul's sister's son, having heard of the lying in wait, came and entered into the fortress and reported [it] to Paul.
texts.act.23.17: And Paul, having called one of the centurions, said, Take this youth to the chiliarch, for he has something to report to him.
texts.act.23.18: He therefore, having taken him with [him], led him to the chiliarch, and says, The prisoner Paul called me to [him] and asked me to lead this youth to thee, who has something to say to thee.
texts.act.23.19: And the chiliarch having taken him by the hand, and having gone apart in private, inquired, What is it that thou hast to report to me?
texts.act.23.20: And he said, The Jews have agreed together to make a request to thee, that thou mayest bring Paul down to-morrow into the council, as about to inquire something more precise concerning him.
texts.act.23.21: Do not thou then be persuaded by them, for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, who have put themselves under a curse neither to eat nor drink till they kill him; and now they are ready waiting the promise from thee.
texts.act.23.22: The chiliarch then dismissed the youth, commanding [him], Utter to no one that thou hast represented these things to me.
texts.act.23.23: And having called to [him] certain two of the centurions, he said, Prepare two hundred soldiers that they may go as far as Caesarea, and seventy horsemen, and two hundred light-armed footmen, for the third hour of the night.
texts.act.23.24: And [he ordered them] to provide beasts, that they might set Paul on them and carry [him] safe through to Felix the governor,
texts.act.23.25: having written a letter, couched in this form:
texts.act.23.26: Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix, greeting.
texts.act.23.27: This man, having been taken by the Jews, and being about to be killed by them, I came up with the military and took out [of their hands], having learned that he was a Roman.
texts.act.23.28: And desiring to know the charge on which they accused him, I brought him down to their council;
texts.act.23.29: whom I found to be accused of questions of their law, but to have no charge laid against him [making him] worthy of death or of bonds.
texts.act.23.30: But having received information of a plot about to be put in execution against the man [by the Jews], I have immediately sent him to thee, commanding also his accusers to say before thee the things that are against him. [Farewell.]
texts.act.23.31: The soldiers therefore, according to what was ordered them, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris,
texts.act.23.32: and on the morrow, having left the horsemen to go with him, returned to the fortress.
texts.act.23.33: And these, having entered into Caesarea, and given up the letter to the governor, presented Paul also to him.
texts.act.23.34: And having read [it], and asked of what eparchy he was, and learned that [he was] of Cilicia,
texts.act.23.35: he said, I will hear thee fully when thine accusers also are arrived. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's praetorium.
texts.act.24.1: And after five days came down the high priest Ananias, with the elders, and a certain orator called Tertullus, and laid their informations against Paul before the governor.
texts.act.24.2: And he having been called, Tertullus began to accuse, saying, Seeing we enjoy great peace through thee, and that excellent measures are executed for this nation by thy forethought,
texts.act.24.3: we receive [it] always and everywhere, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
texts.act.24.4: But that I may not too much intrude on thy time, I beseech thee to hear us briefly in thy kindness.
texts.act.24.5: For finding this man a pest, and moving sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a leader of the sect of the Nazaraeans;
texts.act.24.6: who also attempted to profane the temple; whom we also had seized, [and would have judged according to our law;
texts.act.24.7: but Lysias, the chiliarch, coming up, took [him] away with great force out of our hands,
texts.act.24.8: having commanded his accusers to come to thee;] of whom thou canst thyself, in examining [him], know the certainty of all these things of which we accuse him.
texts.act.24.9: And the Jews also joined in pressing the matter against [Paul], saying that these things were so.
texts.act.24.10: But Paul, the governor having beckoned to him to speak, answered, Knowing that for many years thou hast been judge to this nation, I answer readily as to the things which concern myself.
texts.act.24.11: As thou mayest know that there are not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem,
texts.act.24.12: and neither in the temple did they find me discoursing to any one, or making any tumultuous gathering together of the crowd, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city;
texts.act.24.13: neither can they make good the things of which they now accuse me.
texts.act.24.14: But this I avow to thee, that in the way which they call sect, so I serve my fathers' God, believing all things which are written throughout the law, and in the prophets;
texts.act.24.15: having hope towards God, which they themselves also receive, that there is to be a resurrection both of just and unjust.
texts.act.24.16: For this cause I also exercise [myself] to have in everything a conscience without offence towards God and men.
texts.act.24.17: And after a lapse of many years I arrived, bringing alms to my nation, and offerings.
texts.act.24.18: Whereupon they found me purified in the temple, with neither crowd nor tumult. But it was certain Jews from Asia,
texts.act.24.19: who ought to appear before thee and accuse, if they have anything against me;
texts.act.24.20: or let these themselves say what wrong they found in me when I stood before the council,
texts.act.24.21: [other] than concerning this one voice which I cried standing amongst them: I am judged this day by you touching [the] resurrection of [the] dead.
texts.act.24.22: And Felix, knowing accurately the things concerning the way, adjourned them, saying, When Lysias the chiliarch is come down I will determine your affair;
texts.act.24.23: ordering the centurion to keep him, and that he should have freedom, and to hinder none of his friends to minister to him.
texts.act.24.24: And after certain days, Felix having arrived with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jewess, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
texts.act.24.25: And as he reasoned concerning righteousness, and temperance, and the judgment about to come, Felix, being filled with fear, answered, Go for the present, and when I get an opportunity I will send for thee;
texts.act.24.26: hoping at the same time that money would be given him by Paul: wherefore also he sent for him the oftener and communed with him.
texts.act.24.27: But when two years were completed, Felix was relieved by Porcius Festus as his successor; and Felix, desirous to oblige the Jews, to acquire their favour, left Paul bound.
texts.act.25.1: Festus therefore, being come into the eparchy, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
texts.act.25.2: And the chief priests and the chief of the Jews laid informations before him against Paul, and besought him,
texts.act.25.3: asking as a grace against him that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying people in wait to kill him on the way.
texts.act.25.4: Festus therefore answered that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to set out shortly.
texts.act.25.5: Let therefore the persons of authority among you, says he, going down too, if there be anything in this man, accuse him.
texts.act.25.6: And having remained among them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea; and on the next day, having sat down on the judgment-seat, commanded Paul to be brought.
texts.act.25.7: And when he was come, the Jews who were come down from Jerusalem stood round, bringing many and grievous charges which they were not able to prove:
texts.act.25.8: Paul answering for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I offended [in] anything.
texts.act.25.9: But Festus, desirous of obliging the Jews, to acquire their favour, answering Paul, said, Art thou willing to go up to Jerusalem, there to be judged before me concerning these things?
texts.act.25.10: But Paul said, I am standing before the judgment-seat of Caesar, where I ought to be judged. To the Jews have I done no wrong, as *thou* also very well knowest.
texts.act.25.11: If then I have done any wrong and committed anything worthy of death, I do not deprecate dying; but if there is nothing of those things of which they accuse me, no man can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar.
texts.act.25.12: Then Festus, having conferred with the council, answered, Thou hast appealed to Caesar. To Caesar shalt thou go.
texts.act.25.13: And when certain days had elapsed, Agrippa the king and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to salute Festus.
texts.act.25.14: And when they had spent many days there, Festus laid before the king the matters relating to Paul, saying, There is a certain man left prisoner by Felix,
texts.act.25.15: concerning whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews laid informations, requiring judgment against him:
texts.act.25.16: to whom I answered, It is not [the] custom of the Romans to give up any man before that the accused have the accusers face to face, and he have got opportunity of defence touching the charge.
texts.act.25.17: When therefore they had come together here, without putting it off, I sat the next day on the judgment-seat and commanded the man to be brought:
texts.act.25.18: concerning whom the accusers, standing up, brought no such accusation of guilt as *I* supposed;
texts.act.25.19: but had against him certain questions of their own system of worship, and concerning a certain Jesus who is dead, whom Paul affirmed to be living.
texts.act.25.20: And as I myself was at a loss as to an inquiry into these things, I said, Was he willing to go to Jerusalem and there to be judged concerning these things?
texts.act.25.21: But Paul having appealed to be kept for the cognisance of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I shall send him to Caesar.
texts.act.25.22: And Agrippa [said] to Festus, I myself also would desire to hear the man. To-morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.
texts.act.25.23: On the morrow therefore, Agrippa being come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and having entered into the hall of audience, with the chiliarchs and the men of distinction of the city, and Festus having given command, Paul was brought.
texts.act.25.24: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, ye see this person, concerning whom all the multitude of the Jews applied to me both in Jerusalem and here, crying out against [him] that he ought not to live any longer.
texts.act.25.25: But I, having found that he had done nothing worthy of death, and this [man] himself having appealed to Augustus, I have decided to send him;
texts.act.25.26: concerning whom I have nothing certain to write to my lord. Wherefore I have brought him before you, and specially before thee, king Agrippa, so that an examination having been gone into I may have something to write:
texts.act.25.27: for it seems to me senseless, sending a prisoner, not also to signify the charges against him.
texts.act.26.1: And Agrippa said to Paul, It is permitted thee to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretching out his hand answered in his defence:
texts.act.26.2: I count myself happy, king Agrippa, in having to answer to-day before thee concerning all of which I am accused by the Jews,
texts.act.26.3: especially because thou art acquainted with all the customs and questions which are among the Jews; wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
texts.act.26.4: My manner of life then from my youth, which from its commencement was passed among my nation in Jerusalem, know all the Jews,
texts.act.26.5: who knew me before from the outset [of my life], if they would bear witness, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
texts.act.26.6: And now I stand to be judged because of the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,
texts.act.26.7: to which our whole twelve tribes serving incessantly day and night hope to arrive; about which hope, O king, I am accused of [the] Jews.
texts.act.26.8: Why should it be judged a thing incredible in your sight if God raises the dead?
texts.act.26.9: *I* indeed myself thought that I ought to do much against the name of Jesus the Nazaraean.
texts.act.26.10: Which also I did in Jerusalem, and myself shut up in prisons many of the saints, having received the authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death I gave my vote.
texts.act.26.11: And often punishing them in all the synagogues, I compelled them to blaspheme. And, being exceedingly furious against them, I persecuted them even to cities out [of our own land].
texts.act.26.12: And when, [engaged] in this, I was journeying to Damascus, with authority and power from the chief priests,
texts.act.26.13: at mid-day, on the way, I saw, O king, a light above the brightness of the sun, shining from heaven round about me and those who were journeying with me.
texts.act.26.14: And, when we were all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? [it is] hard for thee to kick against goads.
texts.act.26.15: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, *I* am Jesus whom *thou* persecutest:
texts.act.26.16: but rise up and stand on thy feet; for, for this purpose have I appeared to thee, to appoint thee to be a servant and a witness both of what thou hast seen, and of what I shall appear to thee in,
texts.act.26.17: taking thee out from among the people, and the nations, to whom *I* send thee,
