texts.act.3.16: And, by the faith of his name, unto this man whom ye see and know, hath his name given strength,—yea, the faith which is through him, hath given unto him this perfect soundness, over against you all!
texts.act.3.17: And now brethren, I know that by way of ignorance ye acted,—just as even your rulers.
texts.act.3.18: Howbeit, God—what things he had before declared, through the mouth of all the prophets, for his Christ to suffer,—did thus fulfill!
texts.act.3.19: Repent ye, therefore, and turn,—unto the blotting out of your sins; to the end that in that case, there may come seasons of refreshing from the face of the Lord,
texts.act.3.20: And he may send forth him who had been fore-appointed for you—Christ Jesus:
texts.act.3.21: Unto whom, indeed, heaven must needs give welcome, until the times of the due establishment of all things, of which God hath spoken through the mouth of his holy age-past prophets.
texts.act.3.22: Moses, indeed, said—A prophet, unto you, shall the Lord God raise up among your brethren, like unto me: unto him, shall ye hearken respecting all things whatsoever he shall speak unto you.
texts.act.3.23: And it shall be—every soul, whatsoever, which shall not hearken unto that prophet, shall be utterly destroyed from among the people.
texts.act.3.24: But, indeed, all the prophets,—from Samuel and those following after, as many as have spoken, have even announced these days.
texts.act.3.25: Ye, are the sons of the prophets, and of the covenant which God covenanted unto your fathers, saying unto Abraham—And, in thy seed, shall be blessed, all the families of the ground.
texts.act.3.26: Unto you first, God—having raised up his Servant—hath sent him forth, ready to bless you, when ye are turning away, each one, from your wickednesses.
texts.act.4.1: But, as they were speaking unto the people, the High-priests and the Captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
texts.act.4.2: Being tired out because of their teaching the people, and announcing, in Jesus, the resurrection from among the dead;
texts.act.4.3: And they thrust on them their hands, and put them in custody for the morrow, for it was evening, already.
texts.act.4.4: Howbeit, many of them that heard the word, believed; and the number of the men became about five thousand.
texts.act.4.5: And it came to pass, upon the morrow, that there were gathered together of them, the rulers and the elders and the scribes, in Jerusalem;
texts.act.4.6: Also Annas, the high-priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of high-priestly descent;—
texts.act.4.7: And, setting them in the midst, they began to enquire—In what manner of power, or in what manner of name, did, ye, do this?
texts.act.4.8: Then Peter, filled with Holy Spirit, said unto them—Ye rulers of the people, and elders!
texts.act.4.9: If, we, this day, are to be examined for doing good to a sick man,—in whom, this, man hath been made well,
texts.act.4.10: Be it known unto you all, and unto all the people of Israel: that, in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene,—whom, ye, crucified, whom, God, raised from among the dead, in him, doth, this man stand by, in your presence, whole.
texts.act.4.11: This, is the stone, set at nought by you the builders, which became the head of the corner;
texts.act.4.12: And there is in no one else, salvation, for, neither is there any other name, under heaven, which hath been set forth among men, in which we must needs be saved.
texts.act.4.13: And, looking at Peter’s boldness of speech, and John’s, and having discovered that they were unlettered and obscure men, they began to marvel, recognising them also, that they had been with Jesus;
texts.act.4.14: Seeing, the man also standing, with them, even the [man] who had been cured, they had nothing wherewith to contradict.
texts.act.4.15: Howbeit, ordering them to go forth outside the high-council, they began to confer one with another,
texts.act.4.16: Saying—What are we to do with these men? For, indeed, that a notable sign hath come to pass through their means, unto all who are dwelling in Jerusalem, is manifest, and we cannot deny [it]!
texts.act.4.17: Nevertheless, lest it further spread abroad among the people, let us charge them with threats, to be no more speaking upon this name, to any soul of man.
texts.act.4.18: And, calling them, they gave them the sweeping charge,—not to be sounding aloud, nor even to be teaching, upon the name of Jesus.
texts.act.4.19: But, Peter and John, answering, said unto them—Whether it be right in presence of God, unto you, to be hearkening, rather than unto God, judge!
texts.act.4.20: For, we, cannot but be speaking the things which we have seen and heard.
texts.act.4.21: They, however, further charging them with threats, let them go, finding nothing as to how they might chastise them, on account of the people; because, all, were glorifying God for that which had come to pass;—
texts.act.4.22: For, more than forty years old, was the man, upon whom had taken place, this healing sign.
texts.act.4.23: But, when they had been let go, they came unto their own [friends], and told as many things as, unto them, the High-priests and Elders, had said.
texts.act.4.24: And, they, having heard, with one accord, uplifted voice unto God, and said—O Sovereign! Thou, art he that made the heaven, and the earth, and the sea, and all things that are herein:
texts.act.4.25: Who, by our father, through means of the Holy Spirit, even by the mouth of David thy servant, said—Unto what end did nations rage, and, peoples, busy themselves with empty things?
texts.act.4.26: The kings of the earth stationed themselves, and, the rulers, were gathered together, with one intent, against the Lord, and against his Christ.
texts.act.4.27: For they were gathered together, of a truth, in this city, against thy holy servant Jesus, whom thou hadst anointed,—both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with them of the nations, and peoples of Israel;—
texts.act.4.28: To do whatsoever, thy hand and thy counsel, marked out beforehand to come to pass.
texts.act.4.29: As to the present things, then, O Lord,—look upon their threats, and grant unto thy servants, with all freedom of utterance, to be speaking thy word,
texts.act.4.30: By stretching forth thy hand for healing, and by the coming to pass of both signs and wonders, through the name of thy holy servant Jesus.
texts.act.4.31: And, when they had made supplication, the place was shaken in which they were gathered together, and they were filled, one and all, with the Holy Spirit, and began speaking the word of God with freedom of utterance.
texts.act.4.32: And, the throng of them that believed, had one heart and soul, and not so much as one was saying that, aught of his goods, was, his own, but they had all things common.
texts.act.4.33: And, with great power, were the apostles giving forth their witness of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus; great favour also was upon them all.
texts.act.4.34: For there was not so much as anyone, lacking, among them; for, as many as were possessors of lands or houses, selling them, were bringing the prices of the things that were being sold,
texts.act.4.35: And laying them at the feet of the Apostles, while on the other hand they were distributing unto each one, in so far as any one had, need.
texts.act.4.36: And, Joseph, who had been surnamed Barnabas by the Apostles, which is to be translated Son of Exhortation,—a Levite, a Cyprian by nation,
texts.act.4.37: Having a field, sold it, and brought the money and laid it at the feet of the Apostles.
texts.act.5.1: But, a certain man, Ananias by name, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession,
texts.act.5.2: And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it; and, bringing a certain part, at the feet of the Apostles, he laid it.
texts.act.5.3: But Peter said—Ananias! wherefore did Satan fill thy heart, that thou shouldst deal falsely with the Holy Spirit, and keep back part of the price of the field?
texts.act.5.4: While it remained, was it not, as thine own, it remained? and, when sold, was it not, in thine own authority, that it still continued? Why was it that thou didst contrive in thy heart this deed? Thou hast not dealt falsely with men but, with God.
texts.act.5.5: And, as Ananias heard these words, he fell, and expired. And there came great fear upon all that heard;
texts.act.5.6: But the young men, rising up, wrapped him about, and, bearing him forth, buried him.
texts.act.5.7: And it came to pass, after about three hours interval, that his wife, not knowing what had happened, came in.
texts.act.5.8: And Peter began to say unto her—Tell me! was it, for so much, ye gave up the field? And she said—Yea! for so much.
texts.act.5.9: And, Peter, [said] unto her—Why was it agreed by you to put to the proof the Spirit of the Lord? Lo! the feet of them that have buried thy husband, are at the door, and they shall bear thee forth.
texts.act.5.10: And she fell instantly at his feet, and expired. And the young men, coming in, found her dead; and, bearing her forth, they buried her with her husband.
texts.act.5.11: And there came great fear upon the whole assembly, and upon all them that heard these things.
texts.act.5.12: And, through the hands of the Apostles, were coming to pass many signs and wonders among the people; and they were all with one accord in the portico of Solomon;
texts.act.5.13: Howbeit, of the rest, no one, durst join himself unto them,—nevertheless the people continued to magnify them;
texts.act.5.14: And, the more, were being added, when they believed in the Lord, throngs both of men and women;—
texts.act.5.15: So that, even into the broad-ways, were they bringing forth the sick, and laying them on small couches and beds, in order that, if Peter were coming along, even perchance his shadow, might overshadow some one of them.
texts.act.5.16: Moreover even the throng of the cities all round Jerusalem was coming together, bearing sick folk, and such as were harassed by impure spirits,—who, indeed, were being cured, one and all.
texts.act.5.17: But the High-priest, arising, and all who were with him,—being the sect of the Sadducees,—were filled with jealousy,
texts.act.5.18: And thrust their hands upon the Apostles, and put them in a public ward.
texts.act.5.19: But, a messenger of the Lord, by night, opened the doors of the prison; and, leading them out, said—
texts.act.5.20: Be going your way, and, taking your stand, be speaking, in the temple, unto the people, all the declarations of this Life.
texts.act.5.21: Now, when they heard this, they entered, under the dawn, into the temple, and began teaching. And the High-priest and they who were with him, arriving, called together the high-council, and all the senate of the sons of Israel; and sent off unto the prison, to have them brought.
texts.act.5.22: And, the officers who came to the place, found them not in the prison; and, returning, brought tidings,
texts.act.5.23: Saying—The prison, found we locked with all safety, and the keepers standing at the doors; but, when we had opened the prison, inside, found we, no one.
texts.act.5.24: Now, when both the captain of the temple and the High-priests heard these words, they were utterly at a loss concerning them—what perhaps this might come to.
texts.act.5.25: But some one, entering, brought tidings unto them—Lo! the men whom ye put in the prison, are in the temple, standing, and teaching the people!
texts.act.5.26: Then, the captain with the officers, departing, brought them—not with violence,—for they were afraid of the people, lest they should be stoned;
texts.act.5.27: But, leading them in, set them in the high- council. And the High-priest questioned them,
texts.act.5.28: Saying—Strictly, did we charge you not to be teaching upon this name; and lo! ye have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and are minded to bring down upon us, the blood of this man.
texts.act.5.29: But Peter and the Apostles, answering, said—It is needful to be yielding obedience unto God rather than unto men:—
texts.act.5.30: The God of our fathers, hath raised up Jesus,—whom, ye, got into your hands, suspending him upon a tree:—
texts.act.5.31: Him, as Princely-leader and Saviour, hath God exalted unto his right hand,—to give repentance unto Israel, and remission of sins.
texts.act.5.32: And, we, are witnesses of these things,—also the Holy Spirit, which God hath given unto them who are yielding obedience unto him.
texts.act.5.33: And, they, when they heard this, were cut to the heart, and were making up their minds to slay them.
texts.act.5.34: But a certain man, rising up in the high-council, by name Gamaliel, a law-teacher honoured by all the people, gave orders to put the men, outside, for a little,—
texts.act.5.35: And said unto them—Men of Israel! be taking heed unto yourselves, what ye are about to inflict upon these men.
texts.act.5.36: For, before these days, there rose up one Theudas, affirming, himself, to be somebody,—unto whom was inclined a number of men, about four hundred; who was slain, and, all as many as had been trusting in him, were disbanded, and came to nothing.
texts.act.5.37: After him, rose up Judas the Galilaean, in the days of the enrolling, and drew a people into revolt after him; and, he, perished, and, all, as many as had trusted in him, were scattered.
texts.act.5.38: Now, therefore, I say unto you—stand aloof from these men, and let them alone; because if, of men, be this project or this work, it will be overthrown,—
texts.act.5.39: But, if it is, of God, ye will not be able to overthrow them: lest once, even fighters against God, ye be found.
texts.act.5.40: And they were persuaded by him; and, calling unto them the Apostles, they, with beating, charged them not be speaking upon the name of Jesus; and let them go.
texts.act.5.41: They, therefore, went rejoicing from the presence of the high-council; in that they had been accounted worthy, in behalf of The Name, to suffer dishonour.
texts.act.5.42: And, every day in the temple, and at home, they ceased not to be teaching, and telling the good news as to the Anointed Jesus.
texts.act.6.1: But, in these days, the disciples, multiplying, there arose a murmuring of the Grecian Jews against the Hebrews, in that, their widows, were being overlooked in the daily ministry.
texts.act.6.2: And the Twelve, calling near the throng of the disciples, said—It doth not seem, right, that, we, forsaking the word of God, should be ministering unto tables.
texts.act.6.3: But look out for yourselves, brethren, seven men from among you, who can be well-attested, full of Spirit and wisdom,—whom we will appoint over this need;
texts.act.6.4: But, we, unto prayer and unto the ministry of the word, will give constant attention.
texts.act.6.5: And the word was pleasing in the sight of all the throng; and they selected Stephen, a man full of faith and Holy Spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicholaus, a proselyte of Antioch;
texts.act.6.6: Whom they set before the Apostles, and, praying, they laid upon them their hands.
texts.act.6.7: And, the word of God, went on growing, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem continued to multiply exceedingly; a great multitude of the priests also, were becoming obedient unto the faith.
texts.act.6.8: Now, Stephen, full of favour and power, began to do great wonders and signs among the people.
texts.act.6.9: But there rose up certain of those out of the synagogue which is called [the synagogue] of them of Libertium and Cyrene and Alexandria, and certain of them from Cilicia and Asia,—disputing with Stephen;
texts.act.6.10: And they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he was speaking,
texts.act.6.11: Then, they set on men who were saying—We have heard him speaking profane things against Moses and God.
texts.act.6.12: And they stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes; and, coming upon him, they caught him away, and led him into the high-council.
texts.act.6.13: And they set up false witnesses, who said—This man, ceaseth not speaking things against this holy place and the law;
texts.act.6.14: For we have heard him saying—This Jesus the Nazarene, will overthrow this place, and will change the customs which, Moses, delivered unto us.
texts.act.6.15: And, looking steadfastly at him, all they who were sitting in the high-council, saw his face, as if the face of a messenger;
texts.act.7.1: And the High-priest said—Are these things, so?
texts.act.7.2: And, he, said—Brethren and fathers, hearken! The God of Glory, appeared unto our father Abraham, while he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Haran,—
texts.act.7.3: And said unto him—Get thee forth, out of thy land, and from among thy kindred, and come unto the land which, unto thee, I will point out.
texts.act.7.4: Then, coming forth out of the land of the Chaldeans, he dwelt in Haran; and, from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land, in which, ye, now dwell;
texts.act.7.5: And gave him no inheritance therein, not even a place to set his foot on; and yet promised to give it unto him in possession, and unto his seed after him, when as yet he had not a child.
texts.act.7.6: But God, spake thus—His seed shall be a sojourner in a foreign land, and they will bring it into bondage, and ill-treat it four-hundred years;
texts.act.7.7: And, the nation unto which they shall be in bondage, will, I, judge—said God; and, after these things, shall they come forth, and render divine service unto me, in this place.
texts.act.7.8: And he gave unto him a covenant of circumcision; and, thus, he begat Isaac, and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac, Jacob, and Jacob, the twelve patriarchs.
texts.act.7.9: And, the patriarchs, being jealous of Joseph, gave him up into Egypt; and, God, was, with him,
texts.act.7.10: And rescued him out of all his tribulations, and gave him favour and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he appointed him governor over Egypt and all his house.
texts.act.7.11: And there came a famine upon all Egypt and Canaan, and great tribulation, and our fathers could not find pasture.
texts.act.7.12: But Jacob, hearing there was corn in Egypt, sent off our fathers, first;
texts.act.7.13: And, the second time, Joseph was made known unto his brethren, and, the race of Joseph was made, manifest, unto Pharaoh.
texts.act.7.14: And Joseph, sending forth, called for Jacob his father, and all the kindred, consisting of seventy-five souls;
texts.act.7.15: And Jacob went down [into Egypt]. And he died, he, and our fathers;
texts.act.7.16: And were brought over into Shechem, and laid in the tomb which Abraham had purchased, for a price of silver, of the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
texts.act.7.17: Now, just as the time of the promise was drawing near wherewith God had agreed with Abraham, the people grew, and were multiplied in Egypt,—
texts.act.7.18: Until there arose another sort of king over Egypt, who had not known Joseph.
texts.act.7.19: The same, dealing craftily with our race, ill-treated our fathers, so as to cause their babes to be exposed, to the end they might not be suffered to live.
texts.act.7.20: In which season, Moses, was born, and was exceeding goodly,—who was nourished up three months in the house of his father;
texts.act.7.21: But, when he was exposed, the daughter of Pharaoh rescued him, and nourished him for herself, as a son.
texts.act.7.22: And, so Moses was trained in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in his words and works.
texts.act.7.23: And, when there was being fulfilled unto him a period of forty years, it came up on his heart to look after his brethren the sons of Israel;
texts.act.7.24: And, seeing one being wronged, he defended him, and avenged him that was getting worn out, smiting the Egyptian.
texts.act.7.25: But he supposed his brethren would understand that, God, through his hand, would give them deliverance; whereas they understood not.
texts.act.7.26: On the following day also, he appeared unto them, as they were contending, and would have reconciled them in peace, saying—Men! ye are, brothers! Wherefore wrong ye one another?
texts.act.7.27: But, he that was wronging his neighbour, thrust him away, saying—Who hath appointed, thee, to be ruler and judge over us?
texts.act.7.28: Art, thou, wishing, to kill me, in the same way thou didst kill, yesterday, the Egyptian?
texts.act.7.29: And Moses fled at this saying, and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, where he begat two sons.
texts.act.7.30: And, when forty years were fulfilled, there appeared unto him, in the desert of Mount Sinai, a messenger, in a flame of fire, in a bush.
texts.act.7.31: And, Moses, seeing it, marvelled at the sight; and, as he was going near to observe, there came a voice of the Lord—
texts.act.7.32: I, am the God of thy fathers, The God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. And Moses becoming, terrified, durst not observe.
texts.act.7.33: And the Lord said unto him—Loose the sandals of thy feet; for, the place whereon thou art standing, is, hallowed ground.
texts.act.7.34: I have, indeed seen, the ill-treatment of my people that is in Egypt, and, unto their groaning, have I hearkened, and have come down to rescue them. Now, therefore, come! I will send thee into Egypt.
texts.act.7.35: The same Moses whom they had refused, saying—Who hath appointed thee to be ruler and judge? the same, both as ruler and redeemer, did God send, by the hand of the messenger who had appeared unto him in the bush:
texts.act.7.36: The same, led them forth, doing wonders and signs in Egypt, and in the Red Sea, and in the desert, forty years:
texts.act.7.37: The same, is the Moses that said unto the sons of Israel—A prophet, unto you, will God raise up, from among your brethren, like unto me:
texts.act.7.38: The same, is he that came to be in the assembly in the desert, with the messenger who was speaking with him in Mount Sinai, and with our fathers, he who welcomed living utterances, to give unto us:
texts.act.7.39: Unto whom, our fathers would not become obedient, but thrust him away, and turned in their hearts unto Egypt,
texts.act.7.40: Saying unto Aaron—Make as gods who shall go before us; for, as for this Moses who brought us forth out of Egypt, we know not what hath befallen him!
texts.act.7.41: And so they fell to calf-making in those days, and offered sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their hands.
texts.act.7.42: But God, turned, and delivered them up to be doing divine service unto the host of heaven,—just as it is written in a book of the prophets—Victims and sacrifices did ye offer unto me, forty years in the desert, O house of Israel?
texts.act.7.43: Nay! but ye took with you the tent of Moloch, and the star of the god Rephan,—the forms which ye made to bow down unto them: therefore will I carry you away beyond Babylon.
texts.act.7.44: The tent of witness, was with our fathers in the desert, according as he who was speaking unto Moses, gave instructions, to make it, according to the model which he had seen.
texts.act.7.45: Which our fathers succeeding to, also brought in, with Joshua, when taking possession of the nations, which God put out from before our fathers until the days of David;
texts.act.7.46: Who found favour before God, and asked to find a habitation for the God of Jacob.
texts.act.7.47: But, Solomon, built him a house.
texts.act.7.48: Although indeed, the Most High, not in hand-made places, dwelleth; just as, the prophet, saith—
texts.act.7.49: Heaven is my thrown, and, the earth, is my footstool: What manner of house, will ye build me, saith the Lord,—Or what shall be the place of my resting?
texts.act.7.50: Hath not, my hand, made all these things?
texts.act.7.51: Ye stiff-necked and uncircumcised in hearts and in ears, ye, always, against the Holy Spirit, do strive! As your fathers, ye also:
texts.act.7.52: Which of the prophets, did not your fathers persecute? Yea they slew them who declared beforehand concerning the coming of the Righteous One—of whom, now, ye, have become, betrayers and murderers!
texts.act.7.53: Who, indeed, received the law through ranks of messengers,—and guarded it not.
texts.act.7.54: And, while they were hearing these things, they were being pierced in their hearts, and began gnashing their teeth against him.
texts.act.7.55: But he, being already full of Holy Spirit, looking steadfastly into heaven, saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God;
texts.act.7.56: And said—Lo! I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man, standing, on the right hand of God.
texts.act.7.57: And, crying out with a loud voice, they held their ears, and rushed with one accord upon him;
texts.act.7.58: And, thrusting him forth outside the city, proceeded to stone him. And, the witnesses, laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
texts.act.7.59: And they stoned Stephen, as he was invoking and saying—Lord Jesus! give welcome unto my spirit.
texts.act.7.60: And, kneeling down, he cried out with a loud voice—Lord! do not charge against them, this sin. And, having said this, he fell asleep.
texts.act.8.1: And, Saul, was taking pleasure with them in his death. Moreover there arose, in that day, a great persecution against the assembly which was in Jerusalem; [and], all, were scattered abroad throughout the countries of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles.
texts.act.8.2: Howbeit reverent men assisted at the burial of Stephen, and made great lamentation over him.
texts.act.8.3: But, Saul, went on to lay waste the assembly, along the houses, going in, and, dragging off both men and women, was
texts.act.8.4: They, indeed, therefore, who were scattered abroad, passed through, telling the good-news of the word;
texts.act.8.5: And, Philip, going down unto the city of Samaria, proclaimed unto them the Christ.
texts.act.8.6: And the multitudes began to give heed unto the things that were being spoken by Philip, with one accord, when they heard him, and saw the signs which he was working.
texts.act.8.7: For, from many who had impure spirits, shouting with a loud voice, they were going out, and, many that were paralysed and lame, were cured.
texts.act.8.8: And there came to be great joy in that city.
texts.act.8.9: But, a certain man named Simon, was already in the city, practising magical arts, and astonishing the nation of Samaria,—saying that himself was someone great:
texts.act.8.10: Unto whom all were giving heed, from small even to great, saying—This, is the Power of God, which is called Great.
texts.act.8.11: And they were giving heed to him, because that, for a considerable time, with his magical arts, he had astonished them.
texts.act.8.12: But, when they believed Philip telling the good news concerning the kingdom of God, and the name of Jesus Christ, they proceeded to be immersed, both men and women.
texts.act.8.13: And, Simon himself also, believed; and, having been immersed, was in constant attendance on Philip,—and, beholding signs and great works of power coming to pass, was astonished.
texts.act.8.14: And the Apostles who were in Jerusalem, hearing that Samaria had welcomed the word of God, sent out unto them Peter and John;
texts.act.8.15: Who, indeed, going down, prayed for them, that they might receive Holy Spirit;—
texts.act.8.16: For, not yet, had it, upon any one of them, fallen, but, only, to begin with, they had been immersed into the name of the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.8.17: Then, proceeded they to lay their hands upon them, and they were receiving Holy Spirit.
texts.act.8.18: But Simon, seeing that, through means of the laying on of the hands of the Apostles, the Spirit was being given, offered unto them money,
texts.act.8.19: Saying—Give unto me also this authority,—in order that, on whomsoever may lay my hands, he may receive Holy Spirit.
texts.act.8.20: And Peter said unto him—Thy silver, with thee, go to destruction! Because, the free-gift of God, thou didst suppose could, with money, be obtained!
texts.act.8.21: Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter; for, thy heart, is not upright before God.
texts.act.8.22: Repent, therefore, from this thy baseness, and entreat of the Lord—whether, after all, the purpose of thy heart shall be forgiven thee;
texts.act.8.23: For see that thou servest as a gall-root of bitterness, and a bond of unrighteousness.
texts.act.8.24: And Simon, answering, said—Entreat ye, in my behalf, unto the Lord; that, nothing, may come upon me, of the things whereof ye have spoken!
texts.act.8.25: They, therefore, having fully borne witness, and spoken the word of the Lord, began their return unto Jerusalem, and, unto many villages of the Samaritans, were they telling the glad tidings.
texts.act.8.26: And, a messenger of the Lord, spake unto Philip, saying—Arise, and be journeying along southward, unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza,—the same, is desert.
texts.act.8.27: And, arising, he journeyed. And lo! a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch, one in power under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure [who] had come to worship in Jerusalem;
texts.act.8.28: And was returning, and, sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.
texts.act.8.29: And the Spirit said unto Philip—Go near, and join thyself unto this chariot!
texts.act.8.30: And, running near, Philip heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said—Dost thou, then, understand what thou art reading?
texts.act.8.31: And, he, said—How indeed should be able—unless someone shall guide me? And he called upon Philip, to come up and sit with him.
texts.act.8.32: Now, the passage of Scripture which he was reading, was, this:—As a sheep, unto slaughter, was he led, and, as a lamb, before him that sheareth it, is dumb, so, he openeth not his mouth.
texts.act.8.33: In his humiliation, his judgment was taken away,—his generation, who shall describe? because, his life, is taken away from the earth.
texts.act.8.34: And the eunuch, making answer unto Philip, said—I pray thee! Of whom, is the prophet saying this? of himself, or, of some different person?
texts.act.8.35: And Philip, opening his mouth, and beginning from this scripture, told him the glad tidings of Jesus.
texts.act.8.36: And, as they were journeying along the way, they came unto a certain water,—and the eunuch saith—Lo! water! What doth hinder my being immersed?
texts.act.8.38: And he commanded the chariot to stand still; and they went down, both, into the water, both Philip and the eunuch,—and he immersed him.
texts.act.8.39: But, when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, and the eunuch saw him no more; for he was going on his way rejoicing.
texts.act.8.40: Now Philip was found at Azotus; and, passing through, he was telling the glad tidings unto all the cities, until he came unto Caesarea.
texts.act.9.1: But, Saul, yet breathing threatening and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, going unto the High-priest,
texts.act.9.2: asked from him letters for Damascus, unto the synagogues; to the end that, if he should find, any, who were of The Way, whether men or women, he might bring them, bound, unto Jerusalem.
texts.act.9.3: But, as he was journeying, it came to pass that he was drawing near unto Damascus, and, suddenly, there flashed around him a light out of heaven;
texts.act.9.4: And, falling unto the earth, he heard a voice saying unto him—Saul! Saul! why, me, art thou persecuting?
texts.act.9.5: And he said—Who art thou, Lord? And, he, [said] —I, am Jesus, whom, thou, art persecuting!
texts.act.9.6: But rise up, and enter into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.
texts.act.9.7: But, the men who were accompanying him, stood speechless,—hearing, indeed, the voice, but beholding no one.
texts.act.9.8: And Saul arose from the earth, and, his eyes being opened, he could see nothing; and, taking him by the hand, they led him into Damascus,—
texts.act.9.9: And he was three days without seeing, and did neither eat nor drink.
texts.act.9.10: Now there was a certain disciple in Damascus, by name Ananias; and, the Lord, said unto him in a vision—Ananias! And, he, said—Lo! I, [am here], Lord!
texts.act.9.11: And the Lord [said] unto him—Rise! go into the street which is called Straight, and seek, in the house of Judas, one Saul, by name, of Tarsus. For lo! he is praying,—
texts.act.9.12: And hath seen a man [in a vision], Ananias by name, coming in and laying on him his hands, to the intent he should see.
texts.act.9.13: And Ananias, answered—Lord! I have heard from many concerning this man, how many evil things unto thy saints he hath done in Jerusalem;
texts.act.9.14: And, here, he hath authority from the High-priests to bind all them that call upon thy name.
texts.act.9.15: But the Lord said unto him—Be going thy way; for, a choice vessel unto me, is this man, to bear my name before both [the] nations and kings, and the sons of Israel;
texts.act.9.16: For, I, will let him understand how many things he must needs, for my name, suffer.
texts.act.9.17: And Ananias departed, and entered into the house; and, laying upon him his hands, said—Saul, brother! The Lord, hath sent me,—Jesus, who appeared unto thee in the way by which thou wast coming,—that thou mayest recover sight, and be filled with Holy Spirit.
texts.act.9.18: And, straightway, there fell from him—from his eyes,—as it were scales; he recovered sight also, and, arising, was immersed:
texts.act.9.19: And, receiving food, gained strength. And he came to be with the disciples who were in Damascus certain days;
texts.act.9.20: And, straightway, in the synagogues, he began proclaiming Jesus, that, This, is the Son of God.
texts.act.9.21: And all who were hearing were astonished, and began to say—is not, this, he who destroyed, in Jerusalem, them that invoke this name; and, here, for this purpose, had come, in order that he might lead them, bound, unto the High-priests?
texts.act.9.22: But, Saul, was the more gaining power; and was confounding the Jews who dwelt in Damascus, shewing, by comparison, that—This, is the Christ.
texts.act.9.23: Now, when a considerable number of days were being fulfilled, the Jews took counsel together to kill him;
texts.act.9.24: But their plot was made known unto Saul,—and they were even narrowly watching the gates, both day and night, that they might kill him;
texts.act.9.25: But the disciples, taking him by night, through the wall, let him down, lowering him in a basket.
texts.act.9.26: And, when he had arrived in Jerusalem, he made attempts to join himself unto the disciples; and all were afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
texts.act.9.27: But, Barnabas, taking him, brought him unto the apostles, and related unto them,—how, in the way, he had seen the Lord, and that he had spoken unto him; and how, in Damascus, he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.
texts.act.9.28: And he was with them, coming in and going out in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord;
texts.act.9.29: And was both speaking and discussing with the Grecian Jews,—but, they, were setting to work to kill him.
texts.act.9.30: And the brethren, discovering it, brought him down into Caesarea, and sent him away unto Tarsus.
texts.act.9.31: So then, the assembly throughout the whole of Judaea and Galilee and Samaria, had peace, building itself up, and going on its way in the fear of the Lord; and, by the advocacy of the Holy Spirit, was being multiplied.
texts.act.9.32: And it came to pass that, Peter, going through all [quarters] went down unto the saints also dwelling in Lydda.
texts.act.9.33: And he found there a certain man, by name Aeneas, who, for eight years, had been lying prostrate upon a bed, for he was paralysed.
texts.act.9.34: And Peter said unto him—Aeneas! Jesus Christ healeth thee! Arise, and smooth thy bed for thyself. And, straightway, he arose.
texts.act.9.35: And all who dwelt in Lydda and Saron, saw him,—and, they, turned unto the Lord.
texts.act.9.36: Now, in Joppa, there was a certain female disciple, by name Tabitha, which, being translated, means Dorcas [a Gazelle]. The same, was full of good works and alms which she was doing.
texts.act.9.37: And it came to pass in those days, that she, sickening, died; and, bathing her, they laid her in an upper room.
texts.act.9.38: Now, Lydda being nigh unto Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was therein, sent off two men unto him, beseeching him—Do not delay to come through unto us!
texts.act.9.39: And Peter, arising, went with them,—whom, when he arrived, they brought up into the upper room; and there stood by him all the widows, weeping, and showing the tunics and mantles—whatsoever things Dorcas was making while she was with them.
texts.act.9.40: But Peter, putting them all outside, knelt down and prayed; and, turning towards the body, said—Tabitha, arise! And she, opening her eyes and seeing Peter, sat up.
texts.act.9.41: And, giving her his hand, he raised her up; and, calling the saints and the widows, presented her, living.
texts.act.9.42: And it became known throughout the whole of Joppa, and many believed upon the Lord.
texts.act.9.43: And it came to pass that, for a considerable number of days, he abode in Joppa, with one Simon, a tanner.
texts.act.10.1: But, a certain man in Caesarea, by name Cornelius, a centurion of the band called Italian,—
texts.act.10.2: Devout, and fearing God with all his house, doing many alms unto the people, and supplicating God continually,
texts.act.10.3: Saw, in a vision, manifestly, as if about the ninth hour of the day, a messenger of God, coming in unto him, and saying unto him—Cornelius!
texts.act.10.4: And he, looking steadfastly at him, and becoming full of fear, said—What is it, Lord? And he said unto him—Thy prayers and thine alms, have gone up for a memorial before God.
texts.act.10.5: Now, therefore, send men unto Joppa, and fetch one Simon who is surnamed Peter,—
texts.act.10.6: The same is a guest with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea.
texts.act.10.7: And, when the messenger who had been speaking with him had departed, calling two of the domestics, and a devout soldier of them that constantly attended him,
texts.act.10.8: And relating everything unto them, he sent them off unto Joppa.
texts.act.10.9: Now, on the morrow, as those men were journeying, and, unto the city, drawing near, Peter went up on the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour;
texts.act.10.10: But he became hungry, and wished to eat,—and, while they were making ready, there came upon him a trance;
texts.act.10.11: And he beholdeth heaven opened, and, corning down, a kind of vessel, like a large linen cloth, by its four corners, being let down upon the earth,
texts.act.10.12: In which were all the quadrupeds and creeping things of earth and birds of heaven.
texts.act.10.13: And there came a voice unto him—Rise, Peter! slay and eat.
texts.act.10.14: But Peter said—By no means, Lord! because, at no time, have I eaten anything common or unclean.
texts.act.10.15: And a voice [came] again, a second time, unto him—What things, God, hath cleansed, be not, thou, making common.
texts.act.10.16: Now, this, took place thrice; and, straightway, was the vessel taken up into heaven.
texts.act.10.17: And, as within himself Peter was doubting what the vision which he had seen might mean, lo! the men who had been sent by Cornelius, having sought out the house of Simon, stood at the gate,
texts.act.10.18: And, calling, enquired whether, Simon who was surnamed Peter, was there being entertained.
texts.act.10.19: And, as Peter was pondering over the vision, the Spirit said—Lo! two men, seeking thee.
texts.act.10.20: But rise, go down, and be journeying with them, nothing, doubting; because, I, have sent them.
texts.act.10.21: And Peter, going down unto the men, said—Lo! I, am he whom ye are seeking: What is the cause, for which ye are come?
texts.act.10.22: And they said—Cornelius, a centurion, a man righteous and fearing God, well-attested by the whole nation of the Jews, hath been divinely instructed by a holy messenger to send for thee unto his house, and to hear words from thee.
texts.act.10.23: Inviting them in, therefore, he entertained them; but, on the morrow, he rose up and went forth with them, and certain of the brethren who were from Joppa went with him;
texts.act.10.24: And, on the morrow, he entered into Caesarea. And, Cornelius, was expecting them, having called together his kinsfolk and intimate friends.
texts.act.10.25: And, when it came about that Peter entered, Cornelius met him, and, falling at his feet, did homage.
texts.act.10.26: But, Peter, raised him up, saying—Arise! I also myself, am, a man.
texts.act.10.27: And, conversing with him, he went in, and findeth many come together;
texts.act.10.28: And said unto the—Ye, well know, how unlawful it is, for, a Jew, to be joining himself or coming in unto one of another race. And yet, unto me, hath God pointed out that I should be calling no man, common or unclean.
texts.act.10.29: Wherefore, even without gainsaying, came I when sent for. I ask, therefore, for what reason ye sent for me.
texts.act.10.30: And Cornelius said—Four days ago, counting unto this very hour, I was keeping, the ninth hour, as one of prayer, in my house. And lo! a man stood before me, in bright clothing,
texts.act.10.31: And saith—Cornelius! thy prayer hath been heard, and, thine alms, have been remembered before God.
texts.act.10.32: Send, therefore, unto Joppa, and fetch Simon, who is surnamed Peter. The same is being entertained in the house of one Simon a tanner, by the sea.
texts.act.10.33: Immediately, therefore, I sent unto thee: Thou, also hast, well, done in coming. Now, therefore, all we, before God are present, to hear all things that have been enjoined upon thee by the Lord.
texts.act.10.34: And Peter, opening his mouth, said—Of a truth, I find that God is no respecter of persons;
texts.act.10.35: But, in every nation, he that feareth him and worketh righteousness, is acceptable unto him.
texts.act.10.36: As touching the word he hath sent unto the sons of Israel, announcing the glad tidings of peace through Jesus Christ—the same, is Lord, of all,
texts.act.10.37: Ye yourselves, know what hath come to pass throughout the whole of Judaea, beginning from Galilee, after the immersion which John proclaimed, respecting Jesus who was of Nazareth:—
texts.act.10.38: How God anointed him with Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all that were oppressed by the adversary, because, God, was with him.
texts.act.10.39: We also, are witnesses of all things which he did, both in the country of the Jews and Jerusalem; whom they even slew by suspending upon a tree;—
texts.act.10.40: The same, God raised up on the third day, and gave him to become, manifest,
texts.act.10.41: Not unto all the people, but unto witnesses who had been fore-appointed by God, unto us, who, indeed, did eat and drink with him after his rising from among the dead.
texts.act.10.42: And he charged us to proclaim unto the people, and bear full witness, that—This, is he that hath been marked out by God to be judge of living and dead.
texts.act.10.43: Unto the same, do all the prophets bear witness, That, remission of sins, is to be received through his name, by every one that believeth on him.
texts.act.10.44: While Peter was yet speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who were hearing the word.
texts.act.10.45: And the faithful, of the circumcision, who had come with Peter, were amazed,—in that, upon the nations also, the free-gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out;
texts.act.10.46: For they heard them speaking with tongues, and magnifying God. Then answered Peter—
texts.act.10.47: Surely then, the water, can no man forbid, that these should not be immersed,—seeing that, the Holy Spirit, they have received, as well as we.
texts.act.10.48: And he commanded them in the name of Jesus Christ to be immersed. Then, requested they him, to abide still some days.
texts.act.11.1: Now the Apostles and the brethren who were throughout Judaea heard that, the nations also, had welcomed the word of God.
texts.act.11.2: And, when Peter came up unto Jerusalem, they of the circumcision began to find fault with him,
texts.act.11.3: Saying—he went in unto men uncircumcised, and did eat with them.
texts.act.11.4: But Peter, making a beginning, went on to set forth the matter unto them in order, saying—
texts.act.11.5: I was in the city of Joppa praying, and saw in a trance, a vision:—coming down a sort of vessel, like a large sheet, by four corners, being let down out of heaven, and it came even unto me:
texts.act.11.6: Into which steadfastly looking, began to observe, and saw the quadrupeds of the earth, and the wild beasts, and the creeping things, and the birds of heaven.
texts.act.11.7: Moreover heard a voice also, saying unto me—Rise, Peter! slay and eat.
texts.act.11.8: But I said—By no means, Lord, because, a common or unclean thing, hath at no time entered into my mouth.
texts.act.11.9: And a voice answered, a second time, out of heaven—What things, God, hath cleansed, be not, thou, making common.
texts.act.11.10: And, this, took place thrice,—and the whole was drawn up again into heaven;
texts.act.11.11: And lo! immediately, three men halted at the house wherein we were, sent from Caesarea unto me.
texts.act.11.12: And the Spirit bade me go with them, nothing doubting. And there went with me these six brethren also; and we entered into the house of the man,
texts.act.11.13: And he related to us how he had seen the messenger in his house, standing, and saying—Send away unto Joppa, and fetch Simon, who is surnamed Peter;
texts.act.11.14: Who shall speak words unto thee, whereby thou shall be saved, thou, and all thy house.
texts.act.11.15: And, as I began to be speaking, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as upon us also at the beginning.
texts.act.11.16: And I was put in mind of the word of the Lord, how he used to say—John, indeed, immersed with water; but, ye, shall be immersed in Holy Spirit.
texts.act.11.17: If therefore the like free-gift God gave unto them, as even unto us, when we had believed upon the Lord Jesus Christ, who was, I, that could withstand God?
texts.act.11.18: And, having heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying—Hence, even unto the nations, God hath granted repentance unto life.
texts.act.11.19: They, therefore, who had been scattered abroad by reason of the tribulation that took place on account of Stephen, passed through as far as Phoenice and Cyprus and Antioch, unto no one speaking the word, save alone unto Jews.
texts.act.11.20: And there were some from among them, Cyprians and Cyrenians, who, indeed, coming unto Antioch, began speaking, even unto the Grecian Jews, announcing the glad tidings as to the Lord Jesus;
texts.act.11.21: And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number—they who believed—turned unto the Lord.
texts.act.11.22: And the matter was reported in the hearing of the assembly that was in Jerusalem, concerning them; and they sent forth Barnabas, as far as Antioch;
texts.act.11.23: Who, arriving, and seeing the favour which was of God, rejoiced, and went on to beseech all, with the purpose of their heart, to abide [in] the Lord;
texts.act.11.24: Because he was a good man, and full of Holy Spirit and faith; and a considerable multitude were added unto the Lord.
texts.act.11.25: He went away, however, unto Tarsus, to seek up Saul;
texts.act.11.26: And, finding him, he brought him unto Antioch. And so it was with them, that, for a whole year, they were brought together in the assembly, and taught a considerable multitude; also that the disciples, first in Antioch, were called, Christians.
texts.act.11.27: Now, in these days, there came down from Jerusalem, prophets, unto Antioch.
texts.act.11.28: And one from among them, by name Agabus, rising up, gave a sign, through means of the Spirit, that, a great famine, was coming over all the inhabited earth; which, indeed, came to pass under Claudius.
texts.act.11.29: And, according as any one of the disciples was being prospered, they each one of them set apart [something] for ministering, to send unto the brethren, who dwelt in Jerusalem;—
texts.act.11.30: Which thing they also did, sending it unto the Elders, through the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
texts.act.12.1: Now, in the course of that season, Herod the king thrust forth his hands to harm some of them of the assembly,—
texts.act.12.2: And slew James the brother of John with a sword;
texts.act.12.3: And, seeing that it was acceptable unto the Jews, he went on to apprehend Peter also (now they were the days of unleavened bread),—
texts.act.12.4: Whom also having seized, he put into prison, delivering him up unto four quaternions of soldiers, to be guarding him,—intending, after the passover, to bring him up unto the people.
texts.act.12.5: Peter, therefore, was kept in the prison; but, prayer, was, earnestly, being made by the assembly, unto God, concerning him.
texts.act.12.6: And, when Herod was about to bring him forth, on that night, was Peter sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, guards, also, before the door, were keeping the prison.
texts.act.12.7: And lo! a messenger of the Lord stood over him, and a light shone in the cell; and, smiting the side of Peter, he roused him up, saying—Rise up quickly! And his chains fell off out of his hands.
texts.act.12.8: And the messenger said unto him—Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals. And he did so. And he saith unto him—Throw around thee thy mantle, and be following me.
texts.act.12.9: And, coming out, he began following, and knew not that it was true which was coming about through means of the messenger; but supposed that, a vision, he was beholding.
texts.act.12.10: And, passing through the first ward and the second, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth into the city, the which, of its own accord, opened unto them; and, coming out, they went on through one street, and, straightway, the messenger was parted from him.
texts.act.12.11: And, Peter, coming to himself said—Now, know I, of a truth, that the Lord hath sent forth his messenger, and taken me out of the hand of Herod, and all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
texts.act.12.12: And, considering the matter, he came unto the house of Mary, the mother of John who was surnamed Mark, where a considerable number were gathered together and praying.
texts.act.12.13: And, when he had knocked at the door of the porch, there came unto it a maiden to hearken, by name Rhoda;
texts.act.12.14: And, recognizing the voice of Peter, by reason of her joy, she opened not the porch,—but, running in, bare tidings that Peter was standing before the porch. But, they, unto her, said—Thou art raving
texts.act.12.15: She, however, kept on strongly declaring that, so, it was. But, they, were saying—It is his, messenger.
texts.act.12.16: And, Peter, continued knocking; and, opening, they saw him, and were amazed.
texts.act.12.17: But, making a sign to them with his hand to hold their peace, he related to them how, the Lord, had brought, him, forth out of the prison; and he said—Carry tidings unto James and the brethren, as to these things. And, going out, he went his way unto some other place.
texts.act.12.18: And, when it became day, there was no small commotion among the soldiers, as to what, then, Peter had become!
texts.act.12.19: And, Herod, seeking after and not finding, him, having examined the guards, ordered them to be led away [to death]; and, going down from Judaea unto Caesarea, stayed there.
texts.act.12.20: Now he was bitterly hostile to them of Tyre and Zidon; but, with one accord, they came unto him, and, persuading Blastus, who was over the bed-chamber of the king, they were suing for peace; because their country was fed by the king’s,
texts.act.12.21: And, on an appointed day, Herod, putting on royal apparel, and seating himself upon the tribunal, proceeded to deliver an oration unto them.
texts.act.12.22: And, the populace, began to shout—A god’s, voice, and not, a man’s!
texts.act.12.23: And, instantly, there smote him, a messenger of the Lord, because he gave not the glory unto God; and, becoming worm-eaten, he expired.
texts.act.12.24: And, the word of the Lord, went on growing and multiplying.
texts.act.12.25: And, Barnabas and Saul, returned unto Jerusalem, fulfilling the ministering, taking with them John who was surnamed Mark.
texts.act.13.1: Now there were in Antioch, distributed through the existing assembly,—prophets and teachers: both Barnabas and Symeon who was called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, Manaen also, Herod the tetrarch’s foster-brother, and Saul.
texts.act.13.2: And, as they were publicly ministering unto the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said—Separate forthwith unto me, Barnabas and Saul, unto the work whereunto I have called them.
texts.act.13.3: Then, fasting and praying, and laying their hands upon them, they sent them away.
texts.act.13.4: They, therefore, being sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down unto Seleucia, and, from thence, sailed away unto Cyprus;
texts.act.13.5: And, coming to be in Salamis, they declared the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews;—and they had, John also, as an attendant.
texts.act.13.6: And, passing through the whole island, as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a magician, a false-prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesus;
texts.act.13.7: Who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The same, calling for Barnabas and Saul, sought to hear the word of God.
texts.act.13.8: But Elymas the magician,—for so, when translated, is his name,—withstood them; seeking to turn aside the proconsul from the faith.
texts.act.13.9: But Saul, who is also Paul, filled with Holy Spirit, looking steadfastly at him,
texts.act.13.10: Said—O full of all guile, and all recklessness! Son of an adversary! Enemy of all righteousness!—Wilt thou not cease to pervert the straight ways of the Lord?
texts.act.13.11: Now, therefore, lo! the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun, until a fitting time. And, instantly, there fell upon him a mist and darkness; and, going about, he was seeking such as might lead him by the hand.
texts.act.13.12: Then, the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed, being amazed at the teaching of the Lord.
texts.act.13.13: And, setting sail from Paphos, Paul’s company came into Perga of Pamphylia; but, John, withdrawing from them, returned unto Jerusalem.
texts.act.13.14: They, however, passing through from Perga, arrived at Antioch of Pisidia; and, going into the synagogue on the sabbath-day, sat down.
texts.act.13.15: And, after the reading of the law and the prophets, the synagogue-rulers sent unto them, saying—Brethren! if there is in you a word of exhortation unto the people, say on.
texts.act.13.16: And Paul, standing up, and making a sign with his hand, said—Ye men of Israel! and such as revere God! hearken:—
texts.act.13.17: The God of this people Israel, chose our fathers, and, the people, he exalted, by their sojourn in the land of Egypt,—and, with a high arm, brought he them out of it;
texts.act.13.18: And, for the time of about forty years, bare with their manners in the desert;
texts.act.13.19: And, overthrowing seven nations in the land of Canaan, gave them their land as an inheritance—about four hundred and fifty years.
texts.act.13.20: And, after these things, he gave them judges, until Samuel the prophet.
texts.act.13.21: And, from that time, they asked for themselves a king, and God gave them Saul, son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, during forty years;
texts.act.13.22: And, setting him aside, raised up, David, unto them for king,—of whom he also said, bearing witness—I have found David, the son of Jesse,— [a man] according to my heart, who will do all my will.
texts.act.13.23: From this man’s seed, hath God, according to promise, brought unto Israel, a saviour—Jesus:
texts.act.13.24: John, beforehand proclaiming, before the face of his coming in, an immersion of repentance, unto all the people of Israel.
texts.act.13.25: And, as John was fulfilling his course, he was saying—Whom are ye supposing that I am? I, am not he! But lo! there cometh, after me, one of whom I am not worthy, the sandals of his feet, to loosen.
texts.act.13.26: Brethren! sons of the race of Abraham, and those who among you revere God,—unto you, hath this word of salvation been sent forth.
texts.act.13.27: For, they who were dwelling in Jerusalem, and their rulers, not recognising him, have, by judging him, fulfilled, the very voices of the prophets which every sabbath are being read;
texts.act.13.28: And, though no single cause of death they found, yet claimed they of Pilate that he should be slain.
texts.act.13.29: And, when they had finished all those things which, concerning him, had been written, taking him down from the tree, they put him in a tomb.
texts.act.13.30: But, God, raised him from among the dead:
texts.act.13.31: Who appeared, during many days, unto them who had come up with him from Galilee unto Jerusalem; who, indeed, [now] are his witnesses unto the people.
texts.act.13.32: We, therefore, unto you, bring the good news, as to the promise which, unto our fathers, was made,—
texts.act.13.33: That God hath fulfilled, the same, for our children, by raising up Jesus: as also, in the second psalm, it is written—My son, art, thou: I, this day, have begotten thee.
texts.act.13.34: And, in that he raised him from among the dead, no more destined to return unto corruption, on this wise hath he spoken—I will give unto you the faithful lovingkindnesses of David.
texts.act.13.35: Wherefore also, in a different [place], he saith—Thou wilt not give thy man of lovingkindness to see corruption.
texts.act.13.36: For, David, indeed, unto his own generation having done service, by the counsel of God, fell asleep, and was added unto fathers, and saw corruption;
texts.act.13.37: But, he whom God hath raised, did not see corruption.
texts.act.13.38: Be it known unto you, therefore, brethren,—that, through this man, unto you, remission of sins is declared;
texts.act.13.39: And, from all things from which ye could not, by the law of Moses, be justified, by this man, everyone that believeth, is justified.
texts.act.13.40: Be taking heed, therefore, lest that come upon you which hath been spoken in the prophets—
texts.act.13.41: See, ye despisers, and marvel, and disappear: in that, a work, am, I, working in your days,—a work, which in nowise will ye believe, though one relate it in full unto you.
texts.act.13.42: And, as they were going out, they kept on beseeching that, on the ensuing sabbath, might be spoken unto them these things.
texts.act.13.43: And, when the congregation was broken up, there followed many of the Jews, and of the devout proselytes, with Paul and Barnabas; who, indeed, in speaking unto them, went on persuading them to abide in the favour of God.
texts.act.13.44: And, on the coming sabbath, almost all the city, was gathered together, to hear the word of God.
texts.act.13.45: But, the Jews, seeing, the multitudes, were filled with jealousy,—and began speaking against the things which, by Paul, were being spoken, defaming them.
texts.act.13.46: And Paul and Barnabas, speaking boldly, said—Unto you, was it necessary, that the word of God should first be spoken: seeing ye are thrusting it from you, and, unworthy, are judging yourselves of the age-abiding life, lo! we turn unto the nations;
texts.act.13.47: For so hath the Lord commanded us—I have set thee for a light of nations, that thou mayest be for salvation unto the end of the earth.
texts.act.13.48: And they of the nations, hearing [this], began to rejoice, and to be glorifying God, and they believed—as many as had become disposed for life age-abiding.
texts.act.13.49: And the word of the Lord went on to be carried through the whole country.
texts.act.13.50: But, the Jews, urged on the devout women of the higher class, and the chief men of the city, and roused up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas,—and thrust them out from their bounds.
texts.act.13.51: But they, shaking off the dust of their feet against them, came into Iconium.
texts.act.13.52: And, the disciples, were filled with joy, and with Holy Spirit.
texts.act.14.1: And it came to pass in Iconium that they together entered into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spake that there believed, both of Jews and Greeks, a great throng.
texts.act.14.2: But, the unpersuaded Jews, roused up and provoked the souls of them of the nations against the brethren.
texts.act.14.3: A good while, therefore, tarried they, using boldness of speech [in dependence] upon the Lord, who was bearing witness unto his word of favour, granting signs and wonders to be coming to pass through their hands.
texts.act.14.4: And the throng of the city was divided; and some indeed were with the Jews, while some were with the apostles.
texts.act.14.5: But, when there took place an assault both of them of the nations and of the Jews, with their rulers, to maltreat and to stone them,
texts.act.14.6: They became aware of it, and fled unto the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the surrounding country;
texts.act.14.7: And, there, were they announcing the glad tidings.
texts.act.14.8: And, a certain man in Lystra, impotent in his feet, was sitting,—lame from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.
texts.act.14.9: This man, hearkened unto Paul, as he was speaking,—who, looking steadfastly at him, and seeing he had faith to be made well,
texts.act.14.10: Said, with a loud voice—Stand up on thy feet, erect! And he sprang up, and began to walk about.
texts.act.14.11: And, the multitudes, seeing what Paul had done, lifted up their voice, in the speech of Lycaonia—The gods, made like unto men, have come down unto us!
texts.act.14.12: And they went on to call Barnabas, Jupiter, and Paul, Mercury, seeing that, he, was the leader of discourse.
texts.act.14.13: Also, the priest of the Jupiter that was before the city, bringing bulls and garlands unto the gates, with the multitudes, would have offered sacrifice.
texts.act.14.14: But the apostles Barnabas and Paul, hearing of it, rending asunder their own mantles, sprang forward amidst the multitude, crying aloud,
texts.act.14.15: and saying—Men! Why, these things, are ye doing? We also, of like nature with you, are men, bringing you the good news, that from these vain things, ye should be turning unto a living God:—Who made heaven and the earth and the sea and all things therein;
texts.act.14.16: Who in the bygone generations suffered all the nations to be going on in their own ways,—
texts.act.14.17: Although, not without witness, he left himself, doing good, from heaven, upon you, giving rain and fruitful seasons, filling, with food and gladness, your hearts.
texts.act.14.18: Even these things, saying, scarcely restrained they the multitudes from offering sacrifice unto them.
texts.act.14.19: But there came thither, from Antioch and Iconium, Jews, and, persuading the multitudes, and stoning Paul, they dragged him outside the city, supposing him to be dead.
texts.act.14.20: Howbeit, the disciples surrounding him, he rose up, and entered into the city. And, on the morrow, he went forth, with Barnabas, unto Derbe.
texts.act.14.21: Delivering the good news unto that city also, and making a good number of disciples, they returned unto Lystra, and unto Iconium, and unto Antioch,—
texts.act.14.22: confirming the souls of the disciples, beseeching them to abide in the faith, and [declaring] that, through many tribulations, must we enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.act.14.23: Moreover, appointing unto them by vote, in each assembly, elders, praying with fastings, they commended them unto the Lord on whom they had believed.
texts.act.14.24: And, passing through Pisidia, they came into Pamphylia;
texts.act.14.25: and, speaking in Perga the word, they came down unto Attalia;
texts.act.14.26: and, from thence, they set sail for Antioch, whence they had been given up unto the favour of God for the work which they had fulfilled.
texts.act.14.27: And, when they had arrived and gathered together the assembly, they began recounting how many things God had done with them, and that he had opened, unto the nations, a door of faith.
texts.act.14.28: And they spent no little time with the disciples.
texts.act.15.1: And, certain persons, coming down from Judea, began to teach the brethren—Except ye be circumcised according to the custom of Moses, ye cannot be saved.
texts.act.15.2: And, when Paul and Barnabas had had no little dissension and discussion with them, it was arranged that Paul and Barnabas and certain others from among them should go up unto the Apostles and Elders in Jerusalem concerning this question,
texts.act.15.3: They, therefore, being set forward by the Assembly, began passing through Phoenicia and Samaria, fully relating the conversion of them of the nations, and were causing great joy unto all the brethren.
texts.act.15.4: And, having arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the Assembly and the Apostles and the Elders; and they recounted all things God had done with them.
texts.act.15.5: But there [had] stood forth some of those who, from the sect of Pharisees, had believed, saying—It is needful to be circumcising them, also to charge them to be keeping the law of Moses.
texts.act.15.6: And the Apostles and Elders were gathered together to see about this matter.
texts.act.15.7: And, when much discussion had arisen, Peter standing up, said unto them—Brethren! Ye yourselves, well know that, in days long past, amongst you, God chose that, through my mouth, the nations should hear the word of the glad tidings, and believe.
texts.act.15.8: And, the heart-observing God, bare witness,—unto them, giving the Holy Spirit, just as, even unto us;
texts.act.15.9: and made no distinction at all betwixt us and them, by their faith, purifying their hearts.
texts.act.15.10: Now, therefore, why are ye proving God, that ye should put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which, neither our fathers, nor we, have been able to bear.
texts.act.15.11: But, through the favour of the Lord Jesus, we believe we shall be saved, in like manner as, even they.
texts.act.15.12: And all the throng held their peace, and began to hearken unto Barnabas and Paul relating how many signs and wonders God had done among the nations, through them.
texts.act.15.13: And, after they held their peace, James answered, saying—Brethren! hearken unto me.
texts.act.15.14: Symeon, hath fully told how God, first visited, to take out of the nations, a people for his name.
texts.act.15.15: And, with this, agree the words of the prophets, according as it is written—
texts.act.15.16: After these things, will I return, and will rebuild the tent of David that hath fallen, and, the ruins thereof, will I rebuild, and will set it up again:
texts.act.15.17: That the residues of men may seek out the Lord, and all the nations upon whom my name hath been called, saith the Lord that doeth these things,
texts.act.15.19: Wherefore, I, judge, not to be troubling them who, from the nations, are turning unto God;
texts.act.15.20: but to write unto them, to abstain from the pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from what is strangled, and from blood.
texts.act.15.21: For, Moses, out of ancient generation, hath, in every city, them who proclaim him; seeing, that in the synagogues, every sabbath, he is read.
texts.act.15.22: Then, seemed it good unto the Apostles and the Elders with the whole Assembly to send chosen men from among them unto Antioch, with Paul and Barnabas,—even Judas who is called Barsabbas, and Silas, men taking a lead among the brethren:
texts.act.15.23: writing through their hand—The Apostles and the Elder Brethren, unto the brethren throughout Antioch and Syria and Cilicia, who are from among the nations, wish joy!
texts.act.15.24: Inasmuch as we had heard that, certain from among us, had troubled you with words, dismantling your souls,—unto whom we had given no instructions,
texts.act.15.25: It seemed good unto us, coming to be of one accord, that we should choose men and send them unto you, with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,—
texts.act.15.26: men who have given up their lives in behalf of the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.act.15.27: We have sent, therefore, Judas and Silas, who also, themselves, by word of mouth, can tell you the same things.
texts.act.15.28: For it hath seemed good unto the Holy Spirit and unto us, no greater burden, to be laying upon you, than these necessary things:—
texts.act.15.29: To be abstaining from idol sacrifices, and from blood, and from what is strangled, and from fornication,—From which, if ye keep yourselves, ye shall prosper. Fare ye well.
texts.act.15.30: They, therefore, being let go, came down unto Antioch; and, having gathered together the throng, delivered the letter,
texts.act.15.31: and, when they read it, they rejoiced for the consolation.
texts.act.15.32: And, both Judas and Silas, being themselves also prophets, with much discourse, consoled and confirmed the brethren.
texts.act.15.33: And, when they had spent a time, they were let go, in peace, from the brethren, unto them who had sent them.
texts.act.15.35: But, Paul and Barnabas, tarried in Antioch, teaching and telling the joyful tidings,—along with many others also,—of the word of the Lord.
texts.act.15.36: And, after certain days, Paul, said unto Barnabas—Let us now return, and visit the brethren in every city in which we have declared the word of the Lord, and see how they are.
texts.act.15.37: And, Barnabas, was minded to take with them John also, called Mark;
texts.act.15.38: but Paul deemed it right, as to him who had withdrawn from them, back from Pamphylia, and had not gone with them unto the work, not to be taking with them, this, man.
texts.act.15.39: And there arose an angry feeling, so that they separated one from the other: and, Barnabas, taking Mark, sailed away unto Cyprus,—
texts.act.15.40: whereas, Paul, choosing Silas, went forth, committed unto the favour of the Lord by the brethren,
texts.act.15.41: and proceeded to pass through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the assemblies.
texts.act.16.1: And he came even unto Derbe, and unto Lystra; and lo! a certain disciple, was there, by name Timothy, son of a believing Jewish woman, but whose father was a Greek,—
texts.act.16.2: who was well-attested by the brethren in Lystra, and Iconium.
texts.act.16.3: The same, would Paul have go forth with him, and took and circumcised him, on account of the Jews who were in those places; for they one and all knew that, his father, was, a Greek.
texts.act.16.4: And, as they passed through the cities, they were delivering unto them, for observance, the decrees which had been decided upon by the Apostles and Elders who were in Jerusalem.
texts.act.16.5: The assemblies, therefore, were being confirmed in the faith, and increasing in number, every day.
texts.act.16.6: And they passed through the Phrygian and Galatian country, being forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia;
texts.act.16.7: but, coming along Mysia, they were attempting to journey into Bithynia,—and, the Spirit of Jesus, suffered them not;
texts.act.16.8: but, passing by Mysia, they came down unto Troas.
texts.act.16.9: And, a vision, by night, unto Paul appeared:—A man of Macedonia, there was, standing and beseeching him, and saying—Come over into Macedonia, and bring us succour!
texts.act.16.10: Now, when, the vision, he had seen, straightway, we sought to go forth unto Macedonia, concluding that God, had summoned us to tell the glad tidings unto them.
texts.act.16.11: Setting sail, therefore, from Troas, we ran straight into Samothracia, and, on the morrow, unto New City,
texts.act.16.12: and, from thence, unto Philippi,—which, indeed, is the first city of the part of Macedonia—a colony. And we were, in this city, spending certain days;
texts.act.16.13: and on the day of rest, we went forth outside the gate, beside a river, where we supposed there was a place of prayer,—and, sitting down, we went on to speak unto the women who had come together.
texts.act.16.14: And, a certain woman, by name Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, devout towards God, was hearkening, whose heart, the Lord, fully opened, to be giving heed unto the things being spoken by Paul.
texts.act.16.15: And, when she was immersed, and her house, she besought [us], saying—If ye have judged me to be a believer in the Lord, come into my house, and abide [there]. And she constrained us.
texts.act.16.16: And it came to pass, as we were on our way unto the place of prayer, a certain damsel, having a spirit of Python, met us,—who, indeed, much gain, was presenting unto her masters, by divining.
texts.act.16.17: The same, following after Paul and us, kept crying aloud, saying—These men, are servants of the Most High God,—who, indeed, are declaring unto you a way of salvation.
texts.act.16.18: And, this, she continued to do for many days. But Paul, worn out, and turning unto the spirit, said—I charge thee, in the name of Jesus Christ, to come out from her. And it came out the same hour.
texts.act.16.19: And, her masters, seeing that their hope of gain had gone out, laying hold on Paul and Silas, dragged them into the market-place, unto the rulers;
texts.act.16.20: and, leading them forward unto the magistrates, said—These men, are exceedingly troubling our city, they, being Jews,
texts.act.16.21: And are declaring customs, which it is not allowable for us either to accept or to observe, being Romans.
texts.act.16.22: And the multitude rose up together against them, and, the magistrates, rending off them their mantles, were giving orders to beat them with rods;
texts.act.16.23: and, laying upon them many stripes, they thrust them into prison, charging the prison-keeper, safely, to be keeping them:
texts.act.16.24: who, a charge like this receiving, thrust them into the inner prison, and, their feet, made he fast in the stocks.
texts.act.16.25: And, at midnight, Paul and Silas, being at prayer, began singing praise unto God; and the prisoners unto them, did hearken.
texts.act.16.26: And, suddenly, a great earthquake took place,—so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and all the doors were [instantly] set open, and the bonds of all were unfastened.
texts.act.16.27: And, the prison-keeper, being wakened and seeing that the doors of the prison had been opened, drawing his sword, was about to kill himself, supposing the prisoners to have fled.
texts.act.16.28: But Paul called out with a loud voice, saying—By no means, do thyself harm, for we are, one and all, here.
texts.act.16.29: And, asking for a light, he sprang in, and becoming, agitated, fell down unto Paul and Silas,
texts.act.16.30: and, leading them forth outside, said—Sirs! what must I be doing, that I may be saved?
texts.act.16.31: And, they, said—Believe on the Lord Jesus, and thou shalt be saved, thou, and thy house.
texts.act.16.32: And they spake unto him the word of God, with all who were in his house.
texts.act.16.33: And, taking them with him, in that hour of the night, he bathed them from their stripes, and was immersed, he, and his, one and all, on the spot;
texts.act.16.34: and, leading them up into his house, he set near a table,—and exulted, having, with all his house, believed in God.
texts.act.16.35: And. when day came. the magistrates sent off the constables saying—Let those men go!
texts.act.16.36: And the prison-keeper reported the words unto Paul—The magistrates have sent, that ye be let go. Now, therefore, going forth, be taking your journey in peace.
texts.act.16.37: But, Paul, said unto them—Beating us, in public, uncondemned, men that are Romans, they thrust us into prison;—and, now, by stealth, are they thrusting us forth? Nay, verily! but let them come, themselves, and lead us out!
texts.act.16.38: And the constables reported unto the magistrates these words; and they were struck with fear, when they heard that they were, Romans;
texts.act.16.39: and came, and besought them, and, leading them out, went on to request them to depart from the city.
texts.act.16.40: And so, coming forth from the prison, they went unto Lydia, and, seeing the brethren, they comforted them, and went forth.
texts.act.17.1: And, travelling through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews;
texts.act.17.2: and, according to Paul’s custom, he went in unto them, and, for three sabbaths, reasoned with them from the Scriptures,—
texts.act.17.3: opening up, and setting forth, that it was needful for, the Christ, to suffer, and to arise from among the dead; and [saying], This, is the Christ,—Jesus, whom, I, am declaring unto you.
texts.act.17.4: And, some from among them, were persuaded, and cast in their lot with Paul and Silas; also, of the devout Greeks, a great throng, and, of the chief women, not a few.
texts.act.17.5: But the Jews, being, jealous, and taking unto themselves certain wicked men, of the rabble, and making a riot, were setting the city in an uproar; and, besieging the house of Jason, were seeking to lead them forth unto the populace,—
texts.act.17.6: and, not finding them, they began dragging Jason and certain brethren unto the city-rulers, shouting—They who have thrown the inhabited earth into confusion, the same, hither also, are come,—
texts.act.17.7: unto whom Jason hath given welcome; and, these all, contrary to the decrees of Caesar, are acting,—saying that there is another king, Jesus.
texts.act.17.8: And they troubled the multitude and the city-rulers, when they heard these things;
texts.act.17.9: and, taking security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.
texts.act.17.10: But, the brethren, straightway, during the night, sent away both Paul and Silas unto Beroea, who, indeed, arriving, unto the synagogue of the Jews, went off;
texts.act.17.11: and, these, were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they welcomed the word with all readiness of mind, daily, searching the Scriptures,—whether these things could be so.
texts.act.17.12: Many, therefore, from among them, believed, and, of the Grecian women of the higher class, and of men, not a few.
texts.act.17.13: But, when the Jews from Thessalonica came to know that, in Beroea also, had the word of God been declared by Paul, they came thither also, stirring up and troubling the multitudes.
texts.act.17.14: Howbeit, then, immediately, the brethren sent away, Paul, to be journeying as far as unto the sea; and both Silas and Timothy stayed behind, there.
texts.act.17.15: But, they who were conducting Paul, brought him as far as Athens, and, receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timothy, that with, all possible speed, they would come unto him, they departed.
texts.act.17.16: But, while, in Athens, Paul was expecting them, his spirit within him was being urged on, seeing how the city was given to idols.
texts.act.17.17: So then, he began reasoning in the synagogue with the Jews, and with them who worshipped; and, in the market-place, every day, with them who happened to be at hand.
texts.act.17.18: But, certain both of the Epicurean and of the Stoic philosophers, were encountering him; and some were saying—What might this picker-up-of-scraps wish to be saying?
