And, others—Of foreign demons, he seemeth to be a declarer: because, of Jesus and the Resurrection, he was announcing the joyful tidings.
texts.act.17.19: And so, laying hold of him, they brought him up, to the Hill of Mars, saying—Can we get to know what this new teaching is, which, by thee, is being spoken.
texts.act.17.20: For, certain foreign things, art thou bringing into our hearing: We are minded to get to know, therefore, what these things please to be!
texts.act.17.21: Now, all Athenians and the sojourning foreigners, unto nothing else, were devoting their leisure, than to be telling or hearing, something newer.
texts.act.17.22: And Paul taking his stand in the midst of the Hill of Mars, said—Ye men of Athens! In every way, how unusually reverent of the demons ye are, I perceive.
texts.act.17.23: For, passing through, and carefully observing your objects of devotion, I found an altar also, in which was inscribed—Unto an Unknown God. What, therefore, not knowing, ye reverence, the same, do, I, declare unto you.
texts.act.17.24: The God that made the world and all things that are therein, the same, being, Lord, of heaven and earth, not in hand-made shrines, doth dwell,
texts.act.17.25: nor, by human hands, is waited upon, as though in want of anything, himself, giving unto all life and breath and all things;
texts.act.17.26: he made also, of one, every nation of men to dwell upon all the face of the earth,—marking out fitting opportunities, and the bounds of their dwelling place,
texts.act.17.27: that they might be seeking God—if, after all, indeed, they might feel after him and find him,—although, in truth, he is already not far from any one of us.
texts.act.17.28: For, in him, we live and move and are: as, even some of your own poets, have said—For, his offspring also, we are.
texts.act.17.29: Being, then, offspring, of God, we ought not to be supposing that, unto gold or silver or stone, graven by art and device of man, the Divine, is like.
texts.act.17.30: The times of ignorance, therefore, overlooking, God, as things now are, is charging all men everywhere to repent,
texts.act.17.31: inasmuch as he hath appointed a day, in which he is about to be judging the habitable earth in righteousness, by a man whom he hath pointed out,—offering faith unto all, by raising him from among the dead?
texts.act.17.32: Now, when they heard of raising the dead, some, indeed, began to mock, while, others, said—We will hear thee, concerning this, even again.
texts.act.17.33: Thus, Paul, came forth out of their midst.
texts.act.17.34: But, certain persons, joining themselves unto him, believed; among whom were even Dionysius the Mars-hill judge, and a woman by name Damaris, and others with them.
texts.act.18.1: After these things, withdrawing from Athens, he came unto Corinth;
texts.act.18.2: and, finding a certain Jew, by name Aquila, of Pontus by birth,—lately come from Italy, and Priscilla his wife, because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to be leaving Rome, he came unto them,
texts.act.18.3: and, because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought, for they were tent-makers by their trade.
texts.act.18.4: And he began reasoning in the synagogue every sabbath, and was persuading both Jews and Greeks.
texts.act.18.5: When, however, both Silas and Timothy had come down from Macedonia, Paul began to be urged on in the word, bearing full witness unto the Jews that, Jesus, was, the Christ.
texts.act.18.6: But, as they began opposing and defaming, shaking out his garments, he said unto them—Your blood, be upon your own head! Pure, am, I: henceforth, unto the nations, will I go.
texts.act.18.7: And, removing from thence, he came into the house of a certain man by name Titius Justus, who worshipped God, whose house was adjoining unto the synagogue.
texts.act.18.8: But, Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord, with all his house. And, many of the Corinthians, hearing, were believing, and being immersed.
texts.act.18.9: And the Lord said by night, through means of a vision, unto Paul—Be not afraid! but be speaking,—and do not hold thy peace;
texts.act.18.10: Inasmuch as, I, am with thee, and, no one, shall set upon thee to harm thee; inasmuch as I have much people in this city.
texts.act.18.11: And he remained a year and six months, teaching among them the word of God.
texts.act.18.12: But, when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews, with one accord, set upon Paul, and led him unto the judgment-seat,
texts.act.18.13: saying—Contrary to the law, is this one seducing men to be worshipping God.
texts.act.18.14: But, as Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews—If, indeed, it had been some wrong or wicked recklessness, O Jews, with reason, in that case, should I have been bearing with you.
texts.act.18.15: If, however, they are questions concerning discourse, and names, and law, that which ye have, ye shall see to it, yourselves; A judge of these things, I, am not disposed to be.
texts.act.18.16: And he drove them from the judgment-seat.
texts.act.18.17: But they all, laying hold of Sosthenes the ruler of the synagogue, began to strike him before the judgment-seat; and, for none of these things, did Gallio care.
texts.act.18.18: Paul, however, still further abiding a good many days with the brethren, bidding them adieu, set sail for Syria; and, with him, Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
texts.act.18.19: And they came down to Ephesus; and, as for them, he left them there,—but, himself entering into the synagogue, he reasoned with the Jews.
texts.act.18.20: And, when they requested him for a longer time to abide, he consented not;
texts.act.18.21: but, bidding them adieu, and saying—Again, will I return unto you, God willing, he sailed away from Ephesus;
texts.act.18.22: and, putting in at Caesarea, going up and saluting the assembly, went down unto Antioch;
texts.act.18.23: and, spending some time, he went forth, passing through, in order, the country of Galatia and Phrygia, confirming all the disciples.
texts.act.18.24: But, a certain Jew, Apollos by name, an Alexandrian by birth, a learned man, came down to Ephesus, being, mighty, in the Scriptures.
texts.act.18.25: The same, had been orally taught the way of the Lord, and, being fervent in his spirit, began speaking and teaching accurately, the things concerning Jesus,—properly knowing, only the immersion of John.
texts.act.18.26: The same, also began speaking boldly in the synagogue; and Priscilla and Aquila, hearing him, took him unto them, and, more accurately, expounded unto him the way of God.
texts.act.18.27: And, he being minded to pass through into Achaia, the brethren urgently wrote unto the disciples to welcome him,—who, arriving, was very useful unto them who had believed, with his gift;
texts.act.18.28: for, with great force, began he confuting the Jews, publicly, shewing by the Scriptures that Jesus was, the Christ.
texts.act.19.1: And it came to pass, while Apollos was in Corinth, Paul, passing through the upper parts, came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples;
texts.act.19.2: and he said unto them—Holy Spirit, received ye, when ye believed? And they said unto him—Nay! not even whether there is Holy Spirit, did we hear.
texts.act.19.3: And he said—Into what, then, were ye immersed? And, they, said—Unto John’s immersion.
texts.act.19.4: Then said Paul—John, immersed with an immersion of repentance, unto the people, saying, that, on him who was coming after him, they should believe,—that is, on Jesus.
texts.act.19.5: And, when they heard [this], they were immersed into the name of the Lord Jesus;
texts.act.19.6: and, Paul laying hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they began speaking with tongues and prophesying.
texts.act.19.7: And all the men were about twelve.
texts.act.19.8: And, entering into the synagogue, he was speaking boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading concerning the kingdom of God.
texts.act.19.9: But, when some were hardening themselves, and refusing to be persuaded, speaking evil of the Way before the throng, withdrawing from them, he separated the disciples; day by day, reasoning in the school of Tyrannus.
texts.act.19.10: And, this, took place for two years, so that, all who dwelt in Asia, heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.
texts.act.19.11: Mighty works, also, not the ordinary, God was working through the hands of Paul;
texts.act.19.12: so that, even unto the sick, were being carried from his body, handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases were departing from them, and, the wicked spirits, were going out.
texts.act.19.13: But certain also of the wandering Jews, exorcists, took in hand to be naming, over them that had the wicked spirits, the name of the Lord Jesus, saying—I adjure you, by Jesus whom Paul proclaimeth!
texts.act.19.14: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, a High-priest, who, this thing, were doing.
texts.act.19.15: But the wicked spirit. Answering, said unto them—Jesus, [indeed], I am getting to know, and, Paul, I well-know,—but who are, ye?
texts.act.19.16: And the man in whom was the wicked spirit, springing upon them, mastering them both, prevailed against them, so that, naked and wounded, fled they out of that house.
texts.act.19.17: And, this, became known to all—both Jews and Greeks—who were dwelling in Ephesus; and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was being magnified.
texts.act.19.18: Many also of them who had believed, were coming, making open confession, and renouncing their practices.
texts.act.19.19: And, a good many of them who had practised the curious arts, bringing together the books, were burning them before all; and they reckoned up the prices of them, and found them fifty thousand pieces of silver.
texts.act.19.20: Thus, with might, the Lord’s word, was growing and prevailing.
texts.act.19.21: Now, when these things were fulfilled, Paul purposed in his spirit, going through Macedonia and Achaia, to be journeying unto Jerusalem, saying—After I have been there, Rome also, must I see!
texts.act.19.22: And, sending off into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself, held on awhile in Asia.
texts.act.19.23: And there arose during that season no small disturbance concerning the Way.
texts.act.19.24: For, one Demetrius by name, a silversmith, making [silver] shrines, of Diana, used to bring unto the craftsmen no little business;
texts.act.19.25: gathering whom together, and them who in such things wrought, he said—Men! ye well know that, by this business, we have our prosperity;
texts.act.19.26: and ye perceive and hear that, not only in Ephesus, but well-nigh in all Asia, this Paul, hath persuaded and turned away a considerable multitude, saying that they are, no gods, which, with hands, are made.
texts.act.19.27: And, not only is there danger that this our heritage into ill-repute may come, but even that the temple, of the great Goddess Diana, for nothing, may be counted; also that, even on the point of being pulled down, may be Her Majesty, whom, all Asia and the habitable world, do worship.
texts.act.19.28: Now, hearing this, and becoming full of wrath, they began crying aloud, saying—Great, is Diana of the Ephesians!
texts.act.19.29: And the city was filled with the confusion; they rushed also with one accord into the theatre, carrying off with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, fellow-travellers of Paul.
texts.act.19.30: But, Paul, being minded to enter in among the populace, the disciples would not suffer him.
texts.act.19.31: Moreover, certain of the Asiarchs also, being his friends, sending unto him, were beseeching him not to adventure himself into the theatre.
texts.act.19.32: Others, indeed, were crying out something else; for the assembly had become confused, and, the greater part, knew not for what cause they had come together.
texts.act.19.33: Howbeit, out of the multitude, they bare aloft one Alexander, the Jews thrusting him forward; Alexander, however, waving his hand, was wishing to make his defense unto the populace.
texts.act.19.34: But, recognizing that he was a Jew, one voice arose from all for about two hours, as they cried aloud—Great, is Diana of the Ephesians!
texts.act.19.35: Howbeit the town-clerk, having calmed the multitude, saith—Ephesians! why, who is there of mankind that doth not acknowledge the city of Ephesians to be temple-keeper of the Great Diana, and of the [image] that fell from Jupiter?
texts.act.19.36: As these things, then, cannot be denied, it is needful that ye be calmed at once, and, nothing rash, be doing.
texts.act.19.37: For ye have brought these men, neither as temple-robbers, nor as defaming our goddess.
texts.act.19.38: If then, Demetrius, and the craftsmen with him, have against anyone an accusation, courts, are being held, and there are, proconsuls: let them accuse one another!
texts.act.19.39: But, if after, something further, ye are seeking, in the regular assembly shall it be settled.
texts.act.19.40: For we are, even in danger of being accused of riot, concerning this day, no cause at all, existing, by reference to which we shall be able to give a reason for this concourse.
texts.act.19.41: And, these things, having said, he dismissed the assembly.
texts.act.20.1: But, after the tumult had ceased, Paul, sending for the disciples and exhorting them, took leave, and went forth to be journeying unto Macedonia.
texts.act.20.2: Passing through those parts, however, and exhorting them with much discourse, he came into Greece;
texts.act.20.3: and, spending three months, when a plot was laid against him by the Jews, as he was about to sail to Syria, he determined to turn back through Macedonia.
texts.act.20.4: Now there were accompanying him, Sopater, son of Pyrrhus a Beroean; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe and Timothy; and, of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
texts.act.20.5: And, these, came and were waiting for us at Troas.
texts.act.20.6: And, we, sailed forth, after the days of unleavened bread, from Philippi, and came unto them in Troas in five days, where we tarried seven days.
texts.act.20.7: And, on the first of the week, when we were gathered together to break bread, Paul went on to discourse with them, being about to depart on the morrow; and he prolonged his discourse until midnight.
texts.act.20.8: Now there were a good many torches in the upper room, where we were gathered together.
texts.act.20.9: And there sat, a certain young man by name Eutychus, in the window, who was getting overpowered by a deep sleep; and, while Paul was discoursing yet further, being overpowered by his sleep, he fell, from the third story, down, and was taken up dead.
texts.act.20.10: Going down, however, Paul fell upon him, and, embracing him, said—Be not making confusion; for, his soul, is, in him.
texts.act.20.11: And, going up, and breaking the loaf, and tasting,—for a good while also conversing, until dawn, thus, he departed.
texts.act.20.12: And they brought the boy alive, and were comforted beyond measure.
texts.act.20.13: And, we, going forward unto the ship, set sail for Assos, from thence being about to take up Paul; for, so, had he arranged, being about, himself, to go on foot.
texts.act.20.14: And, when he fell in with us in Assos, we took him on board, and came into Mitylene;
texts.act.20.15: and, from thence sailing away on the morrow, we came over against Chios, and, on the next day, we thrust aside into Samos, and, on the succeeding day, we came into Miletus.
texts.act.20.16: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, lest he should happen to lose time in Asia; for he hastened, if it were possible for him, against the day of Pentecost, to arrive, in Jerusalem.
texts.act.20.17: But, from Miletus, he sent unto Ephesus, and called for the elders of the assembly.
texts.act.20.18: And, when they were come to him, he said unto them—Ye yourselves, well know, from the first day when I set foot in Asia, in what manner came to be with you all the time,
texts.act.20.19: doing service unto the Lord, with all humility and tears, and temptations which befell me through the plots of the Jews:
texts.act.20.20: in what manner I in nowise shrank from announcing unto you anything that was profitable and teaching you publicly and in your homes;
texts.act.20.21: bearing full witness, both to Jews and to Greeks, as to the repentance due unto God, and as to belief on our Lord Jesus.
texts.act.20.22: And, now, lo! I, bound in my spirit, am journeying unto Jerusalem; the things which therein shall befall me, not knowing,—
texts.act.20.23: save that, the Holy Spirit, from city to city, doth bear me full witness, saying that, bonds and tribulations, await me.
texts.act.20.24: But, for no cause whatever, am I making my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my course and the ministry which I have received from the Lord Jesus, to bear full witness as to the good news of the favour of God.
texts.act.20.25: And, now, lo! I, know that, no more, shall ye see my face,—ye all, among whom I have gone about proclaiming the kingdom.
texts.act.20.26: Wherefore I take you to witness, on this very day, that, pure am I from the blood of all;
texts.act.20.27: for I have not shrunk from announcing all the counsel of God unto you.
texts.act.20.28: Be taking heed unto yourselves, and unto all the little flock in which the Holy Spirit hath set, you, as overseers,—to be shepherding the assembly of God which he hath acquired through means of the blood of his own.
texts.act.20.29: I, know, that there will enter, after my departure, grievous wolves into your midst, not sparing the little flock;
texts.act.20.30: and, from among your own selves, will arise men speaking distorted things, to draw away the disciples after themselves.
texts.act.20.31: Wherefore, be on the watch, remembering that, for three years, night and day, I gave myself no rest, with tears, admonishing each one.
texts.act.20.32: Now, therefore, I commend you unto the Lord, and unto his word of favour,—which is able to build up and give the inheritance among all the hallowed ones.
texts.act.20.33: The silver or gold or apparel of no one, did I covet:
texts.act.20.34: yourselves, acknowledge that, for my necessities and for those who were with me, hard wrought these hands!
texts.act.20.35: In all things, I gave you to understand, that, thus toiling, it behoves to be helping the weak, also to be keeping in mind the words of the Lord Jesus, that, he himself, said—Happy is it, rather to give than to receive!
texts.act.20.36: And, these things saying, kneeling down with them all, he prayed.
texts.act.20.37: And they all wept much, and, falling upon Paul’s neck, they were tenderly kissing him;
texts.act.20.38: being most distressed for the word which he had said,—That, no more, should they, his face, behold. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
texts.act.21.1: And it came to pass, when we set sail, having torn ourselves from them, running a straight course, we came unto Cos, and, on the next day, unto Rhodes,—and from thence unto Patara;
texts.act.21.2: and, finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, going on board, we set sail.
texts.act.21.3: And, sighting Cyprus, and leaving it behind to the left, we held on our voyage to Syria, and landed at Tyre; for, there, the ship was to discharge her cargo.
texts.act.21.4: And, finding up the disciples, we remained there seven days, and they, unto Paul, began to say, through the Spirit, that he would gain no footing in Jerusalem.
texts.act.21.5: And, when it came to pass that we had completed the days, we went forth, and continued our journey, all of them accompanying us, with wives and children, as far as outside the city; and, kneeling down on the beach in prayer,
texts.act.21.6: we tare ourselves from each other, and we went on board the ship, while, they, returned unto their homes.
texts.act.21.7: And, we, finishing the voyage from Tyre, reached Ptolemais, and, saluting the brethren, abode one day with them;
texts.act.21.8: and, on the morrow departing, we came to Caesarea, and, entering into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was of the seven, we abode with him.
texts.act.21.9: Now—this man, had four virgin daughters, who used to prophesy.
texts.act.21.10: And, as we stayed on many days, there came down a certain man from Judaea, a prophet, by name Agabus;
texts.act.21.11: and, coming unto us, and taking Paul’s girdle, he bound his own feet and hands, and said—Thus, saith the Holy Spirit, the man whose this girdle is, shall the Jews thus bind in Jerusalem, and deliver up into the hands of Gentiles.
texts.act.21.12: And, when we heard these things, both, we, and they of the place began beseeching him, not to go up unto Jerusalem.
texts.act.21.13: Then, answered Paul—What are ye doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For, I, not only to be bound, but to die in Jerusalem, am ready, in behalf of the name of the Lord Jesus.
texts.act.21.14: And, as he was not to be persuaded, we ceased, saying—the Lord’s, will be done!
texts.act.21.15: And, after these days, making ready what we had, we started to go up unto Jerusalem;
texts.act.21.16: and there went certain also of the disciples from Caesarea, along with us, who were to introduce us unto one with whom we might be entertained, one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple.
texts.act.21.17: Now, when we came to Jerusalem, the brethren, gladly welcomed us.
texts.act.21.18: And, on the next day, Paul went in with us unto James, and, all the elders, were present.
texts.act.21.19: And, saluting them, he went on to narrate, one by one, each of the things which God had wrought among the nations through his ministry.
texts.act.21.20: And, they, having heard, began glorifying God; and they said to him—Thou observest, brother, how many myriads there are among the Jews who have believed, and, all, are zealous for the law.
texts.act.21.21: Now they have heard it rumoured concerning thee, that, an apostacy, art thou teaching, from Moses, unto all the Jews, who are among the nations, telling them not to be circumcising their children, nor, by the customs, to be walking.
texts.act.21.22: What, then, is it? at all events, they will hear that thou hast come.
texts.act.21.23: This, then, do, which unto thee, we say:—We have four men who have a vow upon themselves.
texts.act.21.24: Taking these unto thee, be purified with them, and spend something upon them, that they may shave their head; and all will get to know, that the things which they have heard rumoured concerning thee, are, nothing,—on the contrary, thou thyself, dost keep the ranks, guarding the law.
texts.act.21.25: But, concerning them of the nations who have believed, we ourselves, sent, deciding that they should be guarding themselves, both as to idol sacrifice, and blood, and what is strangled, and fornication.
texts.act.21.26: Then Paul, taking unto him the men, on the next day, with them, being purified, began entering into the temple to declare the filling up of the days of the purification—until, the offering, had been presented for each one of them.
texts.act.21.27: When, however, the seven days were on the point of being concluded, the Jews from Asia, observing him in the temple, began to urge-on all the multitude, and thrust upon them their hands,
texts.act.21.28: crying out—Israelites! be giving help! This, is the man who, against the people, and the law, and this place, is teaching, all men everywhere; furthermore, even Greeks, hath he brought into the temple, and hath profaned this holy place.
texts.act.21.29: For they had before seen Trophimus, the Ephesian, in the city along with him, whom they were supposing, Paul, had brought, into the temple.
texts.act.21.30: And the whole city was set in motion, and there took place a running together of the people, and, laying hold of Paul, they proceeded to drag him outside the temple, and, straightway, the doors were made fast.
texts.act.21.31: When, also, they were seeking to slay him, there was carried up information, unto the captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in confusion:—
texts.act.21.32: who, instantly taking unto him soldiers and centurions, ran down upon them; and, they, seeing the captain and the soldiers, left off striking Paul.
texts.act.21.33: Then, the captain, drawing near, laid hold of him, and ordered him to be bound with two chains,—and began to enquire, who he might be, and what he had done;
texts.act.21.34: but, others, were calling out, something else, in the multitude; and so, as he could not get to know the certainty, because of the tumult, he ordered him to be brought into the castle.
texts.act.21.35: And, when he came unto the stairs, so it was that he was borne along by the soldiers, because of the force of the multitude;
texts.act.21.36: for the throng of the people was following, crying out—Away with him!
texts.act.21.37: But, when he was on the point of being taken into the castle, Paul saith unto the captain—Is it allowed me, to say somewhat unto thee? And he said—With Greek, art thou acquainted?
texts.act.21.38: Not, then, art, thou, the Egyptian, who, before these days, stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four-thousand men of the Assassins?
texts.act.21.39: And Paul said—I, indeed, am a Jew, of Tarsus in Cilicia,—a citizen, of no obscure city; but I beseech thee, give me leave to speak unto the people!
texts.act.21.40: And, when he had given leave, Paul, standing upon the stairs, waved with his hand unto the people; and, when great silence was secured, he addressed them in the Hebrew language, saying—
texts.act.22.1: Brethren and fathers! Hear ye, the defence, which I now make unto you:—
texts.act.22.2: And, when they heard that, in the Hebrew language, he had begun to address them, they kept the more quiet. And he saith—
texts.act.22.3: I, am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but nurtured in this city, at the feet of Gamaliel,—trained after the strictness of our ancestral law; being jealous for God just as, all ye, are this day;
texts.act.22.4: and, this way, I persecuted unto the death, binding and delivering up into prisons both men and women:—
texts.act.22.5: as, even the High-priest, beareth me witness, and all the Eldership,—from whom, letters also, accepting to the brethren, unto Damascus, was I journeying, to bring them who were there bound unto Jerusalem, that they might be punished.
texts.act.22.6: But it befell me, as I was journeying and drawing nigh unto Damascus, that, about mid-day—suddenly—out of heaven, there flashed a great light all around me;
texts.act.22.7: I fell also to the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me—Saul! Saul! Why, me, art thou persecuting?
texts.act.22.8: And, I, answered—Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me—I, am Jesus the Nazarene, whom, thou, art persecuting!
texts.act.22.9: Now, they who were with me, beheld, indeed, the light, but heard not, the voice, of him that was speaking with me
texts.act.22.10: And said—What shall I do, Lord? And, the Lord, said unto me—Arise, and be going thy way into Damascus, and, there, shall it be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.
texts.act.22.11: But, as I could not see clearly owing to the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them who were with me, I came into Damascus.
texts.act.22.12: And, one Ananias, a man devout according to the law, well-attested by all the Jews that dwelt there,
texts.act.22.13: coming unto me, and standing over me, said—Saul, brother! look up. And, I, in that very hour, looked up on him.
texts.act.22.14: And he said—The God of our fathers, hath chosen thee to get to know his will, and to see the Righteous One,—and to hear a voice out of his mouth.
texts.act.22.15: Because thou shalt be a witness to him unto all men, of the things which thou hast seen and heard.
texts.act.22.16: And, now, what art thou going to do? Arise, and get thyself immersed, and have thy sins bathed away, calling upon his name.
texts.act.22.17: And it came to pass, when had returned unto Jerusalem, and was praying in the temple, that I came to be in a trance,
texts.act.22.18: and saw him, saying unto me—Haste thee, and go forth speedily out of Jerusalem, inasmuch as they will not accept thy witness concerning me.
texts.act.22.19: And, I, said—Lord! they themselves, well know that I was imprisoning and beating in every synagogue them who were believing on thee.
texts.act.22.20: And, when the blood of Stephen thy witness was being shed, even I myself, was standing by, and approving, and guarding the mantles of them who were slaying him.
texts.act.22.21: And he said unto me—Be taking thy journey; because, I, unto nations afar off, will send thee.
texts.act.22.22: And they hearkened unto him as far as this word, and lifted up their voice, saying—Away from the earth, with such a man as this, for it is not fit that he should live.
texts.act.22.23: Now, as they were both making an outcry and tearing their mantles,—dust, also were throwing into the air,
texts.act.22.24: the captain ordered him to be brought into the castle, saying, that, with scourging, he should be put to the test,—that he might find out, for what cause they were, thus, clamouring against him.
texts.act.22.25: But, when they had stretched him out with straps, Paul said unto the by-standing centurion—A Roman, and uncondemned, is it allowed you to be scourging?
texts.act.22.26: And, when the centurion heard [that], he went unto the captain, and reported, saying—What art thou going to do? For, this man, is, a Roman?
texts.act.22.27: And the captain, coming up, said to him—Tell me! Art, thou, a, Roman? And, he, said—Yea!
texts.act.22.28: And the captain answered—I, for a large sum, this citizenship acquired! And, Paul, said—But, I, am even, [free-] born!
texts.act.22.29: Straightway, therefore, they who were about to put him to the test, withdrew from him; and, even the captain, was struck with fear, when he found out he was, a Roman, and because, him, he had bound.
texts.act.22.30: But, on the morrow, being minded to get to know the certainty as to why he was being accused by the Jews, he released him, and ordered the High-priests and all the High-council to come together; and, bringing down Paul, set him before them.
texts.act.23.1: And Paul, looking steadfastly, at the High-council, said—Brethren! I, in all good conscience have used my citizenship for God until this day.
texts.act.23.2: And, the High-priest, Ananias, ordered them that stood by him, to be smiting him on the mouth.
texts.act.23.3: Then, Paul, unto him, said—God is about to be smiting thee, thou whited wall! Dost, thou, then sit to judge me according to the law, and, unlawfully, orderest me to be smitten?
texts.act.23.4: And, they who stood by, said—The High-priest of God, dost thou revile?
texts.act.23.5: And Paul said—I was not aware, brethren, that he was high-priest; because it is written—Of a ruler of thy people, shalt thou not speak injuriously.
texts.act.23.6: But Paul, getting to know that, the one part, were Sadducees and, the other, Pharisees, began to cry aloud in the council—Brethren! I, am, a Pharisee, son of Pharisees:—Concerning a hope, even of a rising again of the dead, am I to be judged.
texts.act.23.7: And, as this he was saying, there arose a dissension of the Pharisees and Sadducees; and rent asunder was the throng.
texts.act.23.8: For, Sadducees, say, there is no rising again, nor messenger, nor spirit, whereas, Pharisees, confess them both.
texts.act.23.9: And there arose a great outcry, and certain of the Scribes of the party of the Pharisees, standing up, began to strive, saying—Nothing bad, find we in this man;—but, if a spirit hath spoken unto him, or a messenger…
texts.act.23.10: And, great dissension arising, the captain, fearing lest Paul would be torn in pieces by them, ordered the troop to go down, and take him by force out of their midst, to bring him into the castle.
texts.act.23.11: But, on the following night, the Lord, standing over him, said—Be of good courage! for, as thou hast fully borne witness of the things concerning me in Jerusalem, so must thou, in Rome also, bear witness.
texts.act.23.12: And, when it became day, the Jews, forming a conspiracy, bound themselves under a curse, saying, that they would neither eat nor drink till they had slain Paul.
texts.act.23.13: And they were, more than forty, who, this sworn-confederacy, had formed.
texts.act.23.14: And they went unto the High-priests and Elders, and said—With a curse have we bound ourselves, to taste, nothing, until we have slain Paul.
texts.act.23.15: Now, therefore, do, ye, with the High-council, make it appear unto the captain, that he should bring him down unto you, as though about to ascertain more exactly the things that concern him; and, we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
texts.act.23.16: But Paul’s sister’s son hearing of the lying-in-wait, happening to be near, and coming into the castle,—reported it unto Paul.
texts.act.23.17: And Paul, calling unto him one of the centurions, said—This young man, lead thou away unto the captain, for he hath somewhat to report unto him.
texts.act.23.18: He, therefore, taking him with him, brought him unto the captain, and saith—The prisoner Paul, calling me unto him, requested me to bring this young man unto thee, as having somewhat to tell thee.
texts.act.23.19: And the captain, taking him by the hand, and going aside, began, privately, to ask—What is it which thou hast to report unto me?
texts.act.23.20: And he said—The Jews, have agreed to request thee, that, to-morrow, thou wouldst bring, Paul, down into the High-council, as though about to ascertain something, more exact, concerning him.
texts.act.23.21: Thou, therefore, do not be persuaded by them, for there are lying in wait for him, from among them, more than forty men,—who, indeed, have bound themselves under a curse, neither to eat nor drink, till they have killed him; and, now, are they ready, awaiting the promise, from thee.
texts.act.23.22: the captain, therefore, dismissed the young man, charging him—Unto no one, divulge thou, that, these things, thou hast shewed unto me.
texts.act.23.23: And calling certain two of the centurions he said—Make ye ready two hundred soldiers, that they may journey as far as Caesarea,—and seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen, by the third hour of the night;
texts.act.23.24: beasts also provide, in order that, seating Paul thereon, they may bring him safely through unto Felix the governor.
texts.act.23.25: And he wrote a letter, after this form:—
texts.act.23.26: Claudius Lysias, unto the most excellent governor Felix, Joy!
texts.act.23.27: This man, having been apprehended by the Jews, and being about to be killed by them, I went down with the troop, and rescued; having learned that he was, a Roman.
texts.act.23.28: And, being minded to find out the cause for which they were accusing him, [I took him down into their High-council],
texts.act.23.29: whom I found to be accused concerning questions of their law, but, of nothing worthy of death or bonds, to be charged.
texts.act.23.30: But, when I was informed there would be a plot against the man, forthwith, I sent him unto thee, charging, his accusers also, to be speaking against him before thee.
texts.act.23.31: So the soldiers, according to their orders, taking up Paul, brought him by night unto Antipatris;
texts.act.23.32: and, on the morrow, leaving the horsemen to go on with him, returned to the castle,—
texts.act.23.33: and the others, entering into Caesarea, and delivering the letter unto the governor, set, Paul also, before him.
texts.act.23.34: And, when he had read it, and asked out of what province he was, and learned that he was from Cilicia,
texts.act.23.35: I myself will hear thee in full, said he, whensoever, thine accusers also, are come; and gave orders that, in the palace of Herod, he should be kept under guard.
texts.act.24.1: And, after five days, came down the High-priest Ananias, with certain Elders and a certain orator Tertullus, and they informed the governor against Paul.
texts.act.24.2: And, when he was called, Tertullus began to make accusation, saying—Seeing that, great peace, we are obtaining through thee, and that, reforms, are being brought about for this nation through thy forethought,
texts.act.24.3: both in all ways and in all places, are we accepting it, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
texts.act.24.4: But, lest I too long detain thee, I beseech thee to hear us concisely in thy considerateness.
texts.act.24.5: For, finding this man a pest, and moving sedition with all the Jews that are throughout the inhabited earth, a leader also of the sect of the Nazarenes,—
texts.act.24.6: who also attempted to desecrate even, the temple, whom we also seized,
texts.act.24.8: from whom thou shall be able, thyself, by making examination concerning all these things, to ascertain the things of which, we, are accusing him.
texts.act.24.9: Moreover, the Jews also were joining in the attack, saying that, these things, were, so.
texts.act.24.10: And Paul answered, when the governor had motioned him to be speaking,—Well knowing thee to have been, for many years, judge unto his nation, cheerfully, as to the things concerning myself, do I make defence;
texts.act.24.11: seeing thou art able to ascertain, that there are, not more, than twelve days, since I went up to worship in Jerusalem,—
texts.act.24.12: and neither, in the temple, found they me, with any one, disputing, or causing, a halt, of the multitude, either in the synagogues or throughout the city,—
texts.act.24.13: neither can they make good the things concerning which they are, now, accusing me.
texts.act.24.14: But I confess, this, unto thee,—That, according to the Way which they call a Sect, so, I am rendering divine service unto my father’s God, believing in all the things which, throughout the law, and those which, in the prophets, are written:
texts.act.24.15: Having, hope, towards God, which, even these themselves, do entertain—that, a resurrection, there shall certainly be, both of righteous and of unrighteous:
texts.act.24.16: herein, even I, myself, am studying to have, an unoffending conscience, towards God and men, continually.
texts.act.24.17: Now, after many years, intending to do, alms, unto my nation, I arrived,—also [to present] offerings; among which they found me, purified in the temple, not with a multitude, nor with tumult;
texts.act.24.18: but certain Jews from Asia [caused it],—
texts.act.24.19: who ought, before thee, to have presented themselves, and to have been laying accusation, if, anything, they might have had against me:—
texts.act.24.20: Or, let, these themselves, say what wrong they found, when I stood before the High-council,—
texts.act.24.21: unless concerning this one voice, wherewith I cried aloud among them, as I stood—Concerning the raising of the dead, am, I, to be judged, this day, by you.
texts.act.24.22: And Felix deferred them, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way,—saying—As soon as, Lysias the captain, hath come down, I will give judgment as to your affairs,—
texts.act.24.23: giving orders unto the centurion, that he should be kept, and have a measure of liberty, and to be hindering, none, of his own from waiting upon him.
texts.act.24.24: And, after certain days, Felix having arrived, with Drusilla his own wife, who was, a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith, respecting Christ Jesus.
texts.act.24.25: And, as he was reasoning of righteousness, and self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix, becoming greatly afraid, answered—For the present, be going thy way, and, when I find an opportunity, I will send for thee,—
texts.act.24.26: at the same time, also hoping that, money, would be given him by Paul; wherefore also, the more frequently sending for him, he used to converse with him.
texts.act.24.27: When, however, two years, were completed, Felix, was succeeded, by Porcius Festus, and Felix, wishing to gain favour with the Jews, left Paul bound.
texts.act.25.1: Festus, therefore, having come upon the province, after three days, went up unto Jerusalem from Caesarea;
texts.act.25.2: and the High-priest and chiefs of the Jews laid information before him against Paul, and began to beseech him
texts.act.25.3: asking for themselves as a favour against him, that he would send for him unto Jerusalem,—making, an ambush, to kill him on the way.
texts.act.25.4: Festus, therefore, answered, that Paul should be kept in Caesarea, and that, he himself, was about, shortly, to be going out [thither].
texts.act.25.5: They, therefore, among you (saith he) who are in power, let them go down with me; and, if there is in the man, anything amiss, let them accuse him.
texts.act.25.6: And, spending among them, not more than eight or ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and, on the morrow, taking his place upon the judgment-seat, ordered Paul to be brought.
texts.act.25.7: And, when he presented himself, the Jews who, from Jerusalem, had come down, stood round about him, many and grievous charges, bringing against [him], which they were not able to prove,—
texts.act.25.8: Paul saying in defence—Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I in anything sinned.
texts.act.25.9: But, Festus, wishing, with the Jews, to gain, favour, answered Paul, and said—Art thou willing, unto Jerusalem, to go up, and, there, concerning these things, be judged before me?
texts.act.25.10: But Paul said—Standing before the judgment-seat of Caesar, am I, where, I, ought to be judged. Unto the Jews, have I done no wrong, as, even thou, right well, art discovering.
texts.act.25.11: If then, on the one hand, I am doing wrong, and, anything worthy of death, have committed, I excuse not myself from dying; but, on the other hand, if there is, nothing, in the things whereof these are accusing me, no man, hath power to give, me, unto them as a favour:—Unto Caesar, I appeal!
texts.act.25.12: Then Festus, having conversed with the council, answered—Unto Caesar, hast thou appealed? Unto Caesar, shalt thou go.
texts.act.25.13: And, some days having gone by, Agrippa the king and Bernice came down to Caesarea, to salute Festus.
texts.act.25.14: And, as they were spending more days there, Festus, repeated, unto the king, the things relating to Paul, saying—A certain man, hath been left behind by Felix, as a prisoner;
texts.act.25.15: concerning whom, when I happened to be in Jerusalem, the High-priests and the Elders of the Jews laid information, claiming against him a condemnation:
texts.act.25.16: unto whom made answer—That it is not a custom with Romans, to grant as a favour any man, before the accused, face to face, should have his accusers, and, opportunity of defence, should receive, concerning the charge.
texts.act.25.17: When, therefore, they had come together here, no delay whatever, making, on the next day, taking my place upon the judgment-seat, I ordered the man to be brought:
texts.act.25.18: Concerning whom, taking their stand, his accusers, no accusation at all, were bringing, of the evil things which, I, had been suspecting;
texts.act.25.19: but, certain questions concerning their own demon-worship, had they against him, and concerning one Jesus, who had died, whom Paul was affirming to be alive.
texts.act.25.20: And, I, being at a loss as to the inquiry into these things, was asking—whether he might be minded to go unto Jerusalem, and, there, be judged concerning these things.
texts.act.25.21: But, Paul, having appealed to be kept for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered him to be kept, until I could send him up unto Caesar.
texts.act.25.22: And, Agrippa, [said] unto Festus—I could wish, myself also, to hear, the man. To-morrow, (saith he) thou shalt hear him.
texts.act.25.23: On the morrow, therefore, when Agrippa had come, and Bernice, with great display, and they had entered into the audience-chamber, with the captains of thousands and men of distinction of the city,—and Festus had given orders, Paul was brought.
texts.act.25.24: And Festus saith—King Agrippa! and all ye men, here present with us: Ye observe this person, concerning whom, one and all the throng of the Jews, have interceded with me, both in Jerusalem and here, crying aloud that he ought not to be living any longer.
texts.act.25.25: But, I, gathered, that, nothing worthy of death, had he committed; and, this man himself, having appealed unto the Emperor, I decided to send him:—
texts.act.25.26: Concerning whom, anything certain to write unto my lord, I have not; wherefore, I have brought him forth before you,—and especially before thee, King Agrippa! in order that, after examination had, I might have something I could write;
texts.act.25.27: For, unreasonable, unto me, it seemeth, when sending a prisoner, not also, the accusations against him, to signify.
texts.act.26.1: And, Agrippa, to Paul, said—It is permitted thee, on thine own behalf, to be speaking. Then Paul, stretching forth his hand, went on to make his defence.
texts.act.26.2: Concerning all things of which I am accused by Jews, King Agrippa, I have been counting myself happy, that, before thee, am I about, this day, to be making my defence;
texts.act.26.3: especially, as thou art, well-versed, in all the Jewish customs and questions. Wherefore, I beseech thee, patiently, to hear me.
texts.act.26.4: My manner of life, then, from my youth, which, from its commencement, was formed among my nation, even in Jerusalem, know all Jews,
texts.act.26.5: inasmuch as they were aforetime observing me, from the outset,—if they please to bear witness,—that, according to the strictest sect of our own religion, I lived, a Pharisee.
texts.act.26.6: And, now, for the hope of the promise, unto our fathers, being brought to pass by God, am I standing to be judged,—
texts.act.26.7: unto which [hope], our twelve-tribed nation, with intensity, night and day, rendering divine service, is hoping to attain—concerning which hope, I am being accused by Jews, O King!
texts.act.26.8: What! incredible, is it judged with you, that, God the dead doth raise?
texts.act.26.9: I, therefore, imagined to myself, that, against the name of Jesus the Nazarene, it was needful, many hostile things, to bring about,—
texts.act.26.10: which also I did in Jerusalem, yea and, many of the saints, I myself, in prisons, shut up,—the authority, from the High-priests, having received: and, when they were to be put to death, I brought against them my vote;
texts.act.26.11: and, throughout all the synagogues, ofttimes punishing them, I would fain have compelled them to defame; and, being excessively maddened against them, I went on to pursue them as far as even the outlying cities.
texts.act.26.12: Among which things, being on a journey unto Damascus, with the authority and commission of the High-priests,
texts.act.26.13: at mid-day, on the road, I saw, O King, from heaven, above the splendour of the sun, shining around me, a light, and [around] them who, with me, were journeying;
texts.act.26.14: and, when we were all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice, saying unto me, in the Hebrew language—Saul! Saul! why, me, art thou persecuting? It is hard for thee, against goads, to be kicking!
texts.act.26.15: And, I, said—Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said—I, am Jesus, whom, thou, art persecuting!
texts.act.26.16: But rise and stand upon thy feet; for, to this end, have I appeared unto thee,—To appoint thee an attendant and a witness, both of the things as to which thou hast seen me, and of those as to which I will appear unto thee:
texts.act.26.17: Rescuing thee from among the people, and from among the nations, unto whom, I, am sending thee—
texts.act.26.18: To open their eyes; that they turn from darkness unto light, and the authority of Satan unto God, that they may receive remission of sins, and an inheritance among them who have been made holy by the faith respecting me.
texts.act.26.19: Wherefore, O King Agrippa,—I became not disobedient unto the heavenly vision;
texts.act.26.20: But—both to them in Damascus, first, and in Jerusalem, unto all the country of Judaea also, and unto the nations, I carried tidings—that they should repent, and turn unto God, and, works worthy of their repentance, should practise.
texts.act.26.21: Because of these things, Jews seized me in the temple, and were attempting to slay me with their own hands.
texts.act.26.22: So then, having met with, the help that is from God, until this day, do I stand, witnessing to both small and great, nothing else saying, than those things which both the prophets, and Moses, did say should certainly come to pass:—
texts.act.26.23: If, to suffer, the Christ was destined, if, the first of a resurrection of the dead, he is about to carry tidings, of light, both unto the people, and unto the nations.
texts.act.26.24: Now, as he was saying these things in his defence, Festus, with a loud voice, saith—Thou art raving, Paul! Thy great learning, is turning thee round unto, raving madness.
texts.act.26.25: But Paul—I am not raving (saith he), most noble Festus,—but, the declarations of truth and soberness, am I sounding forth:
texts.act.26.26: For well-knoweth, the king, concerning these things, unto whom, with boldness of utterance, am I speaking; for, that these things are not hidden from him, I am well persuaded,—for, not in a corner, hath this thing been done.
texts.act.26.27: Believest thou, King Agrippa, in the prophets? I know that thou believest!
texts.act.26.28: And, Agrippa, [said] unto Paul—Almost, art thou persuading, me, to become a, Christian!
texts.act.26.29: And, Paul, [answered] —I could pray unto God that, both almost and altogether, not only thou but all they who are hearing me this day, might become such,—as even, I, am, excepting these bonds.
texts.act.26.30: And the king rose up, and the governor, Bernice also, and they who had been sitting with them;
texts.act.26.31: And, retiring, they began conversing one with another, saying, Nothing worthy of death or of bonds, doth this man practise.
texts.act.26.32: And, Agrippa, unto Festus, said—This man might have been released, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.
texts.act.27.1: Now, when it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they proceeded to deliver Paul, and certain other prisoners, unto a centurion by name Julius, of an Augustan band.
texts.act.27.2: And, going on board a ship of Adramittium, about to sail unto the places along the coast of Asia, we put to sea, there being with us, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica;
texts.act.27.3: and, on the next day, we put into Zidon,—and Julius, treating Paul, kindly, gave him leave to go unto his friends and refresh himself;
texts.act.27.4: and, from thence putting out to sea, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary;
texts.act.27.5: and, sailing across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came down to Myra, a city of Lycia.
texts.act.27.6: And the centurion, there, finding a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, put us therein.
texts.act.27.7: And, for a good many days sailing slowly, and getting with difficulty over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us to get on, we sailed under the lee of Crete, over against Salmone;
texts.act.27.8: and, with difficulty coasting it, we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near to which was the city of Lasea.
texts.act.27.9: And, when a considerable time had passed, and sailing was already dangerous, because, even the Fast, had already gone by, Paul began to advise,
texts.act.27.10: saying to them—Sirs! I perceive that, with damage and great loss, not only of the cargo and of the ship, but even of our persons, shall the voyage certainly be attended.
texts.act.27.11: But, the centurion, by the master, and by the shipowner, was more persuaded than by the things which, by Paul, were spoken.
texts.act.27.12: And, the harbour being, incommodious, to winter in, the more part, advised to put to sea from thence, if by any means they might be able to reach Phoenix, to winter, [which was] a harbour of Crete, looking north-east and south-east.
texts.act.27.13: And, a south wind blowing softly, supposing they had secured their purpose, weighing anchor, they began to sail close in shore along Crete.
texts.act.27.14: But, after no long time, there beat down from it a tempestuous wind, called Euraquilo,—
texts.act.27.15: and, the ship being caught and we not being able to bring her head to the wind, we let her go, and were borne along.
texts.act.27.16: And, running under the lee, of some small island, called Cauda, we were able, with difficulty, to make ourselves masters of the boat,—
texts.act.27.17: which, hoisting up, they began to use, helps, under-girding the ship; and, fearing lest, on the sand-bank of Africa, they should run aground, lowering the gear, so, were they borne along.
texts.act.27.18: But, we being exceedingly tempest-tossed, on the next day, they began to throw [cargo] overboard;
texts.act.27.19: and, on the third day, with their own hands, the tackling of the ship, they cast away.
texts.act.27.20: And, neither, sun nor stars, appearing for many days, and, no small tempest, lying upon us, in the end, all hope that we should be saved, began to be taken from us.
texts.act.27.21: But, when they had been, long without food, then, Paul, standing in the midst of them, said—Ye ought, indeed, Sir! yielding to me, not to have sailed away from Crete, to get this damage and loss. …
texts.act.27.22: And, now, I recommend you to be of good courage; for, loss of life, shall there be, none at all, from among you,—only the ship.
texts.act.27.23: For there stood by me this night, belonging unto the God whose I am, unto whom also I am doing divine service, a messenger,
texts.act.27.24: saying—Be not afraid, Paul! for, before Caesar, must thou needs stand. And lo! God hath granted to thee as a favour, all them who are sailing with thee.
texts.act.27.25: Wherefore, be of good courage, Sirs; for I believe in God—that, so, it shall be, according as it hath been told me.
texts.act.27.26: Upon a certain island, however, must we needs be wrecked.
texts.act.27.27: And, when, the fourteenth night, had come, and we were being driven to and fro in the Adriatic, about midnight, the sailors suspected that some country was, nearing, them;
texts.act.27.28: and, sounding, they found twenty fathoms,—and, going a little further, and again sounding, they found fifteen fathoms.
texts.act.27.29: And, fearing lest haply, on rocky places, we should be wrecked, out of stern, cast they four anchors,—and began praying that day might dawn.
texts.act.27.30: But, when, the sailors, were seeking to flee out of the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea, by pretext, as though out of the prow they had been about to reach anchors,
texts.act.27.31: Paul said unto the centurion, and unto the soldiers—Except, these, abide in the ship, ye yourselves, cannot be saved!
texts.act.27.32: Then, the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
texts.act.27.33: And, until day was about to dawn, Paul continued to beseech one and all to take some food, saying—This day is, the fourteenth day, that, suspense, fasting, ye are completing,—having helped yourselves, to nothing.
texts.act.27.34: Wherefore, I beseech you to take some food,—for, this, lays a foundation for your safety; for, of no one of you, shall a hair of the head perish.
texts.act.27.35: And, having said these things, and taken a loaf, he gave thanks unto God before all, and, breaking it, began to eat.
texts.act.27.36: And, all becoming, of good cheer, they also, helped themselves to food.
texts.act.27.37: Now we were, in the ship, in all, about seventy-six souls.
texts.act.27.38: And, when they were satisfied with food, they began lightening the ship, casting out the wheat into the sea.
texts.act.27.39: And, when day came, they could not recognise, the land; but perceived, a certain bay, having a beach,—upon which they were minded, if they could, safely to bring the ship.
texts.act.27.40: And, casting off the anchors, they let them go into the sea,—at the same time, loosening the lashings of the rudders, and, hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.
texts.act.27.41: But, falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and, the foreship sticking fast, remained immoveable, while, the stern, began to break up, from the violence [of the waves].
texts.act.27.42: Now, the soldiers counsel, turned out to be, that they should kill, the prisoners, lest any one should swim out and escape;
texts.act.27.43: but, the centurion, being minded to bring Paul safely through, hindered them of their purpose, and ordered such as were able to swim, to cast themselves overboard and, get first to the land,—
texts.act.27.44: and, the rest, some, on planks, and, some, on other things from the ship, …and, so, it came to pass, that, all, were brought safely through, on to the land.
texts.act.28.1: And, when we were safely through, then, we knew that the island was called, Melita.
texts.act.28.2: And, the natives, began to shew us no common philanthropy; for, kindling a fire, they received us all, because of the rain that had set in, and because of the cold.
texts.act.28.3: But, when Paul had gathered a certain lot of firewood into a bundle, and laid it on the fire, a viper, by reason of the heat, coming forth, fastened on his hand.
texts.act.28.4: And, when the natives saw the brute hanging out from his hand, they began to say, one to another—Doubtless, this man is, a murderer, whom, though brought safely through out of the sea, Justice, hath not suffered, to live.
texts.act.28.5: He, however, shaking of the brute into the fire, suffered no harm;
texts.act.28.6: whereas, they, were expecting, that he was about to become inflamed, or to fall down suddenly dead;—but, when they had been long expecting, and had observed, nothing unusual, happening unto him, they changed their minds, and began to say he was a god.
texts.act.28.7: Now, in the neighbourhood of that place, were lands, belonging to the chief man of the island, by name Publius,—who, making us welcome, for three days, hospitably entertained us.
texts.act.28.8: And it so happened that, the father of Publius, with feverish heats and dysentery distressed, was lying prostrate: unto whom Paul entering in and praying, laid his hands on him, and healed him.
texts.act.28.9: And, when this happened, the rest also, even they in the island who were sick, were coming in and getting cured;
texts.act.28.10: who also, with many honours, honoured us, and, when we were about to sail, put on board such things as we might need.
texts.act.28.11: And, after three months, we sailed in a ship which had wintered in the island, [a ship] of Alexandria, whose ensign was The Twin Brothers;
texts.act.28.12: and, touching at Syracuse, we tarried three days;
texts.act.28.13: whence, going round, we reached Rhegium; and, after one day, a south wind springing up, on the second day, we came to Puteoli;
texts.act.28.14: where, finding brethren, we were entreated to tarry, with them, seven days;—and, thus, towards Rome, we came.
texts.act.28.15: And, when from thence the brethren heard the tidings concerning us, they came to meet us, as far as The Market of Appius and the Three Taverns—seeing whom, Paul thanked God, and took courage.
texts.act.28.16: And, when we entered into Rome, Paul was suffered to abide by himself, with the soldier that guarded him.
texts.act.28.17: And it came to pass, after three days, that he called together those who were the chief of the Jews; and, when they came together, he began to say unto them—I, brethren, though I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, as a prisoner, out of Jerusalem, was delivered into the hands of the Romans;
texts.act.28.18: who, indeed, when they had examined me, were minded to set me at liberty, because there was, nothing worthy of death, in me.
texts.act.28.19: But, as the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar,—not as though, against my nation, I had anything to bring by way of accusation.
texts.act.28.20: For this cause, therefore, have I called for you, to see and to speak with you; for, on account of the hope of Israel, this chain, have I about me!
texts.act.28.21: And, they, said unto him—We, have neither received letters concerning thee from the Jews, nor hath anyone of the brethren who hath arrived reported or spoken concerning thee, anything ill.
texts.act.28.22: But we deem it well, that, from thee, we should hear what are thine opinions; for, indeed, concerning this sect, it is, known to us, that, everywhere, is it spoken against.
texts.act.28.23: And, having arranged with him a day, there came unto him, to the lodging, a larger number; unto whom he proceeded to expound, bearing full witness as to the kingdom of God, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses, and from the prophets,—from morning till evening.
texts.act.28.24: And, some, indeed, were persuaded by the things that were spoken, whereas, others, disbelieved;
texts.act.28.25: and, not being, agreed, among themselves, they began to leave,—Paul having said one thing—Well, did, the Holy Spirit, speak through Isaiah the prophet, unto your fathers,
texts.act.28.26: saying—Go thy way unto this people, and say—Ye shall, surely hear, and yet will in nowise understand. And, surely see, and yet will in nowise perceive;
texts.act.28.27: For the heart of this people, hath become dense, and, with their ears, heavily, have they heard, and, their eyes, have they closed,—lest once they should see with their eyes, and, with their ears, should hear, and, with their hearts, should understand, and return,—when I would certainly heal them.
texts.act.28.28: Be it, known unto you, therefore, that, unto the nations, hath been sent forth this salvation of God: they, will also hear.
texts.act.28.30: And he abode two whole years in his own hired house, and made welcome all who were coming in unto him,—
texts.act.28.31: proclaiming the kingdom of God, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ, with all freedom of speech, without hindrance.

texts.act.1.1: El primer libro que escribí, Teófilo, trataba de todo lo que Jesús empezó a hacer y a enseñar,
texts.act.1.2: hasta el día en que fue recibido arriba, después de haber dado el mandato por medio del Espíritu Santo a los apóstoles que había elegido.
texts.act.1.3: A estos también se mostró vivo después de haber padecido, con muchas pruebas, apareciéndose a ellos durante cuarenta días y hablando del Reino de Dios.
texts.act.1.4: Estando reunido con ellos, les ordenó: «No os vayáis de Jerusalén, sino esperad la promesa del Padre, que habéis oído de mí.
texts.act.1.5: Porque Juan ciertamente bautizó en agua, pero vosotros seréis bautizados en el Espíritu Santo dentro de no muchos días.»
texts.act.1.6: Por eso, cuando se reunieron, le preguntaron: «Señor, ¿restauras ahora el reino a Israel?».
texts.act.1.7: Les dijo: «No os corresponde a vosotros conocer los tiempos o las épocas que el Padre ha fijado con su propia autoridad.
texts.act.1.8: Pero recibiréis poder cuando el Espíritu Santo haya venido sobre vosotros. Seréis testigos de mí en Jerusalén, en toda Judea y Samaria, y hasta los confines de la tierra.»
texts.act.1.9: Cuando dijo estas cosas, mientras ellos miraban, fue alzado, y una nube lo recibió fuera de su vista.
texts.act.1.10: Mientras ellos miraban fijamente al cielo mientras él se iba, he aquí que se pusieron junto a ellos dos hombres vestidos de blanco,
texts.act.1.11: que también dijeron: «Hombres de Galilea, ¿por qué estáis mirando al cielo? Este Jesús, que ha sido recibido de entre vosotros en el cielo, volverá de la misma manera que le habéis visto subir al cielo.»
texts.act.1.12: Luego volvieron a Jerusalén desde el monte llamado del Olivar, que está cerca de Jerusalén, a un día de camino.
texts.act.1.13: Cuando llegaron, subieron al aposento alto donde se alojaban, es decir, Pedro, Juan, Santiago, Andrés, Felipe, Tomás, Bartolomé, Mateo, Santiago hijo de Alfeo, Simón el Zelote y Judas hijo de Santiago.
texts.act.1.14: Todos ellos perseveraban unánimemente en la oración y la súplica, junto con las mujeres y María, la madre de Jesús, y con sus hermanos.
texts.act.1.15: En estos días, Pedro se levantó en medio de los discípulos (y el número de personas reunidas era de unas ciento veinte), y dijo:
texts.act.1.16: “Hermanos, era necesario que se cumpliera esta Escritura que el Espíritu Santo habló antes por boca de David acerca de Judas, que fue guía de los que prendieron a Jesús.
texts.act.1.17: Porque fue contado con nosotros, y recibió su parte en este ministerio.
texts.act.1.18: Este hombre obtuvo un campo con la recompensa de su maldad; y cayendo de cabeza, su cuerpo se reventó y todas sus entrañas se derramaron.
texts.act.1.19: Todos los que vivían en Jerusalén supieron que aquel campo se llamaba en su lengua «Acéldama», es decir, «El campo de sangre».
texts.act.1.20: Porque está escrito en el libro de los Salmos: ‘Que su morada quede desolada’. Que nadie habite en ella”. y, ‘Que otro tome su cargo’.
texts.act.1.21: «Es necesario, pues, que de los hombres que nos han acompañado todo el tiempo que el Señor Jesús entró y salió de entre nosotros,
texts.act.1.22: comenzando por el bautismo de Juan hasta el día en que fue recibido de entre nosotros, uno de ellos sea testigo con nosotros de su resurrección.»
texts.act.1.23: Propusieron a dos: a José, llamado Barsabás, que también se llamaba Justo, y a Matías.
texts.act.1.24: Oraron y dijeron: «Tú, Señor, que conoces el corazón de todos los hombres, muestra a cuál de estos dos has elegido
texts.act.1.25: para que tome parte en este ministerio y apostolado del que Judas se apartó, para ir a su propio lugar.»
texts.act.1.26: Lo echaron a suertes, y la suerte recayó en Matías; y fue contado con los once apóstoles.
texts.act.2.1: Al llegar el día de Pentecostés, estaban todos reunidos en un mismo lugar.
texts.act.2.2: De repente, vino del cielo un ruido como el de un viento impetuoso, que llenó toda la casa donde estaban sentados.
texts.act.2.3: Aparecieron unas lenguas como de fuego que se repartieron entre ellos, y una se posó sobre cada uno de ellos.
texts.act.2.4: Todos fueron llenos del Espíritu Santo y comenzaron a hablar en otras lenguas, según el Espíritu les daba la capacidad de hablar.
texts.act.2.5: En Jerusalén vivían judíos, hombres devotos, de todas las naciones bajo el cielo.
texts.act.2.6: Al oír este ruido, la multitud se reunió y quedó desconcertada, porque cada uno les oía hablar en su propia lengua.
texts.act.2.7: Todos se asombraron y se maravillaron, diciéndose unos a otros: «Mirad, ¿no son galileos todos estos que hablan?
texts.act.2.8: ¿Cómo oímos nosotros, cada uno en nuestra propia lengua?
texts.act.2.9: Partos, medos, elamitas y gentes de Mesopotamia, de Judea, de Capadocia, del Ponto, de Asia,
texts.act.2.10: de Frigia, de Panfilia, de Egipto, de las partes de Libia en torno a Cirene, visitantes de Roma, tanto judíos como prosélitos,
texts.act.2.11: cretenses y árabes: ¡les oímos hablar en nuestras lenguas de las maravillas de Dios!»
texts.act.2.12: Todos estaban asombrados y perplejos, diciéndose unos a otros: «¿Qué significa esto?»
texts.act.2.13: Otros, burlándose, decían: «Están llenos de mosto».
texts.act.2.14: Pero Pedro, poniéndose en pie con los once, alzó la voz y les dijo: “Hombres de Judea y todos los que habitáis en Jerusalén, sabed esto y escuchad mis palabras.
texts.act.2.15: Porque estos no están borrachos, como suponéis, ya que solo es la hora tercia del día.
texts.act.2.16: Pero esto es lo que se ha dicho por medio del profeta Joel:
texts.act.2.17: ‘Sucederá en los últimos días, dice Dios, que derramaré mi Espíritu sobre toda carne. Vuestros hijos y vuestras hijas profetizarán. Vuestros jóvenes verán visiones. Vuestros ancianos soñarán sueños.
texts.act.2.18: Sí, y sobre mis siervos y mis siervas en aquellos días, derramaré mi Espíritu, y ellos profetizarán.
texts.act.2.19: Mostraré maravillas en el cielo arriba, y señales en la tierra abajo: sangre, y fuego, y vapor de humo.
texts.act.2.20: El sol se convertirá en tinieblas, y la luna en sangre, antes de que llegue el día del Señor, grande y glorioso.
texts.act.2.21: Y todo el que invoque el nombre del Señor se salvará’.
texts.act.2.22: “¡Hombres de Israel, escuchad estas palabras! Jesús de Nazaret, varón aprobado por Dios ante vosotros con las obras poderosas, prodigios y señales que Dios hizo por medio de él entre vosotros, como vosotros mismos sabéis;
texts.act.2.23: a este, entregado por el consejo determinado y la presciencia de Dios, le prendisteis y matasteis por manos de inicuos, crucificándole;
texts.act.2.24: a quien Dios resucitó, habiéndole librado de los dolores de la muerte, porque no era posible que fuera retenido por ella.
texts.act.2.25: Porque David dice acerca de él: ‘Veía al Señor siempre delante de mi rostro, porque él está a mi diestra, para que no sea conmovido.
texts.act.2.26: Por eso mi corazón se alegró y mi lengua se regocijó. Además, mi carne también descansará en esperanza,
texts.act.2.27: porque no dejarás mi alma en el Hades, ni permitirás que tu Santo vea corrupción.
texts.act.2.28: Me diste a conocer los caminos de la vida. Me llenarás de alegría con tu presencia.’
texts.act.2.29: “Hermanos, os puedo decir libremente del patriarca David, que murió y fue sepultado, y su sepulcro está con nosotros hasta el día de hoy.
texts.act.2.30: Por eso, siendo profeta y sabiendo que Dios le había jurado que del fruto de sus lomos, según la carne, levantaría al Cristo para que se sentara en su trono,
texts.act.2.31: previendo esto, habló de la resurrección del Cristo, que su alma no fue dejada en el Hades ni su carne vio corrupción.
texts.act.2.32: A este Jesús lo resucitó Dios, de lo cual todos nosotros somos testigos.
texts.act.2.33: Siendo, pues, exaltado a la diestra de Dios, y habiendo recibido del Padre la promesa del Espíritu Santo, ha derramado esto que vosotros ahora veis y oís.
texts.act.2.34: Porque David no subió a los cielos, sino que él mismo dice: ‘Dijo el Señor a mi Señor: Siéntate a mi diestra,
texts.act.2.35: hasta que ponga a tus enemigos por estrado de tus pies.’
texts.act.2.36: «Sepa, pues, ciertísimamente toda la casa de Israel que Dios ha hecho Señor y Cristo a este Jesús a quien vosotros crucificasteis.»
texts.act.2.37: Al oír esto, se compungieron de corazón y dijeron a Pedro y a los demás apóstoles: «Hermanos, ¿qué haremos?»
texts.act.2.38: Pedro les dijo: «Arrepentíos y bautizaos cada uno de vosotros en el nombre de Jesucristo para el perdón de los pecados, y recibiréis el don del Espíritu Santo.
texts.act.2.39: Porque la promesa es para vosotros y para vuestros hijos, y para todos los que están lejos, para cuantos el Señor nuestro Dios llame.»
texts.act.2.40: Con muchas otras palabras les testificaba y exhortaba, diciendo: «¡Salvaos de esta perversa generación!»
texts.act.2.41: Entonces los que recibieron con gusto su palabra fueron bautizados, y aquel día se añadieron unas tres mil almas.
texts.act.2.42: Y perseveraban en la enseñanza de los apóstoles, en la comunión, en el partimiento del pan y en las oraciones.
texts.act.2.43: El temor se apoderaba de todos, y se hacían muchos prodigios y señales por medio de los apóstoles.
texts.act.2.44: Todos los que creían estaban juntos y tenían todo en común;
texts.act.2.45: vendían sus propiedades y bienes, y los repartían a todos, según la necesidad de cada uno.
texts.act.2.46: Perseverando unánimes cada día en el templo y partiendo el pan en las casas, tomaban el alimento con alegría y sencillez de corazón,
texts.act.2.47: alabando a Dios y gozando del favor de todo el pueblo. Y el Señor añadía cada día a la iglesia a los que habían de ser salvos.
texts.act.3.1: Pedro y Juan subían al templo a la hora de la oración, la hora novena.
texts.act.3.2: Y traían a un hombre cojo desde el vientre de su madre, al que ponían cada día a la puerta del templo que se llama la Hermosa, para pedir limosna a los que entraban en el templo.
texts.act.3.3: Este, viendo a Pedro y a Juan a punto de entrar en el templo, les rogaba que le diesen limosna.
texts.act.3.4: Pedro, fijando sus ojos en él, junto con Juan, le dijo: «Míranos».
texts.act.3.5: Él les prestó atención, esperando recibir algo de ellos.
texts.act.3.6: Pero Pedro dijo: «No tengo plata ni oro, pero lo que tengo, te lo doy. En el nombre de Jesucristo de Nazaret, levántate y anda».
texts.act.3.7: Lo tomó de la mano derecha y lo levantó. Al instante, sus pies y tobillos cobraron fuerza.
texts.act.3.8: Y saltando, se puso en pie y comenzó a caminar. Entró con ellos en el templo, andando, saltando y alabando a Dios.
texts.act.3.9: Todo el pueblo lo vio caminar y alabar a Dios.
texts.act.3.10: Y reconocían que era el mismo que solía sentarse a pedir limosna a la puerta del templo, la Hermosa. Se llenaron de asombro y admiración por lo que le había sucedido.
texts.act.3.11: Mientras el cojo que había sido curado se aferraba a Pedro y a Juan, todo el pueblo corría atónito hacia ellos en el pórtico que se llama de Salomón.
texts.act.3.12: Al ver esto, Pedro respondió al pueblo: “Varones israelitas, ¿por qué os maravilláis de esto? ¿Por qué fijáis vuestros ojos en nosotros, como si por nuestro propio poder o piedad le hubiéramos hecho caminar?
texts.act.3.13: El Dios de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob, el Dios de nuestros padres, ha glorificado a su Siervo Jesús, a quien vosotros entregasteis y negasteis en presencia de Pilato, cuando este había decidido liberarle.
texts.act.3.14: Pero vosotros negasteis al Santo y Justo, y pedisteis que se os concediera un homicida,
texts.act.3.15: y matasteis al Autor de la vida, a quien Dios resucitó de entre los muertos, de lo cual nosotros somos testigos.
texts.act.3.16: Por la fe en su nombre, es su nombre lo que ha fortalecido a este hombre que veis y conocéis. Sí, la fe que es por medio de él le ha dado esta perfecta sanidad en presencia de todos vosotros.
texts.act.3.17: “Ahora bien, hermanos, sé que lo hicisteis por ignorancia, como también lo hicieron vuestros gobernantes.
texts.act.3.18: Pero Dios cumplió así lo que había anunciado de antemano por boca de todos sus profetas, que su Cristo había de padecer.
texts.act.3.19: “Así que, arrepentíos y convertíos, para que sean borrados vuestros pecados; para que vengan tiempos de refrigerio de la presencia del Señor,
texts.act.3.20: y envíe a Jesucristo, que os fue anunciado de antemano,
texts.act.3.21: a quien el cielo debe recibir hasta los tiempos de la restauración de todas las cosas, de las que Dios habló hace mucho tiempo por boca de sus santos profetas.
texts.act.3.22: En efecto, Moisés dijo a los padres: ‘El Señor vuestro Dios os levantará un profeta de entre vuestros hermanos, como yo; a él escucharéis en todo lo que os diga.
texts.act.3.23: Y sucederá que toda persona que no escuche a ese profeta será totalmente exterminada de entre el pueblo’.
texts.act.3.24: Y todos los profetas, desde Samuel en adelante, todos los que han hablado, también anunciaron estos días.
texts.act.3.25: Vosotros sois los hijos de los profetas y del pacto que Dios hizo con nuestros padres, diciendo a Abraham: ‘En tu simiente serán bendecidas todas las familias de la tierra’.
texts.act.3.26: Dios, habiendo resucitado a su Siervo Jesús, os lo envió primero para bendeciros, a fin de que cada uno de vosotros se aparte de sus maldades.”
texts.act.4.1: Mientras ellos hablaban al pueblo, se presentaron los sacerdotes, el jefe de la guardia del templo y los saduceos,
texts.act.4.2: muy indignados porque enseñaban al pueblo y proclamaban en Jesús la resurrección de entre los muertos.
texts.act.4.3: Les echaron mano y los pusieron bajo custodia hasta el día siguiente, pues ya era de noche.
texts.act.4.4: Pero muchos de los que oyeron la palabra creyeron, y el número de los hombres llegó a ser como de cinco mil.
texts.act.4.5: Al día siguiente, se reunieron en Jerusalén sus gobernantes, los ancianos y los escribas.
texts.act.4.6: Estaba allí el sumo sacerdote Anás, junto con Caifás, Juan, Alejandro y todos los de la familia del sumo sacerdote.
texts.act.4.7: Y poniéndoles en medio, les preguntaron: «¿Con qué poder o en qué nombre habéis hecho vosotros esto?»
texts.act.4.8: Entonces Pedro, lleno del Espíritu Santo, les dijo: “Gobernantes del pueblo y ancianos de Israel:
texts.act.4.9: Si hoy se nos interroga acerca del beneficio hecho a un hombre enfermo, de cómo este ha sido curado,
texts.act.4.10: sea notorio a todos vosotros y a todo el pueblo de Israel, que en el nombre de Jesucristo de Nazaret, a quien vosotros crucificasteis y a quien Dios resucitó de entre los muertos, por él este hombre está aquí delante de vosotros sano.
texts.act.4.11: Este Jesús es ‘la piedra que vosotros, los constructores, desechasteis, la cual se ha convertido en la piedra angular’.
texts.act.4.12: Y en ningún otro hay salvación, porque no hay bajo el cielo otro nombre dado a los hombres en el que podamos ser salvos.”
texts.act.4.13: Al ver la intrepidez de Pedro y de Juan, y percatándose de que eran hombres sin letras y del vulgo, se maravillaban. Y reconocían que habían estado con Jesús.
texts.act.4.14: Y viendo de pie junto a ellos al hombre que había sido sanado, no podían decir nada en contra.
texts.act.4.15: Entonces les ordenaron que salieran del sanedrín, y consultaban entre sí,
texts.act.4.16: diciendo: «¿Qué haremos con estos hombres? Porque ciertamente es evidente para todos los que habitan en Jerusalén que un milagro notable se ha realizado por medio de ellos, y no podemos negarlo.
texts.act.4.17: Pero para que no se divulgue más entre el pueblo, amenacémosles severamente, para que de ahora en adelante no hablen a nadie en este nombre.»
texts.act.4.18: Los llamaron y les ordenaron que en ninguna manera hablaran ni enseñaran en el nombre de Jesús.
texts.act.4.19: Pero Pedro y Juan les respondieron diciendo: «Juzgad si es justo a los ojos de Dios obedeceros a vosotros antes que a Dios;
texts.act.4.20: porque nosotros no podemos dejar de decir lo que hemos visto y oído.»
texts.act.4.21: Ellos, tras amenazarles de nuevo, los dejaron ir, al no hallar la manera de castigarlos, por causa del pueblo; porque todos glorificaban a Dios por lo que se había hecho.
texts.act.4.22: Pues el hombre en el cual se había realizado este milagro de sanidad tenía más de cuarenta años.
texts.act.4.23: Al ser puestos en libertad, volvieron a los suyos y les contaron todo lo que los principales sacerdotes y los ancianos les habían dicho.
texts.act.4.24: Cuando ellos lo oyeron, alzaron unánimes la voz a Dios y dijeron: “Soberano Señor, tú eres Dios, que hiciste el cielo y la tierra, el mar y todo lo que en ellos hay;
texts.act.4.25: que por boca de tu siervo David dijiste: ‘¿Por qué se amotinan las naciones, y los pueblos traman cosas vanas?
texts.act.4.26: Se levantaron los reyes de la tierra, y los príncipes se reunieron contra el Señor y contra su Cristo’.
texts.act.4.27: «Porque verdaderamente se aliaron en esta ciudad contra tu santo Siervo Jesús, a quien tú ungiste, tanto Herodes como Poncio Pilato, junto con los gentiles y el pueblo de Israel,
texts.act.4.28: para llevar a cabo todo lo que tu mano y tu designio habían predeterminado que sucediera.
texts.act.4.29: Y ahora, Señor, mira sus amenazas, y concede a tus siervos que hablen tu palabra con toda valentía,
